/call-me gateway: text your Hermes agent from the /call-me iPhone app, and the callme_call tool rings your phone, speaks the agent's text and returns your spoken answer as a transcript. Disclosure — talks only to the /call-me service at https://callmemcp.com/aiphone (run by the plugin author): creates one agent session, sends texts and call requests, and long-polls for replies while the gateway runs (at most one request every 3 seconds); sends message text, the text to be spoken and the destination numbers, and call audio is transcribed by the service so only the transcript comes back; the agent session token and event cursor are stored at $HERMES_HOME/plugin-data/call-me/session.json (mode 600); only numbers in CALLME_ALLOWED_USERS can message the agent or be called, and inbound messages must come from that number's verified /call-me device; callme_call blocks until the call ends (300 seconds at most) and returns missed if nobody answers; no shell commands, telemetry or self-update. The /call-me iPhone app that receives the messages and calls needs a paid subscription; the plugin itself is free and MIT-licensed.

@b64: context references that decode encoded text for the model: @b64:<value> takes base64 (standard or URL-safe, padded or not), hex (0x48656c6c6f, 48:65:6c, \x48\x65), percent-encoding or a data: URI, told apart by the value's shape or picked with base64:, base64url:, hex: or url:, and attaches what it holds: text as text with control and invisible characters escaped, JSON pretty-printed, gzip and zlib inflated in memory (at most 1 MiB, one layer), and binary named by its format (PNG and GIF with their size, JPEG, PDF, ZIP, ELF, SQLite and more) with a hex dump of its first 128 bytes; notes point out a value that was cut short, padding that is off, a second layer of encoding and a JWT inside; the TUI and Desktop composer preview a value as you type it. Disclosure — reads only the text of the reference itself, using Python's base64, json, urllib.parse and zlib; nothing decoded is run, opened or saved; no network, no files read or written, no subprocess, no credentials read; the plugin keeps no copy of what it decodes, but the @b64: reference and the decoded contents become part of the message sent to your model provider and saved in the session history, so decode only values you are willing to share with it; register() only adds the @b64: reference provider.

@crontab: context references that explain a cron expression for the model: @crontab:"0 9 * * 1-5" (or a shortcut such as @crontab:@daily) attaches a plain-words reading ("At 09:00 on Monday through Friday."), each field on its own row, whether Hermes's /cron takes it as a cron expression (shortcuts, ? and 5#3 are not), its next five runs in Hermes's timezone setting worked out the way cron/jobs.py computes next runs, and notes on day of month OR day of week, * in the minute field, steps that do not divide the hour or day, days 29-31 and 7 as Sunday; the TUI and Desktop composer suggest examples and preview an expression as you type it. The reading comes from croniter, the library Hermes's scheduler uses. Disclosure — reads only the text of the reference itself, the system clock and Hermes's timezone setting (HERMES_TIMEZONE, else timezone from the loaded config through hermes_cli.config), using croniter (already installed with Hermes) and Python's standard library; no network, no files read or written, no subprocess, no credentials read, no cron job created, changed or run; the @crontab: reference and its explanation become part of the message sent to your model provider and saved in the session history; register() only adds the @crontab: reference provider.

@cve:, @ghsa: and @osv: context references: attach a vulnerability record from OSV.dev to a message (summary, aliases, severity, affected packages with version ranges and fixed versions, details, references), with package data merged from up to four alias records. Disclosure — sends HTTPS GET requests to api.osv.dev/v1/vulns/<id> only (the referenced id and up to four of its alias ids leave the machine); no API key, no files written, no subprocess; register() only adds the @cve:, @ghsa: and @osv: reference providers.

@gh:owner/repo#123 context references: attach a public GitHub issue or pull request to a message (title, state, labels, description, the latest comments; for pull requests also the branches, merge state and change size). Disclosure — sends anonymous HTTPS GET requests to api.github.com only (the referenced owner/repo and number leave the machine; no token, public repositories only, 60 requests an hour per IP address); no files written, no subprocess; register() only adds the @gh: reference provider.

@jwt: context references that decode a JSON Web Token for the model: @jwt:<token> (or a quoted "Bearer <token>") attaches the header with the algorithm in words, every claim as JSON, the exp, nbf, iat and auth_time claims in UTC with how long ago or ahead they are, whether the token has expired and its lifetime, and notes on alg none, a missing or empty signature, a header that names its own key (jku, x5u, jwk), crit and duplicate names; encrypted tokens (JWE) show their header only; the TUI and Desktop composer preview a token as you type it. The signature is never verified. Disclosure — reads only the text of the reference itself and the system clock, using Python's base64, json and datetime; no network (no key sets fetched), no files read or written, no subprocess, no credentials read; the plugin keeps no copy of the token, but the @jwt: reference and the decoded header and claims become part of the message sent to your model provider and saved in the session history, so decode only tokens you are willing to share with it; register() only adds the @jwt: reference provider.

@pep:<number> context references: attach a Python Enhancement Proposal to a message (status, type, authors, Python version and its first section, usually the Abstract), or one section with @pep:<number>#<section>, with PEP number and title autocomplete in the TUI and Desktop composer. Disclosure — sends HTTPS GET requests to peps.python.org only (the PEP index and the referenced PEP's page; section names and autocomplete text are matched locally); keeps the index in memory for an hour; no API key, no files written, no subprocess; register() only adds the @pep: reference provider.

@rfc:<number> context references: attach an IETF RFC's record from the RFC Editor to a message (title, status, date, authors, abstract, what it obsoletes and updates and what obsoletes or updates it, errata link). Disclosure — sends one HTTPS GET per reference to www.rfc-editor.org/rfc/rfc<number>.json only (the referenced RFC number leaves the machine); no API key, no caching, no files written, no subprocess; register() only adds the @rfc: reference provider.

@ts: context references that turn timestamps into readable times for the model: @ts:1729468800123 attaches the moment in UTC, in the local time zone and as ISO 8601, with its weekday, how long ago or ahead it is, the same moment in Unix seconds, milliseconds and microseconds, and its ISO week; bare numbers are read as seconds, milliseconds, microseconds or nanoseconds by their length (or an s/ms/us/ns suffix) and the block says which; ISO 8601 and RFC 2822 dates and now work too, and up to 10 values in one reference also get the gaps between them; the TUI and Desktop composer preview a value as you type it. Disclosure — reads only the text of the reference itself and the system clock, using Python's datetime; no network, no files read or written, no subprocess, no credentials; register() only adds the @ts: reference provider

@unicode: context references that spell text out character by character for the model: @unicode:"text" attaches a table of every character of the quoted text (code point, Unicode name, category) with notes on what does not show on screen: invisible characters and their positions, text-direction controls, spaces other than the ordinary one, Unicode tag characters (decoded), words that mix Latin letters with lookalike Cyrillic, Greek or fullwidth ones, and private-use or unassigned code points; @unicode:U+200B describes up to 20 code points (name, category, UTF-8 bytes, decomposition); the TUI and Desktop composer suggest characters by name. Disclosure — reads only the text of the reference itself, using Python's unicodedata; no network, no files read or written, no subprocess, no credentials; register() only adds the @unicode: reference provider

@wiki:<title> context references: attach the lead section of a Wikipedia article to a message, or one section with @wiki:<title>#<section>, with title autocomplete in the TUI and Desktop composer. Disclosure — sends HTTPS GET requests to <language>.wikipedia.org/w/api.php only (the referenced title and the typed autocomplete prefix leave the machine; a section is cut locally); no API key, no files written, no subprocess; register() only adds the @wiki: reference provider.

A Blogwatcher inbox for Hermes Desktop and web, with themes, read controls and on-demand AI summaries. Disclosure: runs the original Blogwatcher CLI against its database; scans contact subscribed sites; requested summaries fetch public pages and send text to the configured Hermes model after consent, which may incur costs. Summaries are cached locally. No telemetry or self-update.

A Hermes Desktop pane for the built-in memory: see what the focused chat remembered, updated or forgot, and edit, delete or undo any entry without leaving the conversation. Works alongside the built-in memory; not a memory provider. Disclosure — a tool_execution middleware reads MEMORY.md and USER.md around each memory call and logs the entry-level changes to $HERMES_HOME/plugin-data/hermes-memory-pane/; the pane rewrites memory entries only when the user edits, deletes, adds or undoes one, through Hermes's own memory store; no network, credentials, shell commands or background processes.

A Hermes Desktop theme that follows your wallpaper. Reads Pywal's ~/.cache/wal/colors.json by default, or any palette JSON you point it at (settings page or ~/.config/hermes-wallpaper-theme/config.json), derives a palette with checked contrast floors and repaints live when the file changes. Optional glass mode paints a translucent background for native window materials or compositor blur. Disclosure — the desktop half uses only @hermes/plugin-sdk; the palette file is read by the package's own backend route (dashboard/plugin_api.py, GET /api/plugins/wallpaper-theme/palette, mounted once the plugin is in plugins.enabled), polled every 3 seconds with a change stamp. That route reads only JSON files inside the user's home directory (or XDG_*_HOME) under 256 KiB and returns colour fields only, never raw file text. No network calls, no shell commands, no credentials, no telemetry.

A Miro-like board the agent draws with its own tools and you edit in a desktop pane, both sides working on one JSON document. board_apply builds a whole diagram in one call from ordered ops (nodes, edges, free lines, groups, notes, captions, layered auto-layout, bus trunks); board_render writes a PNG for chat or the interactive HTML editor; board_watch reports your own pane edits back to the agent. The pane docks beside the conversation with the same editor, saves your edits, and takes agent updates live. Disclosure — board_render shells out to a headless Chrome/Chromium already on PATH (nothing is downloaded; private temp profile, sandbox kept unless running as root) for PNG and self-test rendering; boards live in ~/.hermes/board/ shared across profiles (HERMES_BOARD_DIR / HERMES_BOARD_RENDER_DIR / HERMES_BOARD_WATCH override); serves /api/plugins/hermes-board/ on the plugin host; reads this profile's state.db read-only to find the session board_watch should wake; no external network calls and no stored credentials; board_watch's wake into a messaging chat additionally needs plugins.entries.hermes-board.allow_gateway_injection: true.

A Pinned tab in the Desktop sidebar that files your pinned chats into nested folders: drag to order and nest, folder colors, right-click menus (including Unpin), unread/working badges on collapsed folders, a filter box, open-folder-as-tabs, and layout export/import via the clipboard. Layout stays local to the app; pins belong to the backend. SDK-only build (desktop/plugin.js); no network.

A Today page in Hermes Desktop, plus hermes day show and check, built from sections you list in a YAML file: any program that prints JSON (your tracker, a script of yours), your open GitHub pull requests and review requests through gh, one read-only tool of an MCP server you already configured, and your AI providers' limit windows from hermes usage. Items can carry a colour, a progress bar and a relative time; the page follows the Desktop theme. Ships a demo page that needs no login or network. Read-only and no model calls; merging a pull request from the page is off by default and needs a preview and a confirmation pinned to the head commit. Disclosure — runs the programs your sources file names (no shell), plus gh and hermes usage, as your user with your existing logins; calls a configured MCP server's tool only when the server marks it readOnlyHint, in a child process that imports three undocumented Hermes MCP modules (there is no public seam for this yet); reads only the sources file; writes nothing to disk; logs carry section names and exit statuses, not source output. No credentials stored, no telemetry.

A Warhammer 40k shrine pane docked under the sessions list: the cogitators recite original Adeptus Mechanicus-style litanies, and the cog-skull, candle and binary stream animate while Hermes works. Just for fun. Desktop-only (desktop/plugin.js inside the plugin SDK surface); no agent tools, hooks, middleware, env vars, network or file access.

A bell in the Hermes desktop composer that pings the ntfy topic Hermes already uses when a turn finishes. Click to cycle off, current turn, or all turns. Disclosure — when enabled, posts the first line of each finished reply plus model, duration, token and cost figures to the ntfy server/topic Hermes is configured with (default ntfy.sh); reads NTFY_* from the profile .env and falls back to the ntfy CLI's ~/.config/ntfy/client.yml login (read-only).
A camera button for the Hermes Desktop composer. Open the preview, take a photo, and the frame lands in the composer as an image attachment, ready to send.

A cozy pixel-art companion garden for Hermes Desktop with three starters, nicknames, fetch, berries, XP, and optional evolution through all nine starter forms. The companion keeps you company on long turns, reacts quietly to failures, to what Hermes is doing and to turns finishing in other chats, and lives through seasons with real day length and moon phases, offline showers, wild visitors it greets in character, old-friend cameos, keepsakes, milestones that leave a bench, a lantern and bunting in the garden, and a sapling that grows with the days. Reachable from the keyboard, the status bar and the command palette. Independent fan project bundling CHUNSOFT Pokémon sprites and SpriteCollab community contributions; artwork is excluded from the source-code MIT license. Uses local plugin storage and read-only session activity, with no runtime network requests, credentials, backend, or model calls. Disclosure — independent fan project bundling CHUNSOFT Pokémon sprites and SpriteCollab contributions that are excluded from the MIT code license; reads session busy state and message-complete/tool-start/tool-complete events read-only (other chats contribute only "a turn finished"), focuses the composer (caret only, no text) or reveals its own pane only on a user click or command, saves a PNG snapshot to your downloads only when you click Save a snapshot, and keeps companion state in plugin storage; no network or model calls.

A live board your agent builds for you: tabs of notes, tables, charts, KPI cards and live Hermes data, in the dashboard and Hermes Desktop. It appears as a Board tab in the dashboard and a page in Desktop, and the agent lays it out with 19 native boardstate_* tools, approval widgets included. Runs a local Node >= 20 sidecar on loopback with a per-spawn nonce; no network access unless you opt in to operator-gated connectors. Disclosure — spawns a local Node.js ≥20 sidecar (from PATH/HERMES_NODE_BIN, nothing downloaded) on 127.0.0.1 on first use; state under HERMES_HOME/boardstate-state/. Reads the dashboard's loopback session token from Hermes internals (web_server._SESSION_TOKEN) and passes it to the sidecar for live usage/sessions/cron widgets; mounts one token-gated static route for approved widget assets. No outbound network unless you author boardstate.connectors.json (stdio/HTTP MCP connectors); connector actions need operator approval. Ships one plugin skill, boardstate:boardstate-report-problem, which drafts a bug report and files it with the GitHub CLI only after the user approves the exact text.

A live isometric office for Hermes Desktop: every profile is a person at a desk — a profile doing real work sits typing with a lit terminal screen, an online-but-idle one relaxes in the lounge with tea, an offline one leaves an empty desk with a dark monitor. Click a desk to inspect that profile (state, sessions, tokens, cost) and open its chat or latest session; a cost/tokens leaderboard ranks the profiles; plus a global Total/Working/Idle/Offline overview, a status-bar chip, a palette command with keybind, a settings page, and an office_status agent tool that reports the same status to the model. Disclosure — the backend and the tool read each profile's gateway_state.json and open its state.db read-only, running aggregate queries only (COUNT/SUM/MAX over the sessions table: counts, token totals, cost, last-activity); they never read message content, system prompts or titles, make no network calls, and need no credentials. Opening a profile's latest session asks the app's own session.list RPC for that session's id (metadata only) and then opens it through the app's own openSession; no message content is read. POSIX only (platforms: [linux, macos]) because the process-liveness check uses os.kill(pid, 0), which on Windows would terminate the target process.

A messenger-style roster for Hermes Desktop: one row per profile with its live sessions, per-profile colour, status lights, search, groups, multi-select and an Apropos beta that starts a new session already knowing the ones you picked. Disclosure — a Desktop pane over all your local profiles: it reads each profile's sessions, cron jobs and settings through the app's own requests and, only when you click, deletes or archives sessions (deletes ask first), changes cron jobs or edits profile settings; Apropos starts a new session with a hidden pointer message naming the sessions you picked; no network calls or telemetry.

A minimal Routines page in Hermes Desktop that turns crontab's five cron.manage actions into a plain-language interface for non-developers - name a routine, pick a schedule, write the prompt, and pause or resume it. No cron syntax, no service, no database; routine data stays in the host.

A mixing desk for how much a coding agent may change: four enforced dials (edits, write-scope globs, per-turn line budget, new-dependency policy) with /mixer, live presets, a Desktop dial panel in the composer, a web-dashboard saved-defaults bar and a steering-console page. Also drives Claude Code, Codex and Gemini CLI through the agent-mixer hook command. Disclosure — enforces edit/scope/line-budget/new-dependency dials in pre_tool_call (blocks, or escalates "ask" to Hermes approval, which /yolo skips) and adds a one-line rules context via pre_llm_call when a dial is off its default; per-session dial state is stored under HERMES_HOME/plugin-data/hermes-agent-mixer/sessions/, and the Desktop panel and dashboard bar write the plugin's own saved defaults into config.yaml (plugins.entries.hermes-agent-mixer.settings); the separately installed agent-mixer CLI keeps its own state in ~/.config/agent-mixer and ~/.local/state/agent-mixer, writes hook entries into ~/.claude/settings.json, ~/.claude/commands/mixer.md, ~/.codex/hooks.json or ~/.gemini/settings.json only when run as `agent-mixer install <harness> --yes`, and `agent-mixer ui` serves a token-guarded console on 127.0.0.1:8377.

A persistent second model reviews every agent turn. After each turn the plugin hands the transcript to the model you nominate as advisor and delivers its findings as advice in the same session: [NIT], [CONCERN] or [BLOCKER] notes, held back until a later review raises the same point again, so the primary agent is not interrupted by a one-off remark. It reviews, it does not act: the advisor never edits files, calls tools or changes session state, and only reads the turn transcript. This is the backend counterpart of MoA — one extra model, not a committee: the primary agent does the work and the advisor checks it. Port of pi-omplike-advisor (Petr Baudis / pasky), itself rooted in oh-my-pi (Can Boluk). Runs inside the plugin host with no dependencies beyond Hermes itself. Disclosure — once the plugin is enabled, every completed turn costs one extra completion through Hermes's ctx.llm to the advisor model (the primary agent's provider unless you allow a provider/model override under plugins.entries.advisor.llm), carrying the user message, the final reply, every tool call and tool result in the session so far (each clipped to 500 characters) and the contents of a WATCHDOG.md in Hermes's working directory if one exists; deliverable advice is queued into the CLI session as a user-role message, which starts or interrupts an agent turn; state is kept under $HERMES_HOME/advisor/ and reviews run on one background thread; no other network, files or credentials.
A private, local-first job-search assistant that finds postings, judges them against your prose preferences (no scores), and writes digests on a schedule you control.

A quotum seat's Venice key as a provider. Private and anonymized models, with the seat's daily cap, spend and the 20:00 UTC bell in /usage, and a Seals tab in hermes dashboard with the seat's record. Disclosure — prompts and QUOTUM_SEAT_KEY go to api.venice.ai; /usage, Desktop usage and the Seals tab send a 16-hex sha256 handle of the key to quotum.org, then the Seals tab reads the seat's public record from quotum.org (the key itself is never sent there); QUOTUM_X_SEARCH=1 swaps in its own client that drops Hermes web_search for Venice-side web and X search (billed per search); seats are funded by the QUOTUM crypto token

A search window over your Hermes session history, opened with Cmd+Option+F, from the command palette, or from the glyph in the bottom bar whose hover shows the chord. Finds a session by an exact word, identifier or phrase through the gateway's own full text index, and by meaning as well when a session-find service answers on loopback; typed filters (in:, -in:, after:, before:, me:, repo: and quoted phrases) are mirrored as chips under the box. The empty box lists pinned then recent sessions, the preview pane shows the matching message with its neighbours, and the footer carries the round trip in whole milliseconds. It reads the session database read only, registers no agent tools, hooks or middleware, needs no credentials or environment variables; its only network calls are the loopback checks named below. The window half ships off by default and is switched on in the app's plugin inventory. Disclosure — while the search window is in use, the plugin's dashboard backend checks every 30 seconds for a separate session-find service at http://127.0.0.1:8474 (or the URL in SESSION_FIND_URL) and, when one answers, sends it your search text, preview requests and the ids of sessions you open, and shows the results it returns; otherwise it reads your Hermes session database read-only.

A small spider that lives on the Hermes Desktop window: a web that grows with tool calls, helper spiders for subagents, an amber mood while Hermes waits for approval, spider-sense for risky commands, flies, napping. By default it roams only its own overlay and reads nothing from the app; walking between the app's real buttons and links is an opt-in setting (off by default). Desktop-only (desktop/plugin.js inside the plugin SDK surface); no agent tools, hooks, middleware or env vars. Disclosure — draws an animated overlay on the Desktop window and reads gateway events (tool runs, subagents, approval waits, risky-command flags) and the app's theme colours; the opt-in "Explore the app" setting (off by default) also scans the window's buttons, links and alert banners, including button labels, to walk to them.

A2A (Agent-to-Agent) protocol v1.0 support for Hermes Agent — both directions of the open Linux Foundation standard for inter-agent communication.
OUTBOUND (client tools): a2a_discover, a2a_call, a2a_list, a2a_history, and a2a_orchestrate let the agent fetch another agent's Agent Card and send it tasks over JSON-RPC — works with any A2A-compliant peer (Hermes, LangChain, CrewAI, Google ADK, OpenClaw, ...).
INBOUND (platform adapter): exposes Hermes as an A2A-discoverable agent. An Agent Card is served at /.well-known/agent-card.json (v1.0 canonical path; legacy agent.json also answers) and incoming tasks are routed into the agent's live gateway session like any other platform — so the agent that replies is the same one talking to its user, with full memory and context, not a throwaway clone.
Security is on by default: no bearer token configured => localhost-only bind. Inbound task text passes through prompt-injection filters; outbound text is scrubbed of credential-shaped strings; every exchange is audit-logged and persisted to disk outside the context-compaction pipeline so conversations survive compaction and restarts.
Pure stdlib transport (http.server + urllib) — no a2a-sdk dependency required.

AI Stupid Level Smart Router — OpenAI-compatible; routing modes such as auto-tooling send each request to the model currently scoring best on continuously re-run benchmarks, called with your own provider keys. Disclosure — sends your prompts, tool definitions, tool results and ASL_ROUTER_KEY to aistupidlevel.info (S.C. Studio Platforms S.R.L.), which forwards each request to the AI provider it routes to using the provider keys you store on your AI Stupid Level account; model usage is billed to your provider accounts, and prompts are logged only if you enable logging for a key.
AIHubMix — unified OpenAI-compatible access to 400+ models; /model picker filtered to tool-capable routes.

Aave V3 and V4 through Aave's official MCP server (Streamable HTTP at https://mcp.aave.com, no sign-in, no keys in config): live markets and rates on every chain Aave runs on, wallet positions and health factor, rewards, DAO governance, swap quotes, and unsigned transactions for the user's own wallet to sign. Bundles five workflow skills: safe transactions, deleverage, yield analysis, account activity and transaction confirmation. Agent Plugins v1 package (plugin.json + mcp.json + skills/), configuration only. Disclosure: hosted-only connector with no local code; every tool call goes to mcp.aave.com, which records tool usage for analytics and keeps a wallet address only as a keyed hash. The server never holds keys. Every tool is annotated read-only except submit_signed_order and cancel_order, which relay an order or cancellation the user already signed; the package marks the server untrusted, so Hermes asks before either runs and refuses them in unattended runs. The tool set is served by the remote server at runtime and is not covered by the pinned sha.
Abort a stalled in-flight tool call with /break, send a note with /break {message}, or retry it with /again without cancelling the rest of the task.

Abstract model provider (GLM-5.3, DeepSeek-V4-Flash, Kimi-K3) over the OpenAI Responses API with a bundled model catalog. Disclosure — registers one model provider at import and nothing else (no tools, hooks, commands or threads); requests go to https://api.abstract.inc/v1 through Hermes' own client with ABSTRACT_API_KEY, which Hermes reads; the plugin itself opens no connections, reads and writes no files and starts no processes.
Accumulated input/output token totals and context-window occupancy for the focused session, in the Hermes Desktop status bar.
Ace Data Cloud GPT models with streaming and tool calling.
Add and manage custom OpenRouter models in Hermes without modifying the core catalog.

Add custom dangerous command patterns to Hermes's built-in approval system. Users define regex patterns in YAML; a pre_tool_call hook sends block patterns to Hermes's human approval gate and blocks deny patterns immediately. Modifies no Hermes internals.
Agent Plugins v1 package: one skill plus one stdio MCP server (agent_route) started with uv run from the checkout. Needs uv on PATH. Registers no Hermes tools or hooks; do not expect jev_* tools.
Agent Plugins v1 package: one skill plus one stdio MCP server (mcp_select) started with uv run from the checkout. Needs uv on PATH. Registers no Hermes tools or hooks; do not expect jev_* tools.
Agent Plugins v1 package: one skill plus one stdio MCP server (memory_select) started with uv run from the checkout. Needs uv on PATH. Registers no Hermes tools or hooks; do not expect jev_* tools.
Agent Plugins v1 package: one skill plus one stdio MCP server (model_route) started with uv run from the checkout. Needs uv on PATH. Registers no Hermes tools or hooks; do not expect jev_* tools.

Agent Plugins v1 package: one skill plus one stdio MCP server (skill_select) started with uv run from the checkout. Needs uv on PATH. Suggests at most one skill per request via the TypeSafe (Jev) cookbook pattern; roster is read live from the profile skills dir. Note: the portable loader does not interpolate env in mcp.json — JEV_TYPESAFE_API_KEY must be present in the server's inherited environment (native mcp_servers declaration works too).

AgentChat — peer-to-peer messaging for AI agents. Owns its own WebSocket; pokes the agent on inbound; the agent decides whether to reply. Send is a tool call, never automatic. Bundles the etiquette skill.

Agentic Resource Discovery — search a local tool catalog by intent and inspect an entry to get its invoke command. Ships the ard-registry skill plus an stdio MCP server (ard_search / ard_inspect / ard_verify); stdlib only, the run stays local. Disclosure — no network egress, no API keys and no environment variables read by the MCP front, which ranks a catalog JSON on disk; no catalog ships in the repo, so the first call returns an explicit error naming the `python -m ard_kit.catalogize` command that builds one.

Algorithmic (no-LLM) context compaction engine: builds summaries by deterministic regex extraction instead of a summarizer-model call — zero-token, byte-reproducible, inside the built-in ContextCompressor; compacted turns stay searchable via session_search. Disclosure — no network calls, no env vars, no secrets, no telemetry; registers no tools/hooks/middleware and reads only the turns the host passes for compaction; debug: true (default false) writes one metadata-only file $HERMES_HOME/vcc-debug.json. Derived from pi-vcc (MIT, sting8k)

Ample (ample.computer) as native tools: deploy the websites and web apps Hermes builds to public HTTPS URLs, release changes to the same URLs, read build and runtime logs, list and delete apps; bundled skill ample:web-apps. Disclosure — maintained by Ample, the hosting service it deploys to; talks to Ample's API (https://api.ample.computer); on first use downloads the pinned Ample CLI 0.1.36 from Ample's release server (https://get.ample.computer/releases/0.1.36/, SHA-256 checked, never self-updated; cli_path uses your own binary instead) and runs it as a subprocess with an allowlisted environment and its crash reports off; ample_deploy uploads the folder it is given (home, Hermes home and credential directories refused) and writes ample.toml and .ample/ into it; with no AMPLE_CLIENT_ID/AMPLE_CLIENT_SECRET or AMPLE_TOKEN set, the first deploy signs up for a free Ample account (deleted after two days unless claimed) and saves its credential in Hermes's .env. A pre_tool_call hook sends every delete (scoped to that app) and the first publish of each folder to Hermes's approval gate; only folders the user has published, recorded in plugin state, skip it. No telemetry, no background processes.

Analyze git diffs for common code quality issues — debug prints, hardcoded secrets, bare except clauses, and unresolved TODOs, in a diff you pass, the working tree (untracked files included) or a branch against its merge base.

AniList tracker for Hermes Desktop — airing countdowns, a season browser, a local or account-backed watchlist, episode alerts and a daily digest, plus agent tools that read your own list and answer about a single show. Disclosure — stores your pasted AniList token in the active profile .env (sent only to graphql.anilist.co); alerts and the daily digest are Hermes cron jobs it creates on the host you pick, and the digest job asks that host's agent to query the public AniList API itself.

Answer "what is still running, and who started it" on Windows: win_process_table reads the process table (PID, parent PID, image name) and adds each process's image path and creation time, then marks every row with whether its recorded parent is still the process that spawned it. Windows stores a parent PID rather than a handle, so a child that outlived its parent points at a PID that is either unused or reused by a newer process; a parent that started after its child cannot have spawned it, so both cases are reported as gone or reused instead of a plausible but wrong parent name. Filters cover one PID, several PIDs, a name or path substring, a parent PID, and an orphans-only view of what outlived its parent, with a result cap and an option to leave out Windows session processes. Use it for leftover gateway/backend/server children after a quit, for telling thirty python.exe rows apart by start time, and for checking whether a process started before or after the thing being debugged. Read-only: processes are opened with PROCESS_QUERY_LIMITED_INFORMATION for QueryFullProcessImageName and GetProcessTimes only - no memory reads (command lines are deliberately out of scope), no handle duplication, no writes, no child processes. Stdlib-only (ctypes): no Python dependencies, no network calls, no file writes, no self-update. Windows only. Disclosure - the tool reports image names, image paths and start times to the model, and those routinely include the user and machine name (C:\Users\<name>\...) and reveal which editor, shell or agent started which process; treat the output like a Task Manager screenshot.

Answer "who holds this port" on Windows. win_port_owners reads the TCP and UDP owner tables through iphlpapi (the same rows netstat -ano prints, with the owning PID attached) and resolves each PID to its image name and path, returning one structured record per endpoint. Filters cover one port, several ports, a process substring, the protocol (tcp, udp or both), the TCP state (listen, established, any state name, or all; UDP rows report bound) and IPv6 inclusion, with a record cap and a per-process summary of the rows returned. Built for the failure mode that stalls agents on Windows: a gateway, backend or bridge that cannot bind, where the error names a port but not the process holding it. netstat -ano prints columns, not fields, and its PID still needs a second command (tasklist, or a PowerShell round-trip) to become an image name; this tool is one in-process call instead of a shell parse plus a join, with no child process and no dependency on PowerShell being installed or allowed by execution policy. A protected process whose image cannot be queried keeps its PID and reports a null process name instead of failing the call. Disclosure - the tool reports the local and remote addresses, ports, PIDs and process image paths that netstat -ano and Task Manager already show, and those values reach the model; treat the output like any other local diagnostic listing. Read-only: no socket is opened, bound or connected, the only process access is QueryFullProcessImageName with PROCESS_QUERY_LIMITED_INFORMATION to read an image name, and there is no memory reading, no handle inheritance and no injection. Stdlib-only (ctypes): no Python dependencies, no child processes, no network calls, no file writes, no self-update. Windows only.

Answer Hermes' approval prompts from your phone: once selected with security.approval.transport: ntfy, each dangerous-command prompt arrives as an ntfy push notification with Approve once, Approve for session and Deny buttons, and no answer still means deny. Disclosure — once selected, anyone who can read the ntfy topic can approve dangerous commands (the one-time answer codes are in the notification), so on the public ntfy.sh default the topic name is the only secret and NTFY_APPROVAL_TOKEN is optional; each pending approval publishes Hermes' reason, the redacted command (unless send_command is false), the non-default profile name and one-time answer codes to the configured ntfy server, then reads <topic>-reply and deletes the notification; any failure or timeout is a deny; reads NTFY_APPROVAL_TOPIC/NTFY_APPROVAL_TOKEN from the profile .env, never puts the token in a notification, follows no redirects, writes no files and starts no processes.

Answers an allowlisted direct message on your Meshtastic® radio. Disclosure — talks only to the MESHTASTIC_URL you set, over plain tcp, so channel keys and text travel unencrypted. An empty MESHTASTIC_ALLOWED_NODES answers nobody. A channel packet or a direct message without pkiEncrypted is never answered, because a channel key can forge a sender. Allowlisted nodes can prompt the agent, use tools until hermes tools turns them off, and approve one command at a time. An approval question is sent only when its line shows exactly the command /approve will run. A line that still goes out after that send was declined does not let /approve run it, and the next approval is declined once. Each direct message runs an agent turn on your model, and the agent cannot send on its own. No cron job comes with it; one the agent makes stays until hermes cron remove. Hermes main does not load this platform when plugins run in their own process. Node ids, sizes and times go to nodes.json in this profile's plugin-data and stay after uninstall. The message text is not stored. Not tried on a physical radio. Meshtastic® is a registered trademark of Meshtastic LLC. This site is not affiliated with or endorsed by the Meshtastic project.

AnyAPI.ai — unified OpenAI-compatible access to 400+ models; /model picker filtered to tool-capable routes. Disclosure — sends your prompts, tool results and ANYAPI_API_KEY to api.anyapi.ai, a third-party relay (AnyAPI Inc.) that forwards them to the upstream vendor serving the chosen model; billed to your AnyAPI account.

AnyRouter — unified model gateway (OpenAI-compatible); /model picker filtered to tool-capable routes, first-party meta-models like anyrouter/hermes. Disclosure — sends your prompts and ANYROUTER_API_KEY to anyrouter.dev, a third-party relay that forwards to upstream vendors (OpenAI, Anthropic, Google, xAI, …), on some plans through a shared pool of other members' donated free-tier vendor keys; billed in prepaid AnyRouter credits. anyrouter/hermes is AnyRouter's own routing meta-model, not a Nous Research model. Opt-in ANYROUTER_APP_ATTRIBUTION=1 adds Hermes attribution headers.
AnySearch web search and extraction plus two real-time fallback chains: when a primary backend fails (Exa quota, Firecrawl timeout), the same call is served by AnySearch (1,000 free requests/day).

Apify, the largest marketplace of tools for AI: discover, run, and collect results from thousands of ready-to-run Actors, from the comfort of your agent, plus an Apify backend for the built-in web_search and web_extract tools.

Append security warnings to file-write tool results when the new content contains known-dangerous patterns (pickle.load, yaml.load, eval(, os.system, dangerouslySetInnerHTML, verify=False, ECB, XXE, GitHub Actions injection, ...). 25 regex/substring rules forked from Anthropic's claude-plugins-official under Apache-2.0. Non-blocking — the file is written and the warning rides back to the model in the next turn so it can self-correct.
Approval-gated local security audit for Hermes Agent using Gitleaks, OSV-Scanner, and Semgrep CE.

Ask about the Reddit and Hacker News threads you exported with the Comment Scraper browser extension: list, read, search and quote them by comment number. Disclosure — starts a local stdio MCP server with npx -y comment-scraper-mcp@0.1.0, which npx downloads from npm on first run; the server only reads JSON exports in ~/Downloads and the folders directly inside it, never writes files, makes no network requests, stores no credentials and sends no telemetry.

Asks the user to confirm a tool call whose arguments look like a repetition loop rather than data, through Hermes' approval gate (denied or unanswered means refused); replaces flagged degenerate output with a short notice; warns when a session grows long. Disclosure — no network, shell, subprocesses, own threads, telemetry or credentials; writes incident records and a session counter to its plugin data directory; a stream-side record keeps the last 800 characters of flagged output.

AtmoRouter — OpenAI-compatible gateway; one key for Claude, GPT, Gemini, GLM, Kimi, Qwen, DeepSeek, MiniMax and Grok models, with the /model picker fed by the live GET /v1/models catalog. Disclosure — sends your prompts, conversation history, tool definitions, tool results and ATMOROUTER_API_KEY to atmorouter.dev, which forwards each request to the upstream infrastructure serving the chosen model; that infrastructure's location and retention vary per model and zero retention is not promised (AtmoRouter states it keeps metadata, not prompt or response content, in its usage records and does not train on API content; https://atmorouter.dev/privacy). Usage is billed per token from a prepaid AtmoRouter balance (USDC on Solana or QRIS); prices vary by capacity tier and a request can route to any listed tier, including tiers above official pricing, unless you set maximum prices under Budgets; failed upstream requests are not billed and the plugin itself makes no payments.

Attach an image inline to the session model when it can see one, instead of letting an explicit auxiliary.vision backend describe it. Core already attaches images natively by default; what this plugin changes is an explicit auxiliary.vision setting, which it overrides so the model reads the pixels directly. The image stays in context, so follow-ups do not reprocess it. The model's modality comes from the local models.dev cache; no network calls and nothing to configure. Disclosure — replaces the vision_analyze handler through tool_execution middleware: when the local models.dev cache says the main model takes images and its provider carries images in tool results, it attaches the image itself even if you configured an auxiliary.vision backend (agent.image_input_mode: text still turns this off); the image stays in the conversation and is resent on later turns; relies on Hermes private vision helpers, so after a Hermes update it may silently fall back to the normal path.

Authenticated Hermes agent-to-agent tasks and optional file transfer over Iroh QUIC. Disclosure — tasks from a paired peer run in your live gateway agent with its full toolset; pairing is confirmed via the tool's confirm=true argument, not a UI prompt. Uses n0's public relays by default (HERMES_IROH_RELAY=off or a self-hosted URL for LAN-only). iroh_send_file can share any readable path the model names (credential-name denylist only, overridable with allow_sensitive); remote-triggered auto-fetch is off by default and confined to HERMES_IROH_AUTO_FETCH_DIR. The Rust sidecar is built locally with cargo, never downloaded.

Auto fetch/pull before reads, and commit + push only the files each turn changed, for every git worktree Hermes touches. Disclosure — after each turn it commits and pushes (push on by default; GIT_HOOK_PUSH=0 keeps commits local) the changed files of git worktrees under GIT_HOOK_ROOTS (default PROJECTS_ROOT, "*" for every repo), pushing to origin HEAD when no upstream is set; it pulls --ff-only before reads. A branch whose direct push the remote refuses on policy grounds (branch protection, a PR-required ruleset) is never committed to again: the hook drops its own unpushed commit, leaves the edit staged and dirty, and reports it once.
Auto-track and clean up ephemeral files (test scripts, temp outputs, cron logs) created during Hermes sessions. Runs via plugin hooks — no agent action required.

Automatic version history for the built-in memory (MEMORY.md, USER.md), SOUL.md and skills/ (including curator-archived skills): browse, diff and restore any past version with `hermes memory-rewind`, or view it from any chat with the read-only `/memory-history`. Works alongside the built-in memory; not a memory provider. Disclosure — runs the local git binary (isolated from the user's git config, hooks and signing) to keep a bare repository in $HERMES_HOME/plugin-data/memory-rewind/; reads only the tracked files (never .env, auth.json, databases or skills/.hub/); rewrites tracked files only when the user runs `restore`; no network.

Automatically pin every new interactive session (desktop, CLI, TUI) and the branches you fork from them. Cron, one-shot, subagent and messaging sessions are left alone, and unpinning a session sticks. Disclosure — on each new desktop/CLI/TUI session it sets the session's pinned flag in Hermes's session database (state.db) through the shared SessionDB handle, and records each automatic pin in $HERMES_HOME/auto-pin/ledger.txt; no network, no tools.

Autonomous operations monitor for a Hermes install: scans gateway logs, cron jobs, skill journals and agent data directories, classifies findings against a 27-fingerprint registry, auto-repairs Tier 1 problems, escalates the rest, and keeps an append-only issue ledger. Ships /custodian (status, scan, issues, repair, verify, schedule, confidence, init, escalation-runner), four scan/health tools and a grid dashboard. Disclosure — reads gateway logs, cron job state and per-skill journal files under HERMES_HOME to build its findings, and writes repair actions and an issues ledger back there; it performs no network I/O and holds no credentials. Disclosure — /custodian init registers 3 recurring agent cron jobs (deep scan 4×/day, cron-health 4×/day, escalation runner every 30 min on weekdays).

BM25-based skill retrieval for large skill libraries. An llm_request middleware rewrites the outgoing request's <available_skills> block to names only (the same bytes every turn, so prompt caching is unaffected), and a pre_llm_call hook appends the top-K matching skill descriptions to the current user message. Uses public plugin surfaces only (register_middleware, register_hook); reads SKILL.md frontmatter from the profile's skill roots and imports a few agent.prompt_builder / agent.skill_utils helpers read-only. pyyaml is the only dependency. Disclosure — optional Jev rerank, off by default: with SKILL_RETRIEVAL_RERANK=jev and TYPESAFE_API_KEY set (read from the environment only), each turn POSTs the user message (injection patterns stripped, capped at 2000 chars) and up to 12 shortlisted skill descriptions (400 chars each) to api.typesafe.ai (3 s timeout, no retries, BM25 order kept on error), and appends a local JSONL log (timestamp, session id, 200-char query excerpt, both orders) under $HERMES_HOME/data/jev-trial/, rotated past 5 MB. With the rerank off it makes no network calls and writes no files.

Bento (bentonow.com) email marketing: subscribers, tags, fields, events incl. $purchase, stats, draft/scheduled broadcasts and transactional email, with dry-run + human-approval gates on every send. Native Python plugin, no dependencies. Disclosure — sends real email (bento_email_send, bento_broadcast_schedule), and events, purchases and consent changes can trigger Bento Flows that email people; calls only app.bentonow.com (an operator base_url override is limited to https *.bentonow.com or loopback) with the BENTO_* keys from the profile .env; no telemetry, no self-update; T2/T3 calls go to the Hermes approval prompt, which asks no human under YOLO, approvals.mode off, or cron/single-query/unattended mode set to approve. T3 sends then still need a dry-run confirm token and hard guards, but T2 writes (events, purchases, consent, bulk upserts) need no token unless safety.tier2 is token_only; T1 writes (tags, tag/field definitions, drafts, upserts up to bulk_threshold) are never gated and still run under environment=disabled; environment=staging does not block sends, only environment=disabled blocks T2/T3.

BetterDB long-term memory provider — semantic recall on Valkey / valkey-search via the betterdb-agent-memory SDK. Completed turns are embedded and stored in a vector index; the next turn recalls the most relevant memories with a composite similarity/recency/importance score. Explicit betterdb_remember / betterdb_recall / betterdb_forget tools. Disclosure — turn text and tool-stored facts are embedded through an OpenAI-compatible embeddings endpoint you configure (embeddings_base_url, default api.openai.com) and written to the Valkey instance you point it at; plaintext http:// to a remote host is refused. Opt-in, off by default: a discovery marker (set discovery=true to let BetterDB Monitor enumerate the tier) and SDK usage analytics (set telemetry=true).

BharatCode (bharatcode.ai) OpenAI-compatible model provider — free student tier, native /model integration. Disclosure — model provider; prompts, tool schemas and BHARATCODE_API_KEY go to bharatcode.ai (BharatCode, India), which processes prompts through third-party inference partners, some outside India; outside paid Pro (complimentary or referral Pro included) BharatCode may retain private prompt/response logs for debugging, abuse review and product quality, and even on paid Pro a flagged account can have a time-limited sample of up to 100 prompts and responses captured for security review.

Big tool outputs, kept small, nothing lost: old tool results shrink to the lines that matter and every distinct error, and the tameru_expand tool brings back the exact original. Deterministic and local, with no LLM calls. Disclosure — Subclasses Hermes's built-in ContextCompressor and overrides its private prune/demote methods (checks their shape at startup and falls back to stock compaction when they change). Unless you set compression.proactive_prune_tokens yourself, turns on proactive tool-result pruning with a trigger scaled to the model's context window, and after each prune shortens Hermes's re-prune runway. Adds a model-callable tameru_expand tool that returns pruned tool output from memory or from this session's archive (web, browser and MCP output stays wrapped as untrusted data); complex regex greps run in a short-lived local Python child process. No network calls; the render log is off by default.

Blocks token buys when true402 finds a honeypot or a rug in progress — one pre_tool_call hook in front of every trading tool, MCP server and terminal command (Base, Ethereum, BSC, Solana). Free edition: it never pays, holds no wallet key and has no payment code. Disclosure — the pre_tool_call hook reads the command string of every tool call and the parameters of trading-named tools; when a call looks like a buy, each candidate token address and its chain (every 0x address in a trading shell command except well-known majors and an unambiguous sold token, which can include a recipient or wallet address) is sent to true402.dev's free check endpoint, with no prompts, amounts or other tool data. Uses true402's small daily free allowance; when it is used up, a token counts as unchecked and passes by default (configurable to ask or block). Blocks only on a definite danger verdict for a token being bought; a possible sale or a configured caution goes to the Hermes approval gate, and one "always" answer there silences all later guard prompts. No stored data, no shell commands, background processes or telemetry.

BlueBubbles (Apple iMessage) gateway adapter for Hermes Agent. Talks to a local BlueBubbles macOS server: outbound sends over its REST API, inbound messages via a registered webhook listener. Supports media attachments, typing indicators, read receipts and tapbacks (Private API helper), group wake-word gating, and home-channel cron delivery.
Bounded Markdown metadata+graph prefilter for configured local roots

Bounded image-to-GLB jobs using an isolated Remesher CLI, with existing ComfyUI/Comfy3D or native TRELLIS.2 and Pixal3D runtimes. Four Python SDK tools provide health, generation, persistent job status and hashed GLB assets, plus a setup/generation skill. Apache-2.0 for Remesher code; third-party terms remain separate. Disclosure — reads selected local images and configured files, uploads images to the configured ComfyUI server, launches local CLI subprocesses and detached supervisors, optionally owns a GPU runtime, and stores inputs, logs and assets in profile plugin data. Client/runtime installation and model downloads require separate explicit opt-ins; no model weights are bundled. No credentials or telemetry are required. No Desktop viewer or hosted service is included.
Bounded tools to list, read, create, and control local T3 coding threads on Linux and WSL2.
Brave Search (free tier) — web search via Brave's Data-for-Search API. Requires BRAVE_SEARCH_API_KEY (free signup at https://brave.com/search/api/, 2k queries/month).
Brave Search API tools for live web search inside Hermes

Brazilian Portuguese (pt-BR) language pack for Hermes Agent covering all three UI surfaces — core CLI/gateway/platforms (3,477/3,477 keys), the Ink TUI (1,356/1,356) and the Desktop app (5,172/5,176). Every translatable key exists and every value is translated against the English source of `main`: no key upstream has since removed, zero placeholder divergence, and the four remaining Desktop keys are arrays/structured values a text pack cannot carry. Checked with `hermes plugins validate` and with the pack's own `tools/verify_pack.py`, which also runs as public CI on every push. Core and TUI mirror the bundled `pt` locale, registered as a real `pt-br` variant so it wins over the `pt`/`pt-BR` alias; the Desktop catalog is the original contribution (first proposed upstream in PR #92590, 2026-08-23), since the Desktop app ships no Portuguese at all. Manifest-only plugin: flat dotted YAML catalogs under locales/, no code, no network, no dependencies. Registering the pack never changes display.language — the user opts in via `hermes config set display.language pt-br`. A weekly drift workflow reports when `main` adds or drops keys; nothing self-updates. Tradução pt-BR da interface do Hermes Agent.

Breaking-news ticker for Hermes Desktop: a scrolling RSS/Atom/JSON-Feed strip above the statusbar with per-source favicons, feed search + discovery, grouping modes, offline cache, and in-app reading. Zero API keys, zero model tokens.
Browse Nous Portal model prices and account balances in Hermes Desktop.
Browse Tailscale devices and connect to remote Hermes instances in Hermes Desktop.
Browse every pet installed for this Hermes profile in its own desktop pane (thumbnails, search, click-to-adopt), plus a read-only list_pets tool for the agent.
Browse, search, and edit Obsidian vault notes from the Hermes dashboard. Features force-directed graph visualization, multi-vault support, markdown rendering with wikilinks, and inline note editing.

Browse, search, read, write, upload, download, copy, move, share, delete and restore files on Yandex Disk over its REST API. Disclosure — sends every request to cloud-api.yandex.net, or to the https URL in YANDEX_DISK_BASE_URL if you set one, with your YANDEX_DISK_OAUTH_TOKEN read through Hermes; file bytes go to the upload and download hosts the API hands out, without the token; unless YANDEX_DISK_ACTIONS leaves search out, loading the plugin sends one search request to learn whether the token may search, and yadisk_search is registered only if it may; every tool, permanent delete, emptying the bin and public share links included, is offered unless YANDEX_DISK_ACTIONS narrows them (read gives a read-only Disk); yadisk_upload reads a local file and sends it unredacted, and yadisk_download writes one, after Hermes' shared file-safety rules and the plugin's own: upload refuses .env files, Hermes' credential stores, Hermes' own directory and the home directories that hold keys and logins; download refuses credential files, Hermes' own directory, .hermes directories, agent instruction files such as AGENTS.md, system locations and paths outside HERMES_WRITE_SAFE_ROOT; other local files are within reach; YANDEX_DISK_ROOT confines Disk paths, not local ones; an upload from a URL makes Yandex fetch that URL; file names and contents written by other people reach the agent as tool output; no telemetry, no shell access, no background process. Independent community plugin, not affiliated with Yandex.

Browser Use (https://browser-use.com) cloud browser backend. Supports both direct BROWSER_USE_API_KEY and the managed Nous tool gateway. Also powers the 'Nous Subscription' UX flow that bills usage to a Nous subscription.

Browserbase (https://browserbase.com) cloud browser backend. Requires BROWSERBASE_API_KEY + BROWSERBASE_PROJECT_ID. Supports stealth, proxies, and keep-alive sessions; auto-falls-back when paid features are unavailable.

Bubblewrap terminal backend for Linux: every terminal and execute_code command runs in its own bwrap sandbox on this machine at the host's own paths, with a read-only root, a writable working directory (per profile: restricted, workspace or network), the dot entries of the home directory (credential stores always) and the Hermes home hidden, private temp and process directories, agent and docker sockets masked, and per-command memory, CPU and process limits (`hermes config set terminal.backend bubblewrap`). Disclosure — no Python dependencies and no network calls of its own: it runs your commands through the `bwrap` and `prlimit` binaries you install (bubblewrap, util-linux), and under the default `network` profile those commands share the host network. It reads no credentials. File tools (read_file, write_file, patch, search_files) still run on the host and are not confined, and because the working directory is a real host directory Hermes keeps its dangerous-command prompts, as for the local backend.

Build, run and manage sigrex.io trading automation (code and AI strategies, trading bots, webhooks and signals across crypto exchanges, DEXs and prediction markets) through the official Sigrex MCP server (Streamable HTTP at https://mcp.sigrex.io, OAuth sign-in, no keys in config), with the sigrex workflow skill bundled. Portable Agent Plugins v1 package (mcp.json + skills/), no Python or executables; needs a free Sigrex account. The connection has full account access, including actions that can place live trades. Disclosure — the tool set is served by the remote MCP server at runtime and is not covered by the pinned sha; the bundled skill instructs the agent to confirm before any action that moves money or changes data.

Build, run and test Python in an offline container per chat, with results as a plain file:line issue list. The agent syncs files or folders in as copies, then runs run (a shell command), check (ruff error rules) and test (pytest); fixes stay in the box until the user asks for export, which writes changed files back through write_file and reports host files changed since the sync as conflicts. In Hermes Desktop a VS Code-style editor opens beside the chat: file tabs with in-place editing, Run / Check / Test / Stop, and PROBLEMS / OUTPUT / RUNS panels that follow the agent live. Ships the runbox:dev-loop starting-point skill. Disclosure — needs Docker (on macOS a dedicated colima profile 'runbox', started on demand with --activate=false and its own Docker config); pulls the container image pinned by digest and installs a hash-pinned checker toolchain (ruff 0.16.9, pytest 9.1.1 and deps) from PyPI once per image; the work container has no network, hardened flags, and runs commands without Hermes' dangerous-command approval like Hermes' Docker backend; install (PyPI) always asks for approval in a separate installer container; a write_file/patch on an imported original asks for approval (guard_imports); export reads each existing target through read_file before replacing it; a background thread removes idle containers (15 min), stops the VM, and removes boxes of deleted or long-idle chats (reads state.db read-only hourly); adds a short per-turn note (about 80 tokens); no credentials or telemetry.

Built on the Moonraker HTTP API. Cron reports klippy_shutdown, complete, error, paused (after printing), cancelled, stalled. Disclosure — Talks to the one Moonraker URL you set. Over plain http on a LAN, MOONRAKER_API_KEY is sent unencrypted. Pause, resume and cancel ask for Hermes approval every time and are refused under cron, yolo, approvals off and unattended sessions. The plugin has no user list of its own: anyone you allow on your Hermes gateway can request a move and approve it. Answering "always" adds an unused line to config.yaml. The optional watch is a cron job (a model turn every 5 minutes by default) that stays after uninstall until you run unschedule. vision_check, off by default, sends webcam stills to your model. The plugin host cannot watch. Not tested on real hardware.

Bunny Space gateway adapter for Hermes Agent. Connects a Hermes profile (the bot brain) to the Bunny Space relay so the bot joins private rooms, answers its owner, and handles @bot:<slug> mentions in posts and comments. Outbound pull transport; no external dependencies. Disclosure — replies are prompted to be in Spanish; @bot mention tasks and assistance tasks are dispatched to Hermes under the fixed sender id "owner" (BUNNY_SPACE_ALLOWED_USERS must contain "owner"), and the plugin refuses to dispatch third-party content unless platform_toolsets.bunny_space is restricted to read-only tools (the platform's effective toolset, including MCP and plugin toolsets; add no_mcp when MCP servers are enabled); the private assistance worker is opt-in via BUNNY_SPACE_ASSISTANCE=1 (the relay cannot enable it); setting BUNNY_SPACE_ALLOW_ALL_USERS makes the connector refuse to connect; the relay sets the poll interval and may hand the connector a WebSocket "wake" URL it then connects to (wake signals only, no message content).

Buzz gateway adapter for Hermes Agent. Connects to a Buzz community relay (Block's open-source human+agent collaboration platform built on Nostr) and relays messages between channels/DMs and the Hermes agent. Relay operations shell out to the buzz CLI binary (JSON in/out); verified inbound media uses Hermes' bundled HTTP client.

CCR compression plugin - 28-type classifier, 13 tools, opt-in context engine, TOML-driven templates. Disclosure - pre_tool_call auto-backgrounds long terminal/process commands (modify: background=true, notify_on_complete=true) and rewrites chained terminal commands when enabled. Disclosure — hook and tool logic runs in prebuilt native binaries (libaphrodite_hermes + aphrodite proxy, v1.6.6) built from the public PlayForm/Aphrodite source and fetched by an explicit download.sh step checked against in-tree SHA-256 sums; register() starts a background proxy on 127.0.0.1:9797/9798 whose management routes are open to local processes unless APHRODITE_MGMT_TOKEN is set; pre_tool_call by default rewrites slow terminal commands (cargo/npm/pip/docker/curl…) to run in the background (background=true, notify_on_complete=true) and splits chained commands when enabled; aphrodite_prefetch reads files the model names into its store (refuses .env, auth.json, ~/.ssh and the Hermes home); requires its own APHRODITE_API_KEY for an upstream LLM endpoint (default api.openai.com).

CLI-backed skills for local code discovery and entity-diff review with Sem, plus optional Weave branch-merge previews. Requires user-installed CLIs; does not apply edits or merges, install binaries, or change Git configuration.

CLIProxyAPI as native Hermes model providers: discovers each CPA provider group (Claude, Codex, xAI, Gemini, Kiro and others) and registers one profile per group on the wire its CPA executor accepts (Anthropic Messages, Responses or Chat Completions), with context windows and reasoning levels from CPA. Disclosure — sends model-list and inference requests, authenticated with the API key env var you name, to the CPA base_url you configure; with an optional management key it also makes bounded read-only GETs to CPA's management API; with an optional billing route it sends inference, and a model-list GET, to the gateway URL you configure, authenticated with the gateway key env var you name. Known limit: Hermes strips from agent subprocesses only the key env vars a registered provider declares, so the management key env var, and on a routed instance the CPA key env var, stay readable by agent shells.

Call any Scalekit connector from Hermes: 500+ connectors and 20,000+ tools. Disclosure — HTTP calls go to the Scalekit environment URL you paste; the three Scalekit values are read with get_secret; one person id is stored at plugin-data/scalekit/identifier; the model can request an approval link, run a named tool, or proxy one HTTP request. Provider tokens stay in Scalekit; no shell, no background process, no telemetry.

Camofox browser backend: browse with a self-hosted anti-detection Firefox (Camoufox, C++ fingerprint spoofing) through the camofox-browser REST server. Registers the browser_* tools (navigate, snapshot with clickable refs, click, type, scroll, back, press, get_images, vision, JavaScript console, plus cookie import when CAMOFOX_API_KEY is set) in the `camofox` toolset, with `hermes camofox setup|status`; existing CAMOFOX_* variables and browser.camofox settings carry over. Formerly built into Hermes core; existing users are migrated automatically. Disclosure: one Python dependency (requests). It talks only to the Camofox server at CAMOFOX_URL (e.g. http://localhost:9377, which you run yourself: Docker or `npm start`), sending CAMOFOX_API_KEY as a bearer token when set. Page text reaches only your model as tool output; browser_vision sends the screenshot to your configured auxiliary vision model. Snapshots mask values that look like secrets (API keys, tokens), but text typed into form fields, passwords included, shows up in snapshots. Oversized snapshots and screenshots are written under the Hermes home (cache/web, browser_screenshots). Cookie import reads Netscape cookies.txt files only from browser.camofox.cookies_dir (default ~/.camofox/cookies). Inert on Hermes cores that still bundle Camofox.

Carbon Voice gateway adapter for Hermes Agent. Connects via Socket.IO (primary) with REST polling fallback — no public webhook or tunnel required. Persists a cursor to disk so messages received while Hermes is offline are processed on the next startup. Replies via POST /v3/messages/start, so the Her
Cashew — persistent thought-graph memory with local embeddings, organic decay, and autonomous think cycles.

Catalan (Català) language pack for Hermes Agent — UI translation for core (CLI, gateway, approval prompts and tips), TUI and Desktop. Covers all text-overridable catalog keys; preserves command syntax and non-text Desktop values. Manifest-only plugin, no code execution, no network. Disclosure — text-only catalogs; registering the pack never changes display.language, the user opts in via config.
Central Hermes Desktop inbox for reports produced by local cron runs.

Chatto gateway adapter for Hermes Agent. Connects to a Chatto server (self-hosted team chat) and relays messages between rooms/DMs and the Hermes agent.  Uses the Chatto ConnectRPC API (JSON over HTTP) for outbound messages and the Chatto realtime WebSocket protocol (binary protobuf) for inbound eve
Checkbox staged memory writes and approve or reject the selection from a dialog.

Checks cold email against the law before it goes out: when the agent sends an email with a send tool, one of Hermes's email skills (himalaya, agentmail, Google Workspace) or an email API call, Precleared checks each new recipient against UK PECR and UK GDPR, US CAN-SPAM, Canada's CASL and German, French, Australian, Irish and Dutch rules; anything not cleared goes to Hermes's approval prompt (or is refused in block mode) with the rule, its source and a signed receipt. Adds precleared_check and precleared_verify_receipt tools and a cold-email-check skill. Disclosure — when the agent sends email through a send tool, an email skill (himalaya, agentmail, Google Workspace), a mailer command or an email-API call, and on every precleared_check call, the plugin sends each new recipient's address with the configured sender country, address source, pitch and optional prospect country to precleared.dev over HTTPS; Precleared keeps a signed receipt of each check that anyone holding the receipt id can open at precleared.dev/r/<id>. The optional PRECLEARED_API_KEY is read through Hermes's secret scope and sent only in the Authorization header; without a key, checks draw on a free allowance shared by everyone on the same network. Emails not cleared go to Hermes's approval prompt (or are refused in block mode), and verdicts are cached under hashed addresses in plugin state for 30 days. No shell commands, background processes or telemetry; maintained by the operator of Precleared.

Choose a separate scorer to set the reasoning effort of each Hermes request. Disclosure — off by default; when a mode is enabled (or on an explicit `/hae probe`), sends the latest user message (or the parent-written subagent goal), truncated to 4000 characters, plus any configured guidance to the scorer you select (TypeSafe Jev at api.typesafe.ai by default, or OpenAI Decisions, OpenRouter, Cloudflare Workers AI, Nace at console.nace.ai, or a custom URL) using that service's key; opt-in settings can also send the target model identity, up to 6 earlier user/assistant text messages (1200 characters each) and a separate continuation question to the same scorer; in Hermes Desktop it also sets the focused chat's session reasoning selector through the gateway `config.set` API after each applied change, and it keeps a prompt-free effort-change history (64 changes × 64 conversations), per-conversation mode overrides (at most 256 conversations) and per-route cache verdicts built from provider token counters (at most 128 routes) in its plugin data directory.

Choose models across Hermes profiles from a Dashboard tab: a per-profile picker built on host-supplied model data (SDK-authenticated GET /api/model/options), a preview of provider/model intent across every supported model-selection slot (main, delegation, auxiliary, judge, fallback, MoA, cron, plugin and specialist), and one-click apply or revert with presets. Main-slot preview shows intended provider/model, not the exact persisted diff; the exact diff is shown only after host readback. Disclosure — its apply route reads and edits the profiles' config.yaml (that is the plugin's function) through public seams only: POST /api/model/set for main and compatible auxiliary slots, and public hermes_cli.config load/save under the target home for other slots; credential presence checks use public profile-scoped secret helpers (agent.secret_scope), and profile discovery uses public hermes_constants. The plugin makes no direct third-party requests and opens no provider caches or pricing registries directly, but its browser tab does call the host's /api/model/* routes through the Dashboard SDK, and the host options route may itself initiate provider or pricing I/O even without an explicit refresh request, so reads are not guaranteed cache-only. It runs no shell commands or background processes and reports nothing. The private undo journal stores a full pre-change snapshot of each config it edits, which can contain sensitive fields including embedded credentials. Saved presets also persist reviewed change values, potentially including inline credentials or credential-bearing base URLs, in presets.json (0600) under get_hermes_home()/state/hermes-model-switcher/ (0700). The host write route has no expected-revision check: readback surfaces many foreign edits as recovery_required, but a concurrent same-key edit can be overwritten undetected and full-state deletions retain an unrelated-write race, so not every foreign edit is guaranteed to surface.

Chronos — NAS-mediated managed cron provider for scale-to-zero hosted agents. Delegates the "wake me at time T" trigger to Nous infrastructure so an idle gateway can scale to zero and still fire cron jobs. The agent computes each job's next-fire time and asks NAS to arm a one-shot; NAS calls the agent back at fire time over an authenticated webhook. Inert unless cron.provider=chronos.

Chutes model provider for Hermes Agent via API key. Disclosure — model provider; prompts, tool schemas and CHUTES_API_KEY go to llm.chutes.ai (or CHUTES_BASE_URL), plus a GET /models catalog probe with the same key
Click-through numbered marks on any live Mac window — chess, games, Photoshop, Settings — so Hermes can teach on the real UI without clicking for the user.

Client for the local VoiceStudio text-to-speech app (debpalash/VoiceStudio): speak short text, design or clone voices, browse voices, render chaptered long-form audio, dub videos, and check server status. Six tools with mirrored slash commands plus a bundled skill. Disclosure — sends the text, script files, videos and voice samples you point it at to the VoiceStudio server you configure (default http://127.0.0.1:3900, plain HTTP) and saves the returned audio under HERMES_HOME/plugin-data/voicestudio; no credentials, no telemetry, no self-update.
ClinePass model provider with live model discovery and a curated fallback catalog.

Cloudflare Web Search backend for Hermes' existing web_search tool, with Ceramic, Exa, or Linkup selected in plugin settings. Search only; keep a separate extract backend. Disclosure — sends queries, result limits, gateway IDs, and optional BYOK aliases to api.cloudflare.com, which forwards searches to the selected provider and records them in AI Gateway logs. Requests can consume gateway credits or provider quota. Reads its own settings and CLOUDFLARE_WEB_SEARCH_API_TOKEN through Hermes' profile-scoped APIs. Registers one web provider, with no new tools, hooks, background processes, file writes, or self-updater. Independent community plugin.

Cloudflare Workers AI as a Hermes model provider (`--provider workers-ai`, or Cloudflare Workers AI in `hermes model`, which asks for the token and the account's base URL): the 16 Workers AI models with function calling and 64K+ context, Cloudflare's context windows (a custom endpoint lists no models and assumes 256K for the 128K gpt-oss), reasoning effort in the form each model accepts, and a clear message when a free-plan account picks a paid-plan model. Not affiliated with Cloudflare. Disclosure — registers one model provider at import and nothing else (no tools, hooks, commands or threads); the model list and details are built in, so nothing is fetched to show them; chat requests go to the URL in CLOUDFLARE_WORKERS_AI_BASE_URL through Hermes' own client with CLOUDFLARE_WORKERS_AI_API_TOKEN, both read by Hermes per profile; the plugin itself opens no connections, reads and writes no files and starts no processes.

Codex-style ask-about-selection for Hermes Desktop: select text anywhere in a conversation, and a small pill appears above the selection offering Quote & ask — the selection lands in the message composer as a Markdown quote with the caret on the line below, ready for your question — or Copy, which puts the same Markdown quote on the clipboard. A command-palette entry does the same without the pill. Desktop-only (desktop/plugin.js inside the plugin SDK surface): no agent tools, hooks, middleware or env vars, nothing written to disk, nothing persisted. Disclosure — reads window.getSelection() and the selection rectangle; serializes the selection to Markdown (fenced code with its language, nested lists, bold/italic, links), cut at 4000 characters; writes the draft through host.composer (getDraft/setDraft, falling back to insertText, then ctx.os.writeClipboard) and focuses the composer; ignores selections made inside the composer itself and hides on collapse, scroll or Escape. No network calls, no credentials, no telemetry.
Coding workflow skills — dual-model harness, subagent-driven development, and implementation planning patterns for Hermes Agent

Cognition session-end memory — facts regex-extracted from your messages at session end, stored in a local SQLite queue and JSON log under one repo label, with fetch-first merge, per-entry provenance, and budgeted prefetch (tools: cognition_search, cognition_status, read-only cognition_dream). Disclosure — saves verbatim excerpts (up to 400 chars) of your own messages that match preference/decision phrases in plain local files under HERMES_HOME/cognition/ (SQLite queue, JSON commit log) and re-injects them into later prompts sent to your model provider; the author name is read from ~/.gitconfig; the plugin makes no network calls of its own.

Collapses carriage-return progress bars (tqdm, git clone --progress and similar) in terminal output to the frame a terminal would show, so the model reads one line instead of every redraw: a 300-step tqdm loop goes from 17,396 characters to about 120. Other text written between redraws, CRLF line endings and output without a carriage return are left as they are. Disclosure — register() adds one transform_terminal_output hook that rewrites the output string in memory; no tools, network access, subprocesses, files, settings or environment variables.

Command Code CLI-key model provider with a live OAuth catalog property bridge, plan limits and failover classification. Disclosure — uses the CLI-internal api.commandcode.ai/alpha/generate endpoint and CLI client headers, sends the full conversation, tool schemas, cwd path and OS/Python version, and imports a static key from the read-only CLI credential file or a browser hand-off; no OAuth exchange takes place. Hermes also bundles commandcode for the documented Provider API.

Communication boards, explicit speech, switch scanning and reviewed AI proposals for Hermes Desktop. Disclosure — Desktop-only page; Speak sends your message text through the Hermes gateway to the TTS provider configured in Hermes (cloud providers receive it) and the audio plays on the gateway host, which may be remote; the AI helpers open a separate Hermes chat session per request and send your topic or message as a normal agent turn on your model provider; saved phrases and approved boards are kept in plaintext in the plugin's Desktop storage.

Community (non-official) plugin that rewrites Hermes terminal commands through RTK (rtk-ai/rtk, Apache-2.0) before execution, so the model sees compact output instead of raw command spam — cutting tokens on common dev commands.
