Adds a fail-open pre_tool_call hook (2s timeout, unexpected exits leave the command untouched), an optional desktop pane, and update scripts. Disclosure — every terminal tool command is passed to the rtk binary found on PATH (rtk-ai/rtk, installed separately) and replaced with rtk's rewrite before approval and execution; fail-open when rtk is missing or errors. Community mirror of upstream's hooks/hermes/rtk-rewrite, not affiliated with rtk-ai. scripts/update.sh downloads the pinned RTK release binary (v0.49.0, checksum-verified).

Community (non-official) plugin wiring GBrain (garrytan/gbrain, MIT) into Hermes as a local memory layer over MCP: /gbrain status command, desktop starter, and per-profile Postgres setup/update/maintenance scripts. Not affiliated with upstream. Disclosure — the plugin itself only adds a /gbrain status command and a Desktop pane; GBrain is installed by the user via scripts/setup.sh, which installs bun (curl|bash), an unpinned gbrain from GitHub HEAD, and provisions PostgreSQL with sudo.

Community Zvec memory backend for Hermes Agent - in-process HNSW + RocksDB FTS store with native hybrid retrieval and session-safe lock governance; embeddings via any Ollama-compatible endpoint (local Ollama bge-m3 by default).

Community platform plugin (not affiliated with Meta or Nous Research) connecting a WhatsApp Agent to Hermes through Meta's WhatsApp Agent Platform API (/agent/v1): long-poll inbound (no public URL), text and media. Disclosure — sends the API key and message content, files included, only to Meta: api.whatsapp.com, plus lookaside.fbsbx.com for downloads (per WhatsApp's Third-Party Agents Terms, agent chats are not end-to-end encrypted); stores the poll cursor, recent message ids and the creator's id under HERMES_HOME; no other network egress, no telemetry, no self-update. Exception: Hermes fetches image URLs in replies (SSRF-guarded, no key), revealing the server's IP to that host. Files go only to the creator; Meta keeps uploads up to 30 days. Received files are cached under HERMES_HOME (deleted after ~24 h while the gateway runs) and may reach the configured model, vision or speech-to-text provider. WHATSAPP_AGENT_PLATFORM_MEDIA_ENABLED=false disables media. By default only the agent's creator (verified through Meta's API) can message Hermes; WHATSAPP_AGENT_PLATFORM_ALLOWED_USERS or WHATSAPP_AGENT_PLATFORM_ALLOW_ALL_USERS widens that explicitly. The agent API key is saved to the Hermes .env; the state file under HERMES_HOME is 0600 and never contains the key.

Community plugin that rewrites Hermes terminal commands through RTK (rtk-ai/rtk, Apache-2.0) so the model sees compact output. Adds a backend gate: it rewrites only for terminal backends a profile opts in to (default local), so a Docker or remote backend without rtk never receives an rtk command. Fail-open pre_tool_call hook (2s timeout). Disclosure — every terminal command on an opted-in backend (default local) is passed to the rtk binary on the Hermes host's PATH (or RTK_BIN) and replaced with rtk's stdout before approval and execution; the plugin does not validate the rewrite, fails open on timeout or error, and downloads nothing (the repo's optional Containerfile fetches a checksum-pinned RTK release only when you build it). Not affiliated with rtk-ai.

Companion to hermes-kame-api-rotation (install both). A model-provider plugin that re-registers Hermes' bundled API-key profiles unchanged except for create_client and create_messages_client, which return the rotation plugin's key-rotating client; otherwise None and Hermes builds its own. Same endpoints as Hermes, no third-party service, no core override.

Compare pinned Terraform provider and module versions with the public registry. Disclosure — tools are on for every Hermes surface, including the gateway. Stop a surface with hermes tools disable --platform <name> terraform-drift, or the plugin with hermes plugins disable terraform-drift. Nothing is written under plugin-data/terraform-drift, and there is no key. Only the directory you name is read, and only .tf, .tf.json, and .terraform.lock.hcl. Symlinks and .. are refused, and .env, tfvars, .terraform, backend values, and hashes are not returned. The provider pin is the lock version, not the required_providers constraint. A module pin is an exact version only. GET calls only registry.terraform.io and, for a github.com source, raw.githubusercontent.com CHANGELOG.md. Redirects and proxy variables are ignored. A timeout or failed read leaves latest empty and is not called current. Semver orders versions, so 1.10.0 is newer than 1.9.0. The digest text is not sent and no cron job is created. known keeps newer versions, and omitting it does not call rows new today. There is no approval card. Before the call, name the directory and say there is no init, plan, apply, or state write. Cron, yolo, and approvals off can still run this read. MIT, no daily cap, requires Hermes >=0.21.4.

Connect 28 production-ready MCP servers to any coding agent. Portable Agent Plugins v1 package (mcp.json + skills/): three zero-config stdio servers out of the box (Hacker News, arXiv, npm registry, each pinned to an exact npm version), plus the umt-mcp skill that drives the umt CLI to wire any of the 28 servers into Claude Code, Cursor, Codex, Windsurf, Zed and more. Needs Node.js and npm on PATH.

Connect AgentPlaybooks skills and hosted MCP/OpenAPI tools to Hermes, with guided setup, profile selection, permission diagnostics and an authenticated MCP check. Requires Node.js 20+ and @agentplaybooks/cli@0.7.0; the CLI is installed separately. Disclosure — skill-only; the separately installed apb CLI does the work. `apb hermes setup --apply` restores complete skill trees into the chosen project and edits the selected Hermes profile's config.yaml to register those skills and a hosted playbook MCP endpoint. Local writes require --apply; setup also probes MCP initialization and tool listing using a scoped key from the process environment, without invoking tools. `doctor` checks profile credential variable names without exposing their values. Hosted operations contact agentplaybooks.ai (or an explicitly configured service); skill restore uses `apb login`, and `apb push --apply` uploads project configuration (secret references, not values).

Connect Hermes to Titanos marketplace, Amazon, listings, Ads, and product research tools through the pinned Titanos OAuth MCP client. This portable Agent Plugin v1 package bundles seven operating skills, requires Node.js 20.18.1 or newer, and uses browser authorization with a Titanos account. Disclosure — starts the npm package @titanos/mcp-agents@1.47.2 via npx (fetched from npm on first run); its tools read and WRITE live marketplace/Ads accounts under your Titanos OAuth session.
Connect Replaid with OAuth to read, triage, and draft replies in your social inbox.

Connect a Hermes agent through an existing Ando invitation and receive authorized messages. Disclosure — connects outbound to Ando (mcp.ando.so, api.ando.so, realtime.ando.so) with an agent API key stored at $HERMES_HOME/ando/connection.json (mode 600); Ando messages from the connecting member (or members the operator explicitly allowlists) start Hermes turns and the final reply, with any files it attaches, is posted back to Ando; message attachments are uploaded and downloaded through short-lived single-use links Ando issues (up to 20 MB each; received files are cached in the profile's Hermes cache); hermes ando connect edits gateway.platforms.ando in config.yaml.

Connect your agent to third-party tools and APIs (web search and scraping, people and company data, social media, media generation, email and phone) through one integration. The agent discovers, compares and runs tools at runtime, paid per call from one Monid balance. Disclosure — Monid (monid.ai, by Monid / monid-ai) is a paid third-party marketplace: the agent installs the @monid-ai/cli npm package or connects to mcp.monid.ai, sends your requests and any uploaded files to Monid and on to its providers, and each run spends your prepaid Monid workspace balance. The "confirm the price first" step is an instruction to the model in the bundled skill, not a Hermes approval prompt, unless you add `trust: untrusted` to `mcp_servers.monid`.

Context and control for any AI. Agent identity, scoped access, and proof across tools. Disclosure — skills-only package: its workflow skills steer the agent to Proofable's hosted MCP server at mcp.proofable.me (which you add yourself with `hermes mcp add … --auth oauth`) to check identity proofs and agent permissions, create wallet-signed proofs, and store, list or revoke secrets in Proofable's hosted vault, so secrets you store and proof/agent data go to Proofable; Hermes does not prompt before those MCP tools run unless you give the server a trust setting; the skills also suggest Proofable's own optional `proofable` CLI, which edits MCP/project config.

Context engine that compresses older tool output and turns locally with LLMSlim instead of asking a model for a summary: no LLM call, deterministic output, and the start of the prompt is sent unchanged, so prompt caching keeps working. Select it with context.engine: llmslim. Disclosure: installs llmslim==0.11.1 from PyPI (with numpy, scikit-learn and jsonschema); registers no tools, hooks or middleware; makes no network calls, runs no shell commands, needs no credentials, writes no files and sends no telemetry; reads its settings from config.yaml through Hermes's config loader. Token counts use a character estimate unless tiktoken is already installed in Hermes's environment, in which case tiktoken may download its encoding file once.
Context optimization and execution alignment for agent sessions.

Context window usage at a glance: a Context button in the status bar shows tokens used vs. budget, percent full, free space and an estimated breakdown by category, plus context-file sources. Works during a running turn. Read-only token/usage monitor, no backend.

Context-window forensics: per-turn input/output token estimates, the single largest tool output of each turn, oversized tool calls (args over 50 KB), and compaction events, recorded as metadata only (tool name, byte length, ids, timestamps — never args or results) in a local SQLite DB under HERMES_HOME/plugin-data/context-audit/. Adds a /context-audit slash command that prints the top 5 context eaters over a window with one mitigation per entry.
Control DaVinci Resolve Studio live, or generate importable interchange files for free DaVinci Resolve.

Control a headless Android emulator from Hermes — live sidebar, app management, GPS/battery/network simulation, and ADB tools. Emulator host is Linux. Disclosure — requires a pre-installed Android SDK under ~/Android/Sdk; runs adb, emulator, avdmanager and sdkmanager on the host, and the dashboard's Create AVD action downloads Android system images from Google via sdkmanager. emu_shell runs arbitrary commands inside the emulator; emu_install/emu_push copy host files into it.

Control real iPhones rented from 0bull (screenshots, on-screen text, taps, typing, device commands, recorded macros, an on-phone agent) and publish videos to TikTok and YouTube Shorts from them, through the hosted 0bull Streamable HTTP MCP server plus three workflow skills. Portable Agent Plugins v1 package (mcp.json + skills/), no plugin code. Requires a 0bull account with a rented phone and browser OAuth consent (add the server with auth: oauth, then hermes mcp login 0bull); no API key or client secret is stored in the plugin. Posting sends the user's video and caption to TikTok or YouTube through the phone's own apps. Disclosure — hosted-only connector; screenshots, on-screen text, anything typed on the phone (including passwords or codes you hand the agent) and your videos and captions go to 0bull.net; posts publish publicly to TikTok or YouTube; the server also exposes rental tools that spend money, which the skills tell the model never to call but Hermes does not block.

Controlled migration engine: maps an existing codebase, turns the behaviour that must survive into reviewable contracts, prepares a separate candidate and records old/new evidence before any production change. Disclosure — 27 tools plus a `hermes modernise` CLI and `/modernise` slash command; `assess`, `plan`, `record` and `recipe` read source trees and files at absolute paths the agent supplies (refusing symlinks, `.env`, `auth.json`, `credentials.json` and SSH keys) and never import or run repository code; `recipe` creates a new directory at an agent-chosen absolute path holding a copy of the source with fixed metadata edits; job records live under the plugin's data directory; only after you set `operator_config` and sign a one-use Ed25519 owner grant do `run`, `cancel` and `recover` invoke the local `docker` CLI, outside Hermes's command-approval prompt, to run, inspect and remove rootless, network-disabled, read-only, resource-limited containers from digest-pinned images you allow-list (never pulled); no network calls, no telemetry, no self-updater.

Convert one local file to Markdown with doc_convert on Linux and macOS, built on Microsoft's MarkItDown. Microsoft and MarkItDown are trademarks of the Microsoft group of companies. Disclosure — the doc_markdown toolset is on by default on every surface, including a gateway, so anyone you allow there can call doc_convert; stop it with hermes tools. It does not fetch pages. Unattended sessions still convert when Hermes calls the tool. This plugin creates no cron job. A child process runs MarkItDown with no Hermes keys in its environment; on macOS the plugin runs ps about every 10 ms to watch that child's memory. It stops 8 seconds after its converters load, at 60 seconds if loading never finishes, or above 922746880 bytes. It is not a sandbox: after realpath it may read any allowlisted path it can open. Unpublished Hermes code locates the Hermes home, and a failed check refuses the path. Removal deletes the plugin directory, not the markitdown package. Windows was not tested.

Conxt governed memory provider — recall before each turn (personal, plus a team's approved memories), conversation capture in batches, and tools to search, remember, and propose team memories that a person approves in Conxt before anyone recalls them. Disclosure — Each turn's message (first 500 characters) and the conversation's user and assistant messages are sent to the Conxt API at mcp.conxt.dev (or an https CONXT_BASE_URL you set) with your CONXT_API_KEY; tool results are not sent, but text the assistant repeats is. Every entry Hermes's built-in memory tool adds is also copied to your Conxt memory, and conxt_remember / conxt_propose send the memory text they are given. No telemetry, no shell commands, and nothing is written automatically from cron or subagent runs. Requires a Conxt plan that includes API keys.

Copy provider API keys (and provider base-URL overrides) from one profile onto other profiles — a one-time, explicit copy from a desktop page. Per-profile missing/present badges, fill-missing by default with an explicit overwrite opt-in. OAuth sign-ins and messaging bot tokens never travel; values never cross back in responses.

CoreWeave Serverless Inference model provider. Disclosure — Hermes sends model discovery and chat requests, including prompts and tool results, to https://api.inference.wandb.ai/v1 (CoreWeave / W&B Inference) using COREWEAVE_API_KEY; the installed provider registers a profile only and reads no credential files, starts no processes and adds no telemetry.

CortexLayer memory provider — page-linked long-term memory with link-expansion retrieval, wired into Hermes' automatic per-turn recall (prefetch) and persistence (sync_turn), plus a pre-compress checkpoint so evidence Hermes' own context compaction would otherwise drop is saved first. Platform mode only: each turn's query and conversational content is sent to the hosted api.cortexlayer.net (HTTPS, API-key authenticated) for storage/retrieval — no local/offline mode. Requires a free CortexLayer account and API key.
Crawl4ai self-hosted web content extraction. Requires CRAWL4AI_URL and CRAWL4AI_API_TOKEN pointing at your instance.

Create, analyze, and optimize campaigns across Google Ads, Meta Ads, TikTok Ads, LinkedIn Ads, Amazon Ads, ChatGPT Ads, and Microsoft Ads through the hosted Adspirer MCP. Portable Agent Plugins v1 package with fourteen paid-media workflow skills and approval safeguards; OAuth uses pinned mcp-remote@0.1.49 over npx stdio, so Node.js 20.18.1+ and npm are required. Disclosure — creates and edits real ad campaigns that spend your ad budgets; confirm-before-spend is enforced by skill instructions, not by Hermes.

Create, clean, and verify standalone Markdown with conservative semantic repair and deterministic artifact checks. Disclosure — skill-only plugin that has the agent run its bundled Node.js 22+ scripts through the terminal; on first use it runs `npm ci` in the plugin folder (lockfile-pinned packages from registry.npmjs.org), and the optional `/wolfmarkdown setup` also creates skill symlinks in ~/.agents/skills and ~/.claude/skills.

Cross-profile agent dispatch for Hermes Agent — 12 tools for agents talking to agents: async dispatch with SSE completion, synchronous multi-turn chat, model-selectable in-process subagents, a durable SQLite run ledger, fail-closed per-target model-route discovery, and host-owned bare LLM inference. Disclosure — sends task text and bearer tokens to the Hermes API servers you configure (plaintext HTTP permitted, warn-only); stores full dispatch text in a local SQLite ledger; delegate_subagent may use any provider credential you have configured.

Crypto research in plain English through the official StalkChain Data MCP server (Streamable HTTP at https://data.stalkchain.com/mcp/directory, OAuth sign-in, no keys in config): check a coin before you buy, vet a trader before you copy them, see what smart money is buying, review a wallet and set price alerts, across Solana, Ethereum, Base, BNB Chain, Monad, Hyperliquid and Robinhood Chain, plus the StonkFun launchpad. Portable Agent Plugins v1 package (mcp.json + 18 skills), no Python or executables; needs a StalkChain account with credits. Read-only: never trades, moves funds or signs anything; the only write is the user's own price alerts, after they confirm. Disclosure — the tool set is served by the remote MCP server at runtime and is not covered by the pinned sha; each tool call sends the tool name and its inputs to data.stalkchain.com and spends the account's credits; price alerts are stored by StalkChain with their destination (account email or a user-given Discord, Slack or Telegram webhook URL, which can embed a bot token) until deleted or fired.

Cua's own plugin: runs Hermes's terminal, file and code tools inside a Cua Space, an isolated Linux, macOS or Windows machine you can watch live, as a terminal backend (`hermes config set terminal.backend cua`). On Hermes 0.22.3 and later, Bot Desktop, computer_use and the browser follow the terminal into the Space too (needs the `cua` command). Disclosure — installs the `cua` Python SDK (>=0.5.0,<0.8); every command the agent runs, every file it touches, and (on 0.22.3+) every screen, click and page the agent drives go to the Space: on this machine for a local Space, or on Cua's cloud (cua.ai) or a machine you name, using the sign-in `cua auth login` saved (the plugin never reads or stores a token, and keeps CUA_API_KEY/CUA_DAEMON_TOKEN out of the Space). Windows Spaces run Hermes's tools in Git Bash, like Hermes on a Windows PC: if the Space lacks Git for Windows or Python, the plugin installs them inside the Space (pinned official installers checked against SHA-256, `winget` fallback) and adds `C:\c`-style drive aliases there. The optional `desktop` setting installs a desktop stack (VNC, Chromium, agent-browser, cua-driver) inside a Linux Space with sudo there. Nothing is installed on this machine. With the default `space: create` it makes a fresh Space per session and deletes it when Hermes finishes (`delete_on_exit`); because that Space is a disposable sandbox, Hermes skips its dangerous-command prompts there, as it does for its other container backends. A Space you name is never deleted and keeps the prompts.

Cursor model provider using the official proprietary Cursor SDK. Disclosure — uses Cursor's proprietary cursor-sdk (PyPI, bundled binary bridge on loopback) with the user's CURSOR_API_KEY; sends the full conversation, tool schemas/results and images (HTTPS URLs or base64) to Cursor; keeps private per-session SDK workspaces under HERMES_HOME/cache/cursor-sdk; Cursor built-in tools and MCP are requested off and Hermes keeps tool execution and approvals.

Cursor-style composer modes (ask / agent / plan / debug) for the Hermes desktop — the mode's operating note reaches the model inside the turn's model-facing bytes, never the bubble, transcript or session titles, and ask mode is enforced read-only on the tool side.

Czech (Čeština) language pack for Hermes Agent covering all three UI surfaces — core CLI/gateway/platforms (3,509/3,509 keys), the Ink TUI (1,385/1,385) and the Desktop app (5,324 of 5,451). Core and TUI keys match the English source of `main` at d050956 (2026-10-25) exactly: no key upstream has since removed and no placeholder divergence, checked by flattening both sides. The remaining 125 Desktop keys are the ones whose English value is a function with branching (plural counts such as `cron.count`, conditional labels such as `assistant.thread.errorSwitchToModel`), which the pack format cannot express as one template — they are omitted so they fall back to English instead of rendering a wrong Czech form. Two core strings (`display.verb_connector.search` and `.default`) drop an invisible zero-width space the upstream English catalog carries for spacing; the install scanner rates it HIGH while the visible text is identical. Ships the same text as upstream PR #105503, so if that PR lands the bundled locale and this pack agree. Manifest-only plugin: flat dotted YAML catalogs under locales/, no network, no dependencies. Disclosure — an `__init__.py` whose `register()` is a no-op is included so the Desktop "Install from Git" flow accepts the pack (#138118); registering the pack never changes display.language, the user opts in via `hermes config set display.language cs`. Česká lokalizace rozhraní Hermes Agent.

DAG-based context engine that never loses a message — full-text search, semantic recall, assertion-backed evidence compilation, and pre-answer sufficiency gating Disclosure — replaces the context engine and stores every turn's full raw transcript in HERMES_HOME/trove.db with secret redaction OFF by default; with TROVE_EMBEDDING_PROVIDER=voyage, transcript text is sent to Voyage AI for embeddings; as a fallback it reads private AIAgent attributes read-only via frame inspection. No other network egress.
DashScope (Qwen Cloud) image generation -- Wan 2.7 models via Alibaba Cloud Model Studio. Works with token plan (sk-sp-*) and PAYG (sk-ws-*) keys.
DashScope (Qwen Cloud) video generation -- HappyHorse 1.1 models via Alibaba Cloud Model Studio. Async task API. Works with token plan (sk-sp-*) keys.

Dashboard auth provider — OAuth 2.0 (authorization-code + PKCE) against Nous Portal. Auto-activates when a client_id is configured via either dashboard.oauth.client_id in config.yaml (canonical surface) or HERMES_DASHBOARD_OAUTH_CLIENT_ID env var (operator override; Portal injects this at Fly.io provisioning). dashboard.oauth.portal_url / HERMES_DASHBOARD_PORTAL_URL are optional and default to https://portal.nousresearch.com.

Dashboard auth provider — generic self-hosted OpenID Connect (authorization-code + PKCE, public client). Works against any conformant OIDC identity provider (Authentik, Keycloak, Zitadel, Authelia, Auth0, Okta, Google, …) via OIDC discovery. Auto-activates when an issuer + client_id are configured, either under dashboard.oauth.self_hosted.{issuer,client_id} in config.yaml (canonical surface) or via the HERMES_DASHBOARD_OIDC_ISSUER + HERMES_DASHBOARD_OIDC_CLIENT_ID env vars (operator override / secret injection). Scopes default to 'openid profile email'. Verifies the OIDC ID token (RS256/ES256) against the discovered jwks_uri.

Dashboard auth provider — non-interactive shared-bearer-secret for the gateway drain-control endpoint. The first consumer of the generic token-auth capability (supports_token/verify_token). nous-account-service provisions a per-agent unique secret via HERMES_DASHBOARD_DRAIN_SECRET; this provider verifies an inbound Authorization bearer token against it with a constant-time compare and registers /api/gateway/drain as token-authable. Fails CLOSED: a weak/short/low-entropy secret (< 256 bits) is rejected at registration and the endpoint stays disabled. No-op when the env var is unset. Behavioural knobs (scope, min_secret_chars) live under dashboard.drain_auth in config.yaml.

Dashboard auth provider — username/password (no OAuth IDP). A self-hosted 'just put a password on my dashboard' provider. Activates when dashboard.basic_auth.username plus a password (or password_hash) are configured via config.yaml (canonical surface) or the HERMES_DASHBOARD_BASIC_AUTH_* env vars. Sessions are stateless HMAC-signed tokens minted by the provider; password hashing uses stdlib scrypt (no third-party dependency). Set dashboard.basic_auth.secret for restart-surviving / multi-worker sessions.

Dashboard-only cron companion: a Pocket Watch pane showing cron jobs by schedule (daily/weekly/monthly), a health view of run outcomes and consecutive failures, a timeline, and maintenance actions — a read-oriented window onto the scheduler rather than another agent-facing toolset. Disclosure — the pane's API reads the cron jobs file under HERMES_HOME to render schedules and run history; it registers no tools, hooks or middleware, performs no network I/O and holds no credentials.
Dashboard-only read plugin for Agent Analytics inside Hermes.

Dashboard-only read plugin: visualize the shared-metrics telemetry Hermes collects locally — metric families, drilldowns, milestone timeline, install snapshot, and the exact next package payload. Send stays off.

Dataset import, adaptation, augmentation, translation, synthetic generation, and AutoScientist fine-tuning through the hosted Adaption MCP. Portable Agent Plugins v1 package with three workflow skills; the MCP server is added separately with OAuth (or an API key for headless use). Disclosure — skill-only, no code; the MCP tools call api.prod.adaptionlabs.ai, and launches spend Adaption credits (the skills request a cost estimate first, Hermes does not enforce it). Hermes does not prompt before those tools unless the server is configured with trust: untrusted.
DeepInfra image generation backend (FLUX, Qwen-Image, …) via OpenAI-compatible /v1/images/generations. Catalog discovered live from api.deepinfra.com.
DeepInfra video generation (text-to-video & image-to-video) via the OpenAI-compatible /v1/openai/videos endpoint. Catalog discovered live from api.deepinfra.com.

DeepSeek Search & Fetch as a backend for the built-in web_search and web_extract. Disclosure — sends web_search queries and web_extract URLs to api.deepseek.com with your DEEPSEEK_API_KEY and DeepSeek fetches the pages server-side; billed to your DeepSeek balance per successful request; no other endpoint, no telemetry, no file or shell access.

DeepSeek Search + Fetch — routes web_search and web_extract through DeepSeek's in-house AI search engine and server-side fetcher on api.deepseek.com (opened up in the vendor's 2026-10-17 changelog: AI-native engine indexing hundreds of billions of pages, multilingual, filters SEO spam / GEO manipulation / low-quality AIGC). Registers the provider id `deepseek-web`. Disclosure — each search/fetch is a separate billed DeepSeek call at $0.75 per 1,000 successful requests per endpoint, and only HTTP 200 responses that produce a result are billable (5 QPS per account per endpoint, plus a per-domain QPS limit on fetch); the provider reuses DEEPSEEK_API_KEY and sends it only to api.deepseek.com; extract returns Markdown only (no HTML variant, so web_extract(format="html") gets Markdown), and anti-bot or JS-rendered sites fail (zhihu.com, x.com, nytimes.com returned HTTP 404 in testing) while static pages work.
Deepgram Aura text-to-speech and Nova speech-to-text providers for Hermes Agent.
Default delegation strategy: every delegate_task subagent follows the delegation section of config.yaml (delegation.provider / model / base_url ...), else inherits the parent's model and credentials.
Defuddle content extraction — local, free, no API key. Shells out to the defuddle CLI for clean article markdown. Extract-only; pair with SearXNG or another search provider.

Delegate coding tasks to the Devin CLI, on your computer or in Devin Cloud, with live progress cards and change review in Hermes Desktop. Every launch goes through Hermes approval; Cloud runs need a separate Cloud-managed-permissions confirmation. Disclosure — spawns the vendor devin CLI from PATH or cli_path (devin acp, devin acp --cloud, devin --print, devin auth status, devin models list); the CLI edits files and runs shell commands in a folder the model picks (any folder unless allowed_roots is set) under the configured permission mode (accept-edits/smart auto-allow edits, dangerous auto-allows everything and needs allow_dangerous: true), and talks to Cognition's servers; Devin Cloud runs use Cognition-managed permissions that Hermes does not gate. Every model-initiated launch goes through Hermes approval; follow-ups typed on a Desktop run card and answers to Devin's prompts on the card start or allow actions on that click without a Hermes prompt (unanswered card prompts are denied after 300 s by default). Uses the existing Devin CLI login and stores no credentials; Hermes provider, bot and tool secrets are stripped from the child environment (extra_env is passed as set). Background runs continue after the turn up to their timeout and post Devin's output back into the conversation as a message when they finish. Run history (prompts, diffs, command output) and model preferences are saved under plugin-data/devin unless persist_runs is off. Independent community add-on, not affiliated with Cognition.
Delegate-only, fail-closed Kimi Code ACP integration for Hermes Agent
Dense, animated supercomputer light banks driven by system telemetry and live agent activity in Hermes Desktop.

Deploy, debug and manage Render applications with 20 unchanged skills from render-oss/skills and Render's hosted MCP connection. Disclosure — connects Hermes to Render's hosted MCP server (mcp.render.com) with your RENDER_API_KEY; the server is marked untrusted so tools without a read-only annotation need approval; account permissions apply and changes can incur Render charges; bundled skills guide shell commands, file edits and Render CLI installs (including the vendor's curl | sh installer).

Desktop RSS reader with reader-mode capture, drag-reorder subscriptions, mute rules, saved searches, AI summaries, keyboard shortcuts, and an optional headline ticker. Disclosure — optional YouTube cookies you paste in Settings are sent with YouTube feed requests; selectable User-Agent presets (incl. a ChatGPT-User string) are sent to feed hosts; YouTube videos render as youtube-nocookie.com embed iframes inside the reader.
Desktop and dashboard plugin: statusbar chip, palette command, and dashboard tab listing your GitHub repos (public + private) via the gh CLI.

Desktop fleet page plus a per-bot Home (status, metrics, alerts, tasks, routines, buttons) published by the bot as JSON. Disclosure — reads each local profile's home files, can run a declared cron routine from the UI on that bot's profile and credentials, and opens chat, a path, or a URL the bot declared; send_prompt buttons send the shown prompt into the bot's Bot Chat. Bot-declared run_action buttons run a script from the bot's home/actions/ folder: a script runs only after the user approves that exact file (SHA-256), is re-approved if it changes, and is limited to 30s and to that folder, but it runs as your user with the Hermes backend's full environment, including provider keys loaded for the profile Hermes was launched with. Approvals are kept under the Hermes root in bot-hq/approvals/. The `hermes hermes-bot-hq setup` command (asks first unless --yes) links the plugin into every profile's plugins folder and enables it there. No database, signup, or telemetry.

Desktop pane to manage skills and MCP connections across agent apps: save named loadouts, review changes, apply them, and undo the latest managed operation. Agent half is inert (no tools or hooks). Disclosure — MCP sync copies your Hermes mcp_servers env/header secrets into ~/.codex/config.toml and claude_desktop_config.json (with 0600 backups).

Desktop workbench for the Honcho memory behind the focused chat: read the newest conclusions, trace their premises, search messages, ask scoped questions, and add confirmed corrections or source files. Uses each profile's existing Honcho provider configuration. Disclosure — talks only to the Honcho server each profile is already configured for, through Hermes's own Honcho client and credentials, and polls it about every 10 seconds for the focused chat while Desktop is open. Ask runs a Honcho reasoning call that may use credits. Add fact/correction and Add to session write to Honcho only after you confirm the target in a dialog; Add to session uploads the text or PDF/JSON/text file you choose. A chat from another local profile is read with that profile's own Honcho configuration, only where this plugin is enabled. It reads the focused chat's title and folder from the profile's session database, read-only. No telemetry.

Desktop-only, read-only monitor for pending memory and skill write approvals. Disclosure — the pane's API reads pending/memory/*.json and pending/skills/*.json under the default Hermes root and every named profile directory beneath it (all profiles, not only the active one), and returns only counts, age buckets, oldest age, and per-item profile/subsystem/id/action/origin/created_at/age_seconds. It never returns or displays summaries, payloads, or record content; it exposes no approve, reject, or delete actions; it registers no tools, hooks, or middleware, performs no network I/O, and holds no credentials.

Detects when a model refuses a request or deflects to an educational alternative, and retries the turn on the next model in your fallback_providers chain; optionally appends your own text to the retry's system prompt after a refusal. Detection is local and rule-based (regex patterns over the response prose); tool-calling responses, code blocks and partial answers are treated as genuine answers. Disclosure — an llm_execution middleware inspects every model response before the agent loop uses it, and when it detects a refusal it sets finish_reason to content_filter (Anthropic: stop_reason to refusal) so Hermes activates its fallback model; this is logged and counted identically to a real provider-signalled refusal (reason=content_policy_blocked), with no way for a plugin to register a distinct reason, so the detection log line carries session/model/provider/api_request_id to let the two be told apart by hand; a triggered fallback resends the full conversation to the fallback provider and spends tokens there; with no fallback provider configured, Hermes replaces the response with its standard safety-refusal notice, so a false positive discards a valid answer. Optional (off by default, empty preprompt/preprompt_escalated settings): an llm_request middleware appends your configured text to the system prompt of requests in an armed session, so a same-route retry of the same model carries it; armed state is memory-only unless persist_state is enabled, in which case session ids/levels/turn ids (never text or credentials) are kept in Hermes's plugin state. No network calls, no files read or written outside the plugin package (and, if persist_state is on, its own plugin-data file), no shell commands, no background processes, no stored credentials, no telemetry sent anywhere.

Deterministic, local-first analysis of your own Apple Health data - weekly trends, rule-based concern checks, nutrition versus Dietary Reference Intakes, an IOM energy target, lab results and opt-in modules (GLP-1 monitoring, medication adherence; all off by default). Portable Agent Plugins v1 package of ten skills that drive the separately installed health-insights command line tool (installed from the plugin's own pinned copy); the plugin itself contains no executable. Works on a self-hosted HealthRelay or Health Bridge receiver database. Disclosure - it handles sensitive health data, so use a local model or one you trust; personal integrations (medication counts, model wording) are off by default. Disclosure — the skills run a separately installed health-insights CLI that reads your HealthRelay or Health Bridge SQLite database read-only and keeps imported lab and ECG results under ~/.local/share/health-insights; the health values it prints are sent to whichever model provider your Hermes session uses.

Dexio shared-wiki memory. Before each turn, the pages of your Dexio wiki that match the user's message; tools to search, read and write the pages your other agents and team also use. Nothing is captured automatically: no transcripts or turn logs. Standard library only; no background threads or local services. Disclosure — with DEXIO_API_KEY set, the first 300 characters of each user message go to the Dexio server (default app.dexio.wiki, or DEXIO_URL) as a search query, tool arguments and the agent's profile name go there on tool calls, and the model is prompted to write, overwrite and edit pages in a wiki shared with the user's team and other agents, without a confirmation step.

DingTalk gateway adapter for Hermes Agent. Connects to DingTalk via the dingtalk-stream SDK (Stream Mode) and relays messages between DingTalk chats and the Hermes agent. Supports text, images, audio, video, rich text, files, group @mention gating, free-response chats, and per-user allowlists.

Direct Mistral Vibe subscription access — browser PKCE login, dedicated credential pool, account-visible catalog discovery, relay-verified reasoning_effort for GLM models. Disclosure — unofficial, not affiliated with Mistral. "hermes auth add mistral-vibe" runs a browser PKCE sign-in against Mistral's Vibe console endpoints (console.mistral.ai/api/vibe/*) and stores the returned API key in the Hermes credential pool (auth.json, slice mistral-vibe), or uses MISTRAL_VIBE_API_KEY. Prompts and model listing go only to api.mistral.ai/v1. Vibe subscription coverage of API use is not guaranteed and may bill as pay-as-you-go. Logout clears the local pool but does not revoke the key remotely.

Disclosure — copies .env key values (and opt-in auth.json backups) between profiles; rewrites other profiles' SOUL, memory and config.yaml. Cross-profile config pane with copy+manifest reconcile and per-group scope.

Disclosure — sends meeting transcripts to Nous inference with your Hermes login (fallback OpenRouter key from ~/.hermes/.env; optional OCTOPUS_DESK_URL); installs a launchd agent that records mic/system audio; writes and deletes under your Obsidian vault; macOS + source install only. Native desktop pane showing the live meeting transcript, answer, and daemon status.

Discord gateway adapter for Hermes Agent. Connects to Discord via the discord.py library and relays messages between Discord guilds/DMs and the Hermes agent. Supports voice mode, slash commands, free-response channels, role-based DM auth, threads, reactions, and channel skill bindings.

Discover and control Govee lights (power, brightness, color, white temperature, scenes) through Govee's developer API. Every command is checked against the model's advertised capabilities and ranges, then confirmed by a state read-back. Disclosure — sends device IDs and control commands to openapi.api.govee.com with your Govee API key; the model can change light state; stores nothing on disk.

Discover learning videos by topic, select numbered recommendations, and turn Bilibili and YouTube videos into transcripts, abstracts, and study notes using the Hermes host model. Disclosure — intercepts gateway messages with a Bilibili/YouTube URL, a "by2kb <topic>" prefix, or (for 1 h after a recommendation list, same user/chat) a bare number reply, and runs the separately installed by2kb CLI (BY2KB_COMMAND or PATH), which searches Bilibili/YouTube, downloads media and runs ASR; enrichment prompts go to your active Hermes model.

Discover priced APIs and pay per request (HTTP 402, x402, MPP) in stablecoins from a wallet on this machine, through the local `pay mcp` stdio server of the official Pay CLI, with the pay workflow skill bundled. Portable Agent Plugins v1 package (mcp.json + skills/), no Python or executables; the user installs the `pay` CLI (brew or npm) and runs `pay setup` first, and the server is offered only while `pay` is on PATH. Disclosure — payments plugin for pay.sh: Hermes starts `pay mcp` as a long-running local process; the curl tool spends the local wallet's stablecoin balance; each payment is confirmed by the user through MCP elicitation (PAY_FORCE_ELICITATION=1, declined when nobody can answer) and the server is marked untrusted; every profile using the plugin shares the same local wallet.

Discover priced APIs and pay per request (HTTP 402, x402, MPP) in stablecoins through the official hosted Pay MCP server (Streamable HTTP at https://connect.pay.sh/mcp, OAuth sign-in, no keys or local wallet), with the pay workflow skill bundled. Portable Agent Plugins v1 package (mcp.json + skills/), no Python or executables. Disclosure — payments plugin for pay.sh: the curl tool spends the hosted Pay account's stablecoin balance; hosted Pay enforces the account's spending limits (none move until the user sets them) and confirms each payment through MCP elicitation, declined when nobody can answer; the plugin marks its server untrusted, but the documented OAuth setup (`hermes mcp add pay`) replaces that entry with a native one that runs at `trust: full` unless the user sets `mcp_servers.pay.trust: untrusted`; chats sharing a Hermes profile share its Pay account; the tool set is served by the remote MCP server at runtime and is not covered by the pinned sha.

Discover, visualize, sanitize/export, and import community agents.md swarm configurations. Outputs abbreviated agent/persona/goal tables, renders ASCII topology diagrams (.svg and .png images + portable 7-bit copy-paste ASCII symbol blocks), generates rich themed swarm illustrations across 12 curated signature themes and orthogonal intensity levels (understated, normal, overstated) via Hermes default model and image_generate, exports sanitized agents.md files, and imports/reverts shared configs with on-screen file preview and best-effort import warnings; every import/revert asks for approval. Disclosure — myswarm_import/myswarm_revert replace the workspace AGENTS.md/agents.md (a file Hermes loads into every session's system prompt) after a Hermes approval prompt; choosing "always" approves all later imports. The import security check is a best-effort regex + model warning, not a security boundary — only import files you trust. Swarm file contents are sent to your configured model for parsing and PII scrubbing (also best-effort; review exports before sharing), and myswarm_visualize_image calls your configured image_generate provider (may cost credits). Adds a ~2.8k-character MySwarm guidance section to every session's system prompt. Writes myswarm-ascii.svg/.png and .md exports into the current folder (exports may overwrite an existing .md file there), plus a .agents.md.myswarm.orig sidecar, and keeps import backups under HERMES_HOME/plugin-data/myswarm/.

Draft enhancement, reusable prompt libraries, undo/redo, and owner-bound full-duplex voice for Hermes Desktop. Disclosure — Derived from hermes-live-voice by Synero (itself derived from hermes-talk) and prompt-enhance by apoapostolov (both MIT; notices preserved). Starting voice captures microphone audio. The Codex-subscription lane spawns the official codex app-server CLI under its own login with a minimal environment; through it the captured profile's SOUL.md (up to 4,000 chars), the list of installed skills and enabled tools, and Hermes task results go to OpenAI. The API lane runs only when COMPOSER_REALTIME_OFFER_URL is set: it posts the SDP offer to that https URL with COMPOSER_OPENAI_API_KEY, or the profile's OPENAI_API_KEY, as a Bearer token (redirects refused). A user-configured wss:// bridge receives microphone audio, chat/profile identifiers and task results. Spoken requests the voice model delegates run as Hermes agent turns with tools in the chat where voice started; runs that need approval are stopped, not approved. Settings and usage totals are stored under HERMES_HOME/plugin-data/enchanted-composer/. No telemetry, no self-updater, no Codex OAuth-file reads.
Draw a shape on a Desktop pad and attach the PNG to the next Hermes chat message. For "what is this shape" when you have no photo.

Drive a live TouchDesigner session through the twozero MCP server (Streamable HTTP on 127.0.0.1:40404), with the touchdesigner-mcp workflow skill bundled. Portable Agent Plugins v1 package (mcp.json + skills/); TouchDesigner itself runs on macOS/Windows.

Drive a real phone from Hermes with one phone_exec tool: an iPhone via iPhone Mirroring on a Mac, an Android over adb, or a cloud phone from Phone Harness Cloud. Disclosure — runs model-written Python on this computer with your user's permissions through the phone-harness package (installed from PyPI); every phone_exec call goes to Hermes's approval prompt unless you opt in to classifier auto-run, a heuristic, bypassable check that decides which scripts ask first; taps and types into your real phone and its apps and accounts; screenshots go to the system temp folder and are attached to the tool result for vision models; a cloud phone streams its screen to Phone Harness Cloud, bills by the minute, and uses phone-harness's own cloud sign-in (~/.config/phone-harness/auth.json); phone-harness's PostHog telemetry (script text, script output, helper arguments) is off under Hermes unless you opt in.

Drive your own Chrome from Hermes through a BrowserPaw MCP server you configure: 16 browserpaw_* tools for navigation, indexed DOM reading, click/fill, batch actions, screenshots and tabs. Disclosure — a thin wrapper over a BrowserPaw MCP server you add yourself (mcp_servers.browserpaw, plus plugins.entries.browserpaw.mcp_allowlist: [browserpaw]); it drives your real Chrome profile (logged-in sessions, cookies) through the separately installed BrowserPaw extension and native host on 127.0.0.1:12306, whose credential lives in ~/.chrome-mcp/bridge-token; the agent can click, fill, submit and read pages without a Hermes approval prompt unless you set trust: untrusted on that server (the README sample enables the full 50-tool profile, including in-page JavaScript, HttpOnly cookie reads and raw CDP, as native Hermes MCP tools); the optional Jev remote mode sends structured page state to TypeSafe AI or a base URL you set, and its local model download contacts hf-mirror.com/aifasthub.com/huggingface.co (probing baidu.com/bilibili.com first).
Dual-panel commander file browser for Hermes Desktop — whitelist-guarded file CRUD, copy/move/symlink, media preview, multi-select, rename, and trash. No network I/O, no model tokens.
DuckDuckGo web search via the ddgs Python package — no API key required. Install with `pip install ddgs`.

Durable local memory for Hermes agents: SQLite FTS5 facts with cited, explainable recall; a Markdown vault with knowledge-graph export and an interactive visual graph; and turn-prefetch context injection with reason tokens. Write policy auto-redacts high-confidence secrets at write time (other PII types are warn-only findings) and stored-content injection screening flags and warns on recall and prefetch payloads (flag-and-warn, fail-open by design, not a blocking filter). Includes a 34-command CLI, destructive-op gates with automatic backups, and an append-only audit log. Disclosure — all memory data (vault markdown, memory.db, index.db, backups) stays local under HERMES_HOME/entropicmem/; a shared publish DB defaults to HERMES_HOME/entropicmem-shared/. The CLI init command appends ENTROPICMEM_* settings to HERMES_HOME/.env (append-only). Vector embeddings are off by default; only with embeddings_enabled: true (provider) or ENTROPICMEM_EMBEDDINGS=1 / query --semantic (CLI) and the optional sentence-transformers extra installed does first use download all-MiniLM-L6-v2 weights from huggingface.co; otherwise the provider has no network egress. The CLI ingest command fetches a user-supplied URL; CLI graph export writes to ./export in the cwd by default and its HTML loads D3/marked from d3js.org and cdn.jsdelivr.net when opened; CLI graph serve starts a loopback HTTP server. entropicmem_patch_core edits the plugin's own Core-memory markdown (Persona/User_Profile), not Hermes core, and is off by default.

Durable memory and context compression for Hermes Agent with local SQLite or flat-file storage. Disclosure — replaces the memory provider (memory.provider: nachos) and, only when context.engine: nachos is set, the context engine; the provider injects a system-prompt block telling the agent to use the nachos_memory_* tools and keep built-in memory disabled; opt-in semantic ranking either runs a separately installed nachos-embeddings CLI or sends the turn query plus memory titles/summaries to api.openai.com with OPENAI_API_KEY; all storage is local under $HERMES_HOME/nachos/.

Durable non-blocking questions with exact answer binding and gateway continuation. Disclosure — its pre_gateway_dispatch hook sees every gateway message and consumes only `dq <id> …` answers from the stored recipient; with `enable_tool` on, the model can send questions to any chat the gateway already authorizes, and a question marked continue_agent resumes that chat's agent with the user's answer; questions and answers are stored unencrypted in $HERMES_HOME/deferred-questions/questions.sqlite3; it calls private gateway and adapter methods, so a Hermes update can break delivery until it is re-pinned.

Durable project ownership and bounded initiative management for Hermes fleets. Disclosure — a `pre_llm_call` hook adds a project's saved rules, decisions and facts to turns of bots assigned to that project; objective checks run allowlisted local programs only at autonomy level 3+ and GitHub objectives shell out to your own `gh api`; it creates and edits Hermes Kanban tasks through Hermes' internal kanban modules (title/body/tenant written directly to kanban.db), keeps its own SQLite DB under `<Hermes home>/plugin-data/hermes-dockyard/`, and its optional HTTP API (`/stewardship/v1`, 127.0.0.1) stays closed until you set a bearer token.

Edit images in a PhotoFresco window you approve: layers, masks, selections, adjustment layers, previews and PNG/PSD export. Portable Agent Plugins v1 package (mcp.json + skills/) with a local stdio MCP server and bundled skill; needs Node.js 22+ and Chrome, Edge or Chromium 120+. Disclosure — opens https://photofresco.com/app/ (remote web editor, live code not covered by this pin) in a separate Chrome/Edge/Chromium profile under ~/.local/share/photofresco-connector (macOS ~/Library/Application Support/PhotoFresco Connector), with cookies/sign-in/autosave kept there; previews and document state the agent requests go to your model provider; with the Send/Spend permissions granted in the PhotoFresco window, AI ops spend PhotoFresco credits up to the budget you set and cloud/feedback ops send document data to PhotoFresco, and Hermes does not prompt before those calls; with Export granted, quick-export ops save to the browser's download folder; no local folders are readable or writable unless you add --read/--write yourself.

Eighteen Hermes Desktop themes in dithered classical marble, one god each: all twelve Olympians plus Hades, Nyx, Helios, Selene and Medusa. Install once, then switch with /skin <name>. Matching terminal skins ship in cli/skins. Disclosure — theme-only desktop plugin: it registers eighteen themes through the plugin SDK, and their stylesheets restyle parts of Desktop's own UI (sidebar art, tabs, composer, wordmark) only while a Pantheon theme is active. It also watches Desktop's active theme: when a terminal skin named pantheon-<god> is active, it switches Desktop to that god's theme through the SDK's requestTheme. The terminal skins are plain YAML files the user copies into the Hermes skins folder by hand; the plugin does not install them or write any files. Fonts and art are bundled; no network requests, no agent tools or hooks.

ElevenLabs sound effects for Hermes: one tool, elevenlabs_sound_effect, that turns a text description ("glass shattering on a tile floor", "90s hip-hop drum loop, 90 BPM") into an audio file, 0.5 to 30 seconds, optionally a seamless loop, and sends it to you in chat. Bundles a sound-design skill with a local ffmpeg script (trim, loudness, mono, loop fixing, game variation packs) and, in Hermes Desktop, an inline sound card and a sound library tab. Model, audio format and endpoint are plugin settings. Disclosure: uses your ElevenLabs API key (ELEVENLABS_API_KEY, the same key as Hermes's ElevenLabs voice; a restricted key needs the Sound Effects permission); every call is a paid generation billed to your ElevenLabs account. Only the sound description and its parameters are sent, to api.elevenlabs.io (or the data-residency endpoint you set). Files are written to cache/generated/audio under the Hermes home and never overwritten. One Python dependency (httpx, already part of Hermes).

Email and calendar through an existing local GigaMail MCP server, with a workflow skill and stdio launcher. Requires Python and a separately configured backend; no automatic backend installation or updates. Reads real mail and attachments; sending, deletion and calendar writes use GigaMail's out-of-band human approval. Disclosure — a thin stdio launcher for the separately installed GigaMail MCP server from Adecubed inc. (gigamail.ai, github.com/adecubed/gigamail, same author as this plugin); the plugin holds no mail logic or credentials and downloads nothing, but it starts that third-party executable from PATH or a configured path, points it at GigaMail's own data directory under your user profile (%APPDATA%\ADE or ~/.ade), and send, delete and calendar writes are gated by that backend's out-of-band approval rather than by Hermes.

Email and chat-message drafts as reviewable cards in the Hermes Desktop chat. The agent's draft_card tool stores each draft and its revisions; the card shows recipients, subject and body, highlights the words each revision changed (removed text on demand), supports inline editing, and offers Copy and Open in Mail. The plugin never sends anything: pressing Send records approval of that exact version and posts it to the chat, then the agent sends it with the user's existing mail or messaging tools and reports the outcome with draft_card_status. Disclosure — stores draft text (recipients, subject, body, versions) in the profile's plugin-data/draft-cards/drafts.db (the 500 most recent drafts are kept); the desktop half appends one scoped stylesheet, removed on disable; no network calls, no credentials, no shell commands, no background processes, no telemetry.

Email for Hermes through Pidgeon: mail to your agent's own address starts a conversation, one per email thread, and the agent's answer goes back as a reply in that thread. The agent reads Pidgeon Firewall's clean text, mail flagged as prompt injection is held before it reaches the agent, mail whose From fails DMARC never reaches it, and the agent can only reply, never write to a new recipient. Standard library only. Disclosure — while the gateway runs it polls pidgeon.ai (or `PIDGEON_BASE_URL`) every five seconds with `PIDGEON_API_KEY` and sends the agent's answers as email replies through Pidgeon; mail from senders in `PIDGEON_ALLOWED_USERS` that passes DMARC becomes agent turns with the agent's full toolset (Firewall-flagged mail is held by default; setting `PIDGEON_ALLOW_UNAUTHENTICATED=true` also admits mail whose From is not authenticated, so anyone who knows an allowed address could instruct the agent), and a cursor/message-id state file is kept under `<HERMES_HOME>/pidgeon/`.

Email for your agents through a self-hosted Agent Mail Gateway: the agent-mail skill teaches reading, searching, replying and forwarding mail, attachments, sending and answering calendar invitations, how to react when the gateway's pre-send review or the operator's policies stop a message, and prompt-injection rules for email content. Portable Agent Plugins v1 package (skills/ only, no code, no mcp.json): you connect the gateway yourself as a remote MCP server in mcp_servers with your own key; the gateway enforces per-mailbox sender/recipient allow lists.
Email gateway adapter for Hermes Agent. Polls an IMAP mailbox for inbound messages and replies over SMTP, relaying email threads to and from the Hermes agent.

EmpirioLabs AI as a Hermes model provider (provider id `empiriolabs`): chat models with tool calling from the live EmpirioLabs AI catalog, each with its context window, image input and reasoning support declared to Hermes, a low-cost auxiliary model picked from the same catalog, and `reasoning_effort` sent only when you choose a level and the model accepts it. Submitted by EmpirioLabs AI. Disclosure — registers one model provider at import and nothing else (no tools, hooks, commands or threads); chat requests (prompts, tool definitions and tool results) go through Hermes' own client to https://api.empiriolabs.ai/v1 (or EMPIRIOLABS_BASE_URL) with EMPIRIOLABS_API_KEY, which Hermes reads, and are billed to that EmpirioLabs AI account; the plugin itself only reads the model catalog (GET /v1/models, kept in memory for an hour), writes no files and starts no processes.

EmpirioLabs AI backends for Hermes' image_generate, video_generate and text_to_speech tools (backend `empiriolabs` for image_gen.provider, video_gen.provider and tts.provider): image generation and editing, text-to-video and image-to-video, and text-to-speech, with models and voices from the live EmpirioLabs AI catalog. Submitted by EmpirioLabs AI. Disclosure: registers three backends and nothing else (no tools, hooks, commands or threads); when one is selected and its tool is called, the prompt, source images or text to speak go to https://api.empiriolabs.ai/v1 (or EMPIRIOLABS_BASE_URL) with EMPIRIOLABS_API_KEY, read through Hermes' secret scope, and each call is billed to that EmpirioLabs AI account with no Hermes approval prompt; it reads the model catalog (GET /v1/models), polls GET /v1/jobs/{id} while a generation runs (videos up to 15 minutes by default), downloads the generated files from the returned URLs into Hermes' cache (the key is never sent to them), and reads a local image file only when the agent asks to edit one.

Encrypted, fully offline memory provider. AEAD-encrypted local vault (vectors included), bundled embedding model, exact hybrid search, no API key and no network at runtime. One vault shared with Claude, Cursor and any other MCP client on the machine. Disclosure — installs the full compartment engine (about 27 Python packages including onnxruntime, tokenizers, mcp and system-tray dependencies) into the Hermes venv; the provider's system prompt instructs the model to store passwords and API keys in the encrypted vault.

Engineering rigor stack: poteto-mode orchestrator with 17 playbooks, plus how, architect, interrogate, swarm, unslop, and 46 other skills and principles. Disclosure — skills only, no tools or network calls of their own; when the user asks, the setup-pstack skill changes Hermes `delegation` model/provider/reasoning settings via `hermes config set`, the autopilot, shipping and babysit playbooks push and force-push the agent's own branches, squash-merge pull requests and arm hourly Hermes cron jobs to watch them, and the reflect skill files backlog issues in your team's tracker without asking per item.

Ephemeral credential paste: request_secret asks through clarify and injects the reply over CDP, never storing it. Disclosure — the reply is typed into the focused field of the page whose origin matches the requested service, over the endpoint from BROWSER_CDP_URL or SECRET_HANDOFF_CDP_URL; the answer is visible in the CLI scrollback or the chat history of the surface that asked, and the value is never written to disk, the tool result, or the session transcript.
Everything Hermes made - cross-session shelf of wrote/patched paths. Full Desktop page, chip, pin. No API keys.

Everything that snagged - cross-session shelf of failed tool calls. Full Desktop page, chip, pin, fix-prompt insert. No API keys. Disclosure — stores failed tool-call metadata (tool, truncated args with key-name redaction, error snippet) locally in plugin-data; no network.
Evidence-based, session-safe skill routing with auditable decisions and opt-in learning
Exa web search and content extraction. Requires EXA_API_KEY — sign up at https://exa.ai.

Exact Western and Vedic astrology through the Astro Agents MCP server (Streamable HTTP at https://astro-agent.dev/mcp, no sign-in, no keys in config): birth chart, transits, synastry, kundli with D1-D60 divisional charts, Vimshottari dashas, doshas, panchang and Gun Milan, computed from the NASA/JPL DE440 ephemeris with no LLM; every result carries a SHA-256 hash. Bundles the astrology skill (when to call which tool, input conventions). Agent Plugins v1 package (plugin.json + mcp.json + skills/), configuration only. Disclosure — hosted-only connector with no local code; every tool call sends the birth date, time and coordinates it is given to astro-agent.dev, and the tool set is served by that server at runtime, not covered by the pinned sha. Each client gets 3 free calls, after which a tool returns REST payment instructions (x402 or MPP); nothing is charged over MCP and the package holds no wallet or key.
Excel-backed hierarchical long-term memory tree (10-row cap per workbook, dynamic branching, leaf pointers). Classifier defaults to the host model; third-party keyless rotation is opt-in.

Experiential Labs - OpenAI-compatible multi-model gateway provider (chat, /model picker, aux and curated fallback models, /usage wallet snapshot). All network calls go to api.experientiallabs.ai - /v1 chat + models via Hermes' own transport, /api/v1/credits and /api/v1/key only when /usage runs; no telemetry; credentials resolve through Hermes routes (hermes auth / .env). Disclosure — When you pick Experiential Labs as your model, every prompt, tool result and attachment of that session goes to api.experientiallabs.ai, a third-party gateway that routes to upstream model vendors. /usage sends your key to its Cost API (GET /credits and /key) or to the cost_api_base you set. Independent integration, not affiliated with Experiential Labs.

Experimental model provider that runs Hermes turns on a Claude Pro/Max subscription through the official Claude Code CLI (the Agent SDK path), so no separate API key or per-token bill. Requires the claude CLI installed and logged in; the plugin checks for it at load, in hermes model, in the pickers and before every request, and refuses cleanly with the install hint when it is missing. Disclosure — every turn is billed against your Claude subscription's Agent SDK allowance, and the provider inherits whatever account claude is logged into.

Experimental model transport using the official Cursor Agent SDK. Requests go to Cursor through its official SDK. The plugin cannot enforce an included-only spending cap and never changes account spending settings. Instructions use a Cursor project rule, not a native system-role override. Permission and prompt-hierarchy equivalence remain unqualified. The plugin spawns Node and a local SDK agent, runs Git initialization in a plugin-owned workspace, and writes project rules, hooks, and SDK state under its own runtime directory. That state may contain private conversation data and currently remains on disk. Credentials come from Hermes's profile-scoped secret accessor. No credential store or vendor token file is read directly by plugin code. Text-only, buffered responses. The bundled model snapshot is not live entitlement discovery. Optional picker hooks require Hermes support. This plugin does not patch the desktop. Disclosure — spawns Node and a local Cursor Agent SDK worker per request (`npm ci` in the plugin dir installs Cursor's official native platform binaries from npm); sends the full conversation, system prompt and tool schemas to Cursor with your CURSOR_API_KEY; Cursor-native shell/file tools are denied by a fail-closed project hook and the run is cancelled if one fires, but that enforcement is not proven in every Cursor runtime; each request's workspace and conversation state stay under the plugin's runtime/ directory until you delete them.
Explicit Jev decision sidekick via TypeSafe or Cloudflare; advisory judgments, no automatic tool gating.

Explicit per-profile readiness and native missing-profile preparation; Python installation remains per profile, never automatic on refresh. Profile model settings, default-on Heavy/Light task routing, fallback controls, runtime limits and Fast inheritance. Reads Hermes profile configuration; explicit saves update selected profiles via the native CLI. Routed jobs launch background Hermes children using the user's configured providers/MCP and store private prompts/results locally. No separate credential store, telemetry, self-updater or approval bypass. Disclosure — after you trust and enable the plugin, routing defaults ON for every installed profile without a saved choice, including profiles that installed an earlier version and never saved one (the update turns it on); existing saved OFF and explicit skill opt-outs remain OFF. On enabled profiles, the model-callable `coding_route` tool starts detached background Hermes agents. They get file, terminal and code-execution tools in any existing folder the model names, run under that profile's credentials and approval policy (single-query mode: dangerous commands are refused unless `approvals.single_query_mode: approve`), and their per-job time limit can be set to none. Prompts and results are stored in `plugin-data/model-router/jobs/`. Saving settings writes model, delegation, auxiliary, fallback and `skills.disabled` keys into the config.yaml of the profiles listed in the preview (backups are taken first) and copies a skill into those profiles' `skills/` folders. The Desktop "prepare profiles" action, after you select profiles and confirm, installs and enables this same catalog pin in up to 32 other local profiles through Hermes's plugin manager, where routing then defaults ON. From install, native subagents inherit the parent session's Fast (priority/ultrafast) tier on first-party OpenAI/Codex routes, which can raise costs.

Extends Hermes Agent API capabilities to deliver a richer chat interface with Talaria WebUI. Disclosure — adds API_SERVER_KEY-authenticated /talaria/v1 routes to the Hermes API server (cross-session history search, rewind/branch/compress of API sessions, runs with the profile's instructions and prefill); stores response metadata (no message bodies) in $HERMES_HOME/talaria/observations.db; relies on private api_server/AIAgent internals behind feature detection.
FAL.ai image generation backend (flux-2-klein, flux-2-pro, nano-banana-2, nano-banana-pro, gpt-image-1.5, recraft-v3, etc.).
FAL.ai video generation backend. Multi-model — Veo 3.1, Kling, Pixverse — covering text-to-video and image-to-video via fal_client's queue API.

FXMacroData macro and FX research: official-source economic releases, indicator history, release calendars, policy rates, yield curves, FX, commodities and COT positioning, with source citations. Native tools for 23 REST operations and 49 hosted MCP tools, plus a /fxmacrodata USD brief command. Disclosure — tool calls send their arguments over HTTPS to api.fxmacrodata.com and mcp.fxmacrodata.com only, with FXMACRODATA_API_KEY in a request header when it is set. The key is optional: without it the data catalogue, the USD release calendar and recent USD releases (15-minute delay) work, and other data answers with a subscribe message. No files written, no shell commands, no background processes, no telemetry. It also adds a short research-guidance section to the system prompt and 72 tools in the fxmacrodata toolset; MCP tool behaviour is served remotely and not covered by the pinned sha.

Fact-checked genealogy instructions for DNA evidence, record searches and proof judgment. Native read-only skill bundle with recipe sources and an offline given-name lookup helper. Disclosure — optional third-party services and commands described by recipes require separately authorized tools and credentials; the adapter itself makes no service calls and registers no tools, hooks or MCP server.
Fail-closed attribution middleware for Sabi's local adaptive routing lane (sabi-code). Adds opaque session/turn headers on loopback only; ignores all other models. Verified on Hermes 0.21.3.

Federated web search backend (provider name `federated`): fans one query out to multiple configured search backends in parallel and returns merged, deduplicated, relevance-ranked results (keyword scoring; optional LLM re-rank with automatic fallback). Phase 2 — official settings-page exposure (config_schema, six keys) merged with the legacy web.federated block, and per-line multi-card credential pools (environment-variable names only) with automatic failover and host-aligned cooldowns. Phase 3 — a desktop card config page (Settings → Plugins; opt-in via Settings → Skills & Tools → Plugins): one card per line, two-level membership checkboxes (backends / credentials), add/remove lines and keys, a per-line Key rotation strategy (pool_strategy), an LLM ranker model picker (seventh schema key `ranker`), and a current-settings string with paste import; no type picker/badges (`type` round-trips verbatim); every edit serializes back to the settings tree (string ↔ UI parity). The LLM re-rank request pins thinking off (`reasoning_effort=off`) and the card page states it. Disclosure — reads the operator's config.yaml (read-only) for its own settings (web.federated and plugins.entries.hermes-federated-search.settings); sends the query to the operator-configured sub-backends (registered providers or custom HTTP endpoints); no telemetry, no subprocesses, no credential storage (key values stay in the runtime environment).

Feishu / Lark OAuth sign-in for the web dashboard, admitted by tenant + open_id allow-list. Registers the `feishu` dashboard auth provider once plugins.entries.dashboard-auth-feishu.settings (app_id, tenant_key, owner_open_ids) and an app secret are configured. Disclosure — calls only the fixed Feishu or Lark authorize, token and user_info endpoints; reads HERMES_DASHBOARD_FEISHU_APP_SECRET or, as a fallback, the Feishu gateway's FEISHU_APP_SECRET, plus HERMES_DASHBOARD_FEISHU_SESSION_KEY; stores tenant, open_id and display name per sign-in in a 0600 SQLite file under plugin-data (no upstream tokens); a refused sign-in logs the tenant_key and open_id Feishu returned (identifiers only, for first-time setup); every admitted identity gets full dashboard access; upstream PKCE is not used (confidential client with single-use cookie-bound state); pending logins are in memory, so one dashboard worker only; WebSockets opened before logout may stay open until the session key is rotated and the dashboard restarted.

Feishu / Lark gateway adapter for Hermes Agent. Connects to Feishu (China) or Lark (International) via the official lark-oapi SDK over WebSocket or webhook and relays messages between Feishu/Lark chats and the Hermes agent. Supports text, images, video, voice, documents, threads, DM pairing, group @mention gating, drive comment events, and meeting invites.

Field notes for a Hermes install: search known pitfalls before debugging and record new ones with root cause; register every local core edit as a patch note with a declarative checks file, then verify read-only after each hermes update (OK / MISSING / UPSTREAMED / N/A / UNKNOWN with reason) and list core files changed outside the registry. Ships 42 pitfalls and 10 patch recipes checked against 0.22.0. Optional pinned Telegram dashboard edited in place by an hourly no_agent cron job. Portable Agent Plugins v1 package (plugin.json + skills/); no tools, hooks, middleware or env vars; never edits the core or runs patch scripts. Disclosure — its scripts only read the Hermes core (pyproject.toml, read-only git status/diff) and never edit it or run patch scripts; the skill does walk the agent through hand-editing core files from its patch recipes and re-running the owner's re-apply scripts, each only after the user says yes. Network: Telegram Bot API only when the dashboard is enabled (reuses the agent's TELEGRAM_BOT_TOKEN from env or ~/.hermes/.env), and the public GitHub API without credentials (latest release plus compare against the installed commit SHA, cached 12 h; upstream.check=false disables). Writes: the notes store (~/.hermes/field-notes), ~/.hermes/field-notes.json, state and lock files in ~/.hermes/cache, a copy of the cron script in ~/.hermes/scripts when install.py runs (the skill runs it on first use), and one hourly no_agent cron job only when the user runs install_cron.py (it reads ~/.hermes/installs/*/facts.json to find Hermes' own Python and re-runs itself with it). Without a dashboard chat, install_cron.py sends the job's alerts to the Telegram home channel when TELEGRAM_HOME_CHANNEL is set (read from env or ~/.hermes/.env), else local.

Find people and coordinate real-world work through the RentAHuman marketplace. Disclosure — runs the third-party `rentahuman-mcp` server via npx, which sends your requests and your RentAHuman API key to rentahuman.ai and stores agent identity keys in `~/.rentahuman-identities/`; its tools can post and fund tasks, accept workers, send messages and release real money to people — write-capable calls ask for approval because the server is marked `trust: untrusted`, but each approval moves money or commits you to work.

Find, search, summarize and save insights for your ParrotNotes in-person meeting notes through the hosted ParrotNotes MCP server (Streamable HTTP, OAuth 2.0 + DCR), with the parrotnotes workflow skill bundled. Portable Agent Plugins v1 package (mcp.json + skills/). Disclosure — hosted-only connector with no local code: every tool call goes to the vendor's remote MCP server at mcp.parrotnotes.app (OAuth via a Supabase auth backend); note titles, transcripts and insights from the user's ParrotNotes account are pulled into the session context, and text the model passes to save_note_insight is written to that account. OAuth must be enabled with `hermes mcp add parrotnotes --url https://mcp.parrotnotes.app/mcp --auth oauth`; the bundled mcp.json alone yields 401.

Fine-tune a small calibrated encoder classifier on Modal and rate it with gonogo. Every GPU launch goes through the human approval gate with the exact config shown; data checks and evaluation run locally for free. Disclosure — thomas_encoder_train spends the user's Modal GPU credits and uploads the chosen training JSONL rows to Modal after the human approval gate; the base model is downloaded from Hugging Face on the Modal side. Training and inference run in a separate Python interpreter the user configures via THOMAS_PYTHON (with the author's thomas package, torch and modal installed); the Hermes venv only gets gonogo-eval. Runs and artifacts are written under HERMES_HOME/thomas/runs; the eval tool writes report files to the path the model supplies.

Firecrawl (https://firecrawl.dev) cloud browser backend. Requires FIRECRAWL_API_KEY. Distinct from the firecrawl WEB search/extract plugin — the two share an API key but operate on different endpoints.
Firecrawl web search + content extraction. Supports keyless cloud, direct API, and Nous-hosted tool-gateway routing for subscribers.

Fleet control for Hermes Desktop: live statusbar chip (N/M IOWAP nodes online), a draggable fleet pane, a full fleet page (status, load, queue depth, capabilities per node, activity) and a tasks page that submits to any task-type capability on the fleet and tracks submitted tasks live (per-stage status dots, result previews, artifacts). Data stays local via the local node-cli against your own IOWAP relay; agent sessions join through an optional iowap-task bridge into a shared track store. Disclosure — the dashboard backend runs the local node-cli (the IOWAP node client from github.com/iowap-org/iowap-node) to read your relay's node list, capabilities and task results, and to submit tasks you start from the Tasks page to nodes on your IOWAP fleet. Relay health also goes through the local node-cli (`server health`) — the plugin itself makes no raw HTTP calls to the relay; node identity comes from the node's own ~/.relay state files. Tracked task ids are stored in your Hermes home under plugin-data/iowap/.
Fleet-wide provider and model presets with CLI and Hermes Desktop support. Disclosure — writes model/provider keys into the config.yaml of the profiles you select (backup taken first).

Flight and hotel search from your own machine through a local MCP server and one skill that tells the agent how to read the results. Portable Agent Plugins v1 package (mcp.json + skills/). No API keys and no account. Disclosure — mcp.json runs `npx -y @viajante/mcp@1.5.2`, which downloads the pinned npm shim and then `uvx` installs the same-version `viajante` package from PyPI on first start, so it needs Node.js, uv and Python 3.10+. Searches read Google Flights and Google Hotels public pages from your IP address (Booking.com and Skiplagged are opt-in). Optional local state (price-history log, cooldown file) is written under the viajante state directory. Nothing is booked and no credentials are stored.

Fluxer gateway adapter for Hermes Agent. Native Fluxer integration using Fluxer's bot REST API for outbound messages, Gateway WebSocket events for inbound dispatches, message edits, agent-requested reactions, pins, reply references, media delivery, and channel-directory enumeration. Component button

For administrators who pin settings through the managed scope: records what each agent role really sends to the provider (model, reasoning effort, service tier, plus the tier the provider says it served) next to the managed-scope state and the effective config (`hermes fleet-policy status --json`); measures cron cost per job — runs, empty runs, $/day, gate present (`crons --cost`); and `watch`, a generic wake gate for cron scripts that replays one read tool on an MCP server and wakes the agent only when new item ids appear (stock `wakeAgent` gate, no LLM call otherwise). Ships two skills (managed-scope admin, recurring tasks).
