Local Presidio-based PII pseudonymization for Hermes model requests and tool results with an encrypted profile-scoped alias vault. Disclosure — PII detection runs locally with Presidio and the spaCy en_core_web_lg model, which you install manually; alias mappings are stored encrypted in the Hermes plugin DB under HERMES_PRIVACY_GATEWAY_KEY; requests are blocked when the engine cannot load; tools outside rehydrate_tool_allowlist receive alias tokens, not plaintext.

Local System One / Laya Typed Decisions control plane for Hermes Agent. Sends bounded turn data to a configurable sidecar for reversible OFF/Shadow/Canary routing decisions, with explicit Canary acknowledgement and fail-open behavior. Disclosure — executes nothing and does not start the sidecar. In Shadow/Canary mode, Search and Model Tier may POST the current task plus bounded recent conversation context; Notification Shadow may POST the completed turn's final assistant response (up to 6000 chars) plus lifecycle metadata. The default sidecar URL is loopback 127.0.0.1:8787 but is user-configurable to any host and no auth header is added. Notification is observation-only: the plugin never sends a push/message/webhook and persists decision metadata, not raw response text. Its only request mutations, in acknowledged Canary mode on the first provider call of a turn, are removing web_search/web_extract tools for audited deterministic no-Web rules and (off by default) lowering reasoning_effort for gemini-3.8-flash-tiered on audited hard-fast rules. The sidecar (same repo, separate pip install, Apple-Silicon MLX/CoreML) is a text classifier that downloads a pinned Hugging Face model.
Local developer tools, transformation recipes, and reviewed chat handoff inside Hermes Desktop.
Local health and daily-context data store for Hermes.

Local ledger of Hermes's approval prompts (dangerous commands, protected writes, MCP consent, smart-mode verdicts): /approval-log shows how often each rule asked, how many prompts were approved, denied or left unanswered, and how long a person took to answer, per rule, per surface or per day, for the last 24 hours, any number of hours or days, the latest session or everything recorded; /approval-log recent lists the newest decisions (ten, or up to 100 with /approval-log recent 50). Disclosure — writes decision metadata (session id, surface, rule label, answer, timings; no command, description or session key) to plugin-data/approval-ledger/approvals.jsonl, trimmed to 5,000 rows past 2 MB; observer only, cannot answer or change an approval; no network

Local ledger of Hermes's auxiliary LLM calls (titling, compression, vision, approval): /aux shows tokens, time and failures per task, model, provider or day, or lists the newest calls (ten, or up to 100 with /aux recent 50), for the last 24 hours, any number of hours or days, the latest session or everything recorded. Disclosure — writes auxiliary-call metadata (ids, models, timings, token counts, no prompt or response text) to plugin-data/aux-ledger/calls.jsonl, trimmed to 5,000 rows past 2 MB; no network

Local ledger of failed provider calls (rate limits, overloads, timeouts, context overflows): /errors shows how many attempts failed per model, provider or cause, how many Hermes could retry, and the most common HTTP status, for the last 24 hours, any number of hours or days, the latest session or everything recorded; /errors days puts one day on each line, newest first; /errors recent lists the newest failures (ten, or up to 100 with /errors recent 50) and how long ago each happened. Disclosure — writes failed-attempt metadata (ids, provider, model, HTTP status, Hermes's failure class, exception class name, timings; no error message, request or prompt text) to plugin-data/error-ledger/errors.jsonl, trimmed to 5,000 rows past 2 MB; no network

Local ledger of the emoji reactions people leave on messages in your Telegram chats with Hermes: /reaction-log counts each message once, with the reactions it has now, and shows per emoji how many messages carry it, in how many chats and how long ago it was last set, or per day with the day's most used emoji, for the last 24 hours, any number of hours or days, or everything recorded; /reaction-log recent lists the newest reaction changes (ten, or up to 100 with /reaction-log recent 50). Only reactions the gateway authorizes reach it. Disclosure — subscribes to gateway_platform_event as an observer only and ignores every event but a reaction change; writes the emoji a message has after the change, a count of custom emoji and 12-digit hashes of the chat and message ids (never a user id, user name or message text) to plugin-data/reaction-ledger/reactions.jsonl, trimmed to 5,000 rows past 2 MB; no network

Local ledger of the messages models write in the middle of a turn, before their final answer (the text that comes with a tool call, which on chat platforms can arrive as messages of their own): /interim-log shows how many each model wrote, in how many turns, how many per such turn, their median length and how long ago the last one was, per model, provider, surface or day, for the last 24 hours, any number of hours or days, the latest session or everything recorded; /interim-log recent lists the newest messages (ten, or up to 100 with /interim-log recent 50). Counted even where display.interim_assistant_messages hides them. Disclosure — writes message metadata (model, provider, surface, step of the turn, length in characters, 12-digit hashes of the session and turn ids; never the message text) to plugin-data/interim-ledger/interim.jsonl, trimmed to 5,000 rows past 2 MB; observer only, cannot delay, change or hide a message; no network

Local ledger of the slash commands you run in Hermes (built-in commands in the CLI, built-in and plugin commands on messaging platforms): /command-log shows how often each command was used, its share, in how many sessions and when last, per command, platform, surface or day, for the last 24 hours, any number of hours or days, the latest session or everything recorded; /command-log recent lists the newest commands (ten, or up to 100 with /command-log recent 50) with the alias typed. Disclosure — writes command metadata (command name, alias typed, surface, platform, a 12-digit hash of the session key; no arguments, session key or user id) to plugin-data/command-ledger/commands.jsonl, trimmed to 5,000 rows past 2 MB; observer only, cannot block or change a command; no network

Local ledger of the times Hermes stopped to wait for you (approval prompts, clarify questions, password prompts): /waits shows how many waits there were, how many were answered or left unanswered, and how long Hermes stood still in total, typically and at most, per kind of prompt, per platform or per day, for the last 24 hours, any number of hours or days, the latest session or everything recorded; /waits recent lists the newest waits (ten, or up to 100 with /waits recent 50). Disclosure — writes wait metadata (session id, platform, kind of prompt, how it ended, wait time; no prompt text, answer or session key) to plugin-data/wait-ledger/waits.jsonl, trimmed to 5,000 rows past 2 MB; observer only, cannot answer, delay or change a prompt; no network

Local ledger of the turns in which the agent changed files with write_file or patch: /edit-log shows how many turns changed files, how many files in all, the median per turn, the most changed file type and how long ago the last one was, per model, platform or day, a table of file types (extensions), or the newest turns, for the last 24 hours, any number of hours or days, the latest session or everything recorded; /edit-log recent lists the newest turns (ten, or up to 100 with /edit-log recent 50). A turn another plugin keeps going is counted once. Disclosure — subscribes to pre_verify as an observer only: always returns nothing, so it never keeps the agent going or changes a turn; writes turn metadata (model, platform, file count, files per extension, a 12-digit hash of the session id; never a path, file name or answer text) to plugin-data/edit-ledger/edits.jsonl, trimmed to 5,000 rows past 2 MB; never opens the changed files; no network

Local ledger of the turns you stopped while Hermes was still working (/stop, or /new and /reset during a running turn, on messaging platforms, the TUI and the desktop app): /stop-log shows how many running turns were stopped, how many by /stop and by /new, in how many sessions and how long ago the last one was, per platform or per day, for the last 24 hours, any number of hours or days, the latest session or everything recorded; /stop-log recent lists the newest stops (ten, or up to 100 with /stop-log recent 50). Disclosure — writes stop metadata (platform, /stop or /new, Hermes's label for the stop, a 12-digit hash of the session key; no session key or chat content) to plugin-data/stop-ledger/stops.jsonl, trimmed to 5,000 rows past 2 MB; observer only, cannot delay or undo a stop; no network

Local ledger of the voice messages and recordings Hermes transcribes (voice messages from messaging platforms, CLI voice mode): /voice-log shows how many recordings there were, how much audio in total and typically, and how long ago the last one was, per speech-to-text provider, model, source, language or day, for the last 24 hours, any number of hours or days or everything recorded; /voice-log recent lists the newest recordings (ten, or up to 100 with /voice-log recent 50). Disclosure — writes recording metadata (source, provider, model, language, file size read from the file system; no audio, file path, prompt or transcript) to plugin-data/voice-ledger/voice.jsonl, trimmed to 5,000 rows past 2 MB; observer only, always returns None so the transcription request is unchanged; no network

Local pixel-art town where every Hermes session is a resident and every tool call walks to a building. Passive lifecycle bridge to a loopback-only server; prompts, arguments, and output never leave the process. Disclosure — version 0.3.0 bundles the Town Node server and a prebuilt browser app inside the plugin directory and adds a hermes town setup/start/status/stop/open command tree. Nothing is downloaded and no npm install runs at any point; node (^20.19 or >=22.12) must already be installed and is launched only by the explicit hermes town start command, bound to 127.0.0.1 only. Runtime state, a 0600 bridge token, a bounded event journal and rotated server logs are written under HERMES_HOME/hermes-town/runtime/. On start the server also reads HERMES_HOME/cron/jobs.json (job id and enabled flag only) to place one resident per enabled scheduled job.

Local prompt library for Hermes Desktop. Save, edit, search, and copy named prompts for manual use, with validated JSON import/export and IndexedDB storage. Does not read or modify composer drafts, send messages, or make network requests.

Local speech-to-text (provider stt_enhance) with faster-whisper or opt-in sherpa-onnx Parakeet V3 and long-audio chunking, plus an optional bounded LLM pass that enhances the transcript using a custom skill, an inline prompt or the default, and keeps the raw transcript on failure. Disclosure — audio is decoded locally. Post-processing is on by default and sends the transcript text to the LLM Hermes routes the stt_enhance auxiliary task to (your main, usually remote, provider unless you point it at a local endpoint or set post_processing.enabled: false). It reads the body of the SKILL.md you configure (never executed) and runs ffmpeg/ffprobe. The opt-in Parakeet backend reads a local model export and, on first use and only when your config.yaml explicitly sets security.allow_lazy_installs: true, installs pinned sherpa-onnx and numpy from PyPI into ~/.hermes/plugin-runtimes/hermes-stt-enhance/ (shared by all profiles). No tools, hooks, background processes, telemetry or stored credentials.

Local video editor for your own footage: 45 FFmpeg tools for the agent (cut, silence removal, 9:16 reframe, captions, music with ducking, loudness, platform export and checks) plus a visual editor in Hermes Desktop with canvas, any number of tracks for text, shapes, video overlays and music, scenes and an English/German help. 100% local, no API key. Licence: PolyForm Noncommercial 1.0.0. Disclosure — the Desktop page starts a local web server on 127.0.0.1 (random port, per-run token) that can read and write media and image files anywhere under your home folder (and any VE_EDITOR_ROOTS); preview caches go to the system temp folder. The agent tools run ffmpeg/ffprobe on the input paths the model passes and write media, image or .srt files at the output paths it passes (replacing an existing file only with overwrite: true).
Local-first Arabic/English intelligent memory with canonical facts, conflict lifecycle, bounded recall, and selective Hermes cloud enrichment.
Local-first LanceDB vector memory with a strict write contract, calibrated abstention, typed relations, conflict tracking and a retrieval-quality gate. Requires local Ollama + nomic-embed-text.

Local-first OpenWhispr dictation history and shared notes for Hermes agents: find what the user said, search notes, transcribe local audio. Free local desktop bridge by default, paid cloud opt-in only. Skill-carrier plugin, no tools or hooks registered. Disclosure — skill only: the agent runs the external OpenWhispr CLI (installed with an unpinned `npm install -g @openwhispr/cli`) through the terminal tool to read your dictation history and notes over the OpenWhispr desktop app's authenticated loopback bridge, and, with your consent each time, to create, update or delete notes, transcriptions and dictionary entries and to transcribe local audio files; OpenWhispr Cloud (api.openwhispr.com, including an email-code sign-in that mints an API key kept in the CLI's own config) is used only when you opt in; the agent never opens credential files itself.

Local-first WeChat relationship memory assistant for macOS: captures only what is visible in the WeChat window via system OCR/Accessibility, stores everything in a local SQLite database (0600/0700 permissions, no cloud), and serves contact briefs, follow-up planning, outreach drafts and weekly relationship reports through 32 MCP tools. Engine pinned to the immutable PyPI release wechat-social-assistant==1.5.1 over uvx stdio; Portable Agent Plugins v1 package (mcp.json + skills/), needs uv on PATH. All data confined to PLUGIN_DATA via WSA_ALLOWED_ROOT + path enforcement. Never reads WeChat databases, never injects into WeChat, never sends messages — outreach is drafts for human review only. Disclosure — reads WeChat only by screenshotting/OCR-ing and walking the macOS Accessibility tree of the frontmost window (not WeChat's databases or a bot API), compiles bundled Swift helpers with swiftc into ~/Library/Caches/wechat-social-assistant/bin on first use, and needs Screen Recording (optionally Accessibility) permission for the host terminal; no network egress, never sends messages.
Local-first diagnostics, safety audit, and incident postmortems for Hermes Agent.

Local-first evidence debugger for failed, stalled or expensive agent runs: import one explicitly selected trace and get a deterministic timeline, observed failure points, ranked hypotheses that cite their evidence, missing-evidence gaps and an inert replay of the recorded run. Disclosure — imports a trace file explicitly named by you or by the model through the rundebug_import tool and writes only under the active profile's plugin-data directory, with redaction before the store, the journal and exports; replay executes nothing (no subprocess, no network connection, no live database); no telemetry, no background capture, no stored credentials, no third-party network calls and no self-updater; the export command is operator-CLI-only and is not exposed through tool, slash or gateway routes.

Local-first long-term memory and memory-aware context compression for Hermes — SQLite, no account, API key or hosted service required. Captures every turn durably, extracts beliefs with provenance, answers from memory (raw-tier fallback and abstention), derives scoped conclusions, and compresses the context window losslessly with a restorable record. Registers the memory-provider AND context-engine slots from one shared core, and ships the Tapestry dashboard. Disclosure — off-host embedding endpoints are refused by default (RFC1918/ULA/CGNAT and https peers); sending memory excerpts off the host requires opting in via embeddings.allow_remote. Disclosure — the git mirror (engine/gitmirror.py) is on by default and writes plaintext JSONL copies of memory into a local git repo at ~/.hermes/commons/db/chronicle/git; it pushes only when git_remote is configured, and its 'encryption' option is a repeating-key XOR obfuscation, not cryptographic encryption.

Local-first long-term memory backed by total-agent-memory (TAM) over MCP — saves each completed turn (with a noise filter; TAM's quality gate applies), recalls relevant memories before each turn within a token budget, and adds tam_recall / tam_save tools; optional TAM team server for shared company memory. Disclosure — local mode starts the separately installed tam binary as a child process per session with an allowlisted environment that carries no credentials: Hermes provider keys (including HF_TOKEN and OLLAMA_API_KEY), TAM_API_TOKEN and any *_TOKEN / *_API_KEY / *_SECRET / *_PASSWORD variable are withheld, and of HF_* / OLLAMA_* only non-secret settings pass (OLLAMA_URL, OLLAMA_EMBED_MODEL, HF_HOME, HF_HUB_OFFLINE); it stores user/assistant turn text plus built-in memory additions (not tool output) in TAM's store, by default outside HERMES_HOME and shared with other agents using TAM; remote mode sends the same text to the user-configured URL with an optional TAM_API_TOKEN bearer token; hermes memory setup tam writes tam.json, TAM_API_TOKEN to .env and memory.provider in config.yaml.

Local-first long-term memory for Hermes, kept on your own computer: recall before each turn, tool-outcome logging, opt-in turn capture, 16 skills and /slm commands. Disclosure — talks only to the `superlocalmemory` MCP server you configure and grant in `plugins.entries.superlocalmemory.mcp_allowlist` (on this computer, or on another one with `connection: remote`): each turn's user message (redacted) is sent for recall and every tool call's arguments and result (redacted, up to 2,000 characters each) are logged to it, and with `capture_turns` on every turn is saved; `/slm` commands run the local `slm` CLI, including ones that change SLM and host settings (`/slm upgrade-hosts --apply` writes the plugin's grant into Hermes config.yaml); `slm_agent` starts a child agent that inherits the parent session's tools.

Local-first memory layer for Hermes Agent — SQLite with vector + FTS5 hybrid recall, episodic consolidation, temporal knowledge graph. Zero cloud. Disclosure — the mnemosyne_remember_media tool refuses local file paths unless MNEMOSYNE_MEDIA_ALLOWED_PATHS is set and sends media only to an operator-configured OpenAI-compatible endpoint when modality_enabled is on; video uses ffmpeg/ffprobe from PATH; the embedding model (BAAI/bge-small-en-v1.5) downloads from Hugging Face on first use.

Local-first persistent memory for coding agents. SQLite on your disk - decisions, preferences, error patterns, and guidelines with project and global scopes and guideline-aware search. No cloud, no API key, nothing leaves the machine.

Local-first persistent memory: store durable facts once and recall them in any session. Portable Agent Plugins v1 package (mcp.json + skills/): the @mem-os/sdk MCP server (pinned 1.6.26) over npx stdio, plus the mem-os-memory skill covering when to store and when to recall. All data stays in a local SQLite database under the user home directory; no cloud, no telemetry, no API keys. Server cwd is ${PLUGIN_DATA} so nothing is written into the install tree. Needs Node.js and npm on PATH.

Local-first personal health records: encrypted on-device Vault (AES-GCM) for vitals, medications, activities, emotions, sleep, encounters, diagnosis mentions, medication plans and reminders, served through a Keychain-paired local daemon with 24 scoped MCP tools. Zero-config first run: the plugin bootstraps Vault + daemon + agent pairing automatically under PLUGIN_DATA. Engine pinned to an immutable PyPI release (healthcare-mcp==0.2.1) over uvx stdio; Portable Agent Plugins v1 package (mcp.json + skills/), macOS only, Python 3.11+. Zero network by default; the optional LLM report-import endpoint stays off unless the user configures it. Approval-gated deletes, tamper-evident audit chain. Disclosure — personal health record-keeping, not medical advice (the skill forbids diagnoses and dosage changes); first run has uvx fetch healthcare-mcp==0.2.1 from PyPI; the optional report-import path posts report images to Alibaba DashScope (qwen-vl-max) unless HEALTHCARE_LLM_ENDPOINT points elsewhere, and only when HEALTHCARE_LLM_API_KEY is set.
Local-first regression workbench turning agent failures and corrections into reviewed, evidence-backed checks.

Local-first, file-native long-term memory with HTTP and embedded ReMe backends. Disclosure — search queries and full user/assistant turns are sent to the configured ReMe endpoint (default http://127.0.0.1:2333; a non-loopback http:// endpoint receives them in plaintext) or handled by the in-process ReMe SDK; no API keys are forwarded.
Local-only YantrikDB dashboard for Hermes Agent memory operations
Local-only content-free usage tally and native Desktop statusline (Windows and macOS beta).
Local-only iMessage platform plugin backed by a launchd-supervised OpenBubbles RustPush sidecar over a same-user Unix socket.
Local-only web dashboard for browsing and visualising Mnemosyne memories, triples, stats, and consolidation history.

Long-term memory for Hermes agents, stored in a local SQLite database. FTS5 full-text search with optional vector (sqlite-vec) recall, importance-weighted decay, a queryable memory graph, and automatic capture: a declarative rule engine classifies corrections, constraints, preferences, decisions, and agent-discovered facts from a conversation and stores each one as a distilled, self-contained fact. Runtime notifications and read-only OpenLTM tool requests are excluded by named guards so ops noise never becomes memory. No cloud, no telemetry, no API keys required; optional semantic recall via a local llama.cpp embedding server. MIT licensed. Disclosure — local SQLite in HERMES_HOME; runs git config to read the repo remote; memory text goes to Gemini or OpenAI embeddings, or to the llama.cpp server URL you set (default 127.0.0.1:8080), only if selected in openltm.json (default local Ollama)

Long-term memory for Hermes, backed by HydraDB. Relevant context is recalled before each turn, and completed turns are saved in the background. Disclosure — when selected as the memory provider, each turn's user message (as the recall query) and every completed user/assistant turn are sent over HTTPS to the HydraDB API (api.hydradb.com, or HYDRADB_BASE_URL) under HYDRADB_API_KEY.

Long-term memory for Hermes. Capture conversations, recall useful facts across sessions and search your knowledge. Choose Quick Local, OpenViking Service (managed cloud) or your own server. Disclosure — conversation turns, tool results and MEMORY.md / USER.md edits are sent to the configured OpenViking server. Quick Local setup installs the newest OpenViking 0.5.x server release from PyPI at setup time (checked against PyPI's hash, not the version reviewed here; re-running setup upgrades it) plus a hash-pinned llama-cpp-python wheel and a local embedding model. It copies the active Hermes static LLM API key into a private file under the profile for extraction, and its localhost server keeps running after Hermes exits and after plugin removal (stop it with `hermes openviking local stop`). Extraction can use a remote LLM. Custom localhost connections can start openviking-server from PATH with the profile environment minus Hermes bot, gateway, GitHub and dashboard secrets; model and tool API keys still pass.

Long-term memory for you and your AI from Membase (membase.com, by Unibase): one memory every connected AI shares. Searches the user's Membase memory before each turn (8 s, fail-open) and adds membase_search, membase_save and membase_profile. Disclosure — user prompts are sent as search queries to the Membase API (api.app.membase.com); with the opt-in capture_turns setting the user's messages are saved there too, and what Hermes' built-in memory records about the user is saved to their Membase profile. MEMBASE_API_KEY comes from the Hermes secret scope; the only local file is $HERMES_HOME/unibaseio-membase.json. No background processes, shell commands or telemetry.

Look a paid x402 or MPP URL up in vet402's public record of real purchases before the agent pays it. BLOCK stops the tool call. ALLOW, and a WARN that only says vet402 has not bought there yet, let it run. Any other WARN, a URL with no record for the paying HTTP method, and a vet402 outage ask for approval, and the call is refused when nobody can answer (yolo, approvals off, cron). vet402 only knows endpoints in public x402 and MPP discovery, so an unlisted URL asks. By default only mpp_fetch is checked, and a payment made inside Hermes HTTPX traffic is not seen. Disclosure — sends each guarded or model-queried URL (scheme, host, port and path; userinfo, query and fragment stripped) and its HTTP method to vet402.com in up to two HTTPS GETs; a missing record or a vet402 outage asks for approval and is refused when nobody can answer, unless VET402_UNKNOWN=allow lets it pay; while enabled, its skill adds one line to the skills index of every session.

Look up current library docs from public npm and PyPI (no API keys). Resolve a package, fetch README and metadata, keep recent lookups on Desktop. Disclosure — HTTPS to registry.npmjs.org, pypi.org and cdn.jsdelivr.net (npm READMEs) only; package name and version leave the machine; recent lookups are stored under $HERMES_HOME/plugin-data/lib-docs; the Desktop pane inserts text through Hermes Desktop's internal hermes:composer-insert event (not a public SDK API).

LoreConvo memory provider: cross-surface persistent session memory with search, recall and structured memory items. Disclosure — stores end-of-session transcripts (truncated, including tool output) and Hermes memory writes in ~/.loreconvo/sessions.db, a store shared across all Hermes profiles and other LoreConvo clients, and injects context from those sessions into each turn; a Pro license enables a one-time Hugging Face embedding-model download; installs the loreconvo package (BUSL-1.1) with lancedb, fastembed and onnxruntime into the Hermes environment.

Lossless memory for long sessions: LCM-X keeps every turn in a local store instead of compacting it away, and the agent can search and expand it. The store is local SQLite (lcm.db) with a recoverable DAG of summaries over it and 15 lcm_* tools for search, recall and expansion. Select it with context.engine: lcm-x. Upgrading from hermes-lcm (breaking in v0.24.0): stop Hermes, then in plugins.enabled replace hermes-lcm with hermes-lcm-x and run exactly one LCM copy (the install script prints the steps; the old engine name lcm still resolves with a deprecation warning); lcm.db and the lcm: config block are unchanged. Summaries use the model Hermes is configured with. Disclosure — optional semantic recall (embeddings_enabled, off by default) sends message text to the embedding provider you configure (Voyage via VOYAGE_API_KEY, an OpenAI-compatible endpoint, or a local Ollama), and once enabled new summaries are embedded automatically in the background; in-process FastEmbed keeps it on the machine after a one-time model download. For known cloud providers the provider-bound copy is privacy-transformed by default (LCM_EMBEDDING_PRIVACY_ENABLED=false opts out), while lcm.db keeps the raw text. Every turn (user, assistant and tool output) is stored in plaintext in lcm.db (secret redaction at rest is opt-in), and oversized tool outputs are by default written as plaintext files under HERMES_HOME/lcm-large-outputs and replaced in the model's context by recoverable references. The engine also reads Hermes' state.db read-only for session lineage, reads private AIAgent attributes via the call stack on Hermes builds without subagent hooks, and runs git on its own install directory for lcm_status/lcm_doctor; tiktoken may fetch its BPE file on first use.

LowRouter as a Hermes model provider (`--provider lowrouter`, or LowRouter in `hermes model`). The picker shows the 180 `auto/` chat models with tool calling and 64K+ context, plus the user's own `alias/` models, instead of all 719 IDs from /v1/models. Context windows come from LowRouter's catalog instead of Hermes' 256K fallback, and /usage shows the credit balance in euros. LowRouter bills in EUR, so the plugin reports no USD cost and Hermes shows it as unknown. Maintained by LowRouter. Disclosure — registers one model provider and nothing else (no tools, hooks, commands or threads). Prompts, tool schemas and LOWROUTER_API_KEY go to https://api.lowrouter.ai/v1 (or the configured model.base_url) through Hermes' client, and LowRouter forwards each request to the host serving the model. The plugin's own requests are GET /v1/models (cached for an hour) and GET /v1/credits on /usage, to the same base URL with the same key, through Hermes' open_credentialed_url. No files read or written, no processes.

MAX messenger gateway with polling/webhook, streaming, interactive questions, native attachments, Core voice transcription, optional PNG tables and a Desktop sessions sidebar. Disclosure — sends the bot token and message/file content to the MAX Bot API (platform-api2.max.ru) and MAX upload hosts (*.max.ru, *.oneme.ru, *.okcdn.ru). Inbound attachments are downloaded only for allowlisted senders, with SSRF protection, and cached under HERMES_HOME. The bundled Russian Trusted Root CA is trusted only by the MAX API/upload clients, not attachment downloads. Its platform hint lets the agent attach local host files to MAX replies via MEDIA paths, and a public output hook adds a filename caption to file-only MAX replies. Webhook mode opens a listener (default 0.0.0.0:8646) that requires a secret and public HTTPS. Polling startup deletes all of the bot's webhook subscriptions. Optional table rendering launches Playwright/Chromium; with MAX_AUTO_INSTALL_PLAYWRIGHT=true it pip-installs playwright==1.62.0 and downloads Chromium (~115 MB). The MAX allowlist does not honour Hermes pairing approvals. No telemetry or self-update.

MIT-licensed product judgment across User, Evidence and Business flows, with one portable Agent Plugins v1 skill and all 91 original skill files. Disclosure: skill instructions run bundled local Python/jsonschema validators and read/write user-controlled local briefs, context packs and review outputs, which can contain personal data. Optional evidence gathering uses explicitly user/host-authorized tools, including external search and connectors; selected claims, queries or evidence go to the chosen services under their policies. There is no publisher-operated receiving endpoint, retention service, telemetry or background process. The bundled jev_gate.py runs offline; connecting a remote decision service needs separate configuration and consent. No MCP server, native plugin entrypoint, registered tools, hooks or middleware.

Make Hermes a team member in an ActVox workspace: on a schedule it works the tasks people assign it and answers the comments that @mention it, and submits each task for a person's review. Skills actvox:actvox and actvox:actvox-inbox, a first-turn inbox line (pre_llm_call), /actvox inbox|status, and hermes actvox setup|install-gate. A cron pre-run gate wakes the agent only when the inbox has work, so an empty tick makes no model call. Disclosure — ActVox is reached only through the user's own actvox MCP server (ctx.call_mcp, needs plugins.entries.actvox.mcp_allowlist) and the user's own actvox CLI (the gate runs `actvox inbox --all --json`); on the first turn of every non-cron session the pre_llm_call hook calls the server's check_inbox (up to 5 s) and adds one line saying how many tasks and mentions wait; the plugin holds and reads no credential and sends no telemetry. `hermes actvox install-gate` writes one file, $HERMES_HOME/scripts/actvox-inbox-gate.py, only on that explicit command and never over a file it did not write; gate state lives in $HERMES_HOME/plugin-data/actvox/. No background work of its own: the cron job runs only after the user creates it, and from then on anyone who can assign Hermes a task or @mention it in your ActVox workspaces decides what an unattended agent run on your host works on, with that job's toolsets (dangerous commands follow approvals.cron_mode, deny by default). Unattended writes need the default trust: full on the actvox server.

Make realistic AI videos of yourself, with your own face and voice, from inside Hermes. Powered by Promoat. Disclosure — sends your scripts, prompts and the public media URLs you supply to Promoat's hosted API (promoat-platform-plugins.vercel.app) with your PROMOAT_KEY; video, character, voice-clone and speech tools spend paid Promoat credits; clone_voice and create_character build a reusable voice or face from the samples you pass; delete_character and delete_voice permanently remove account assets.
Manage SSH connections and remote workspaces in Hermes Desktop.

Manage ads on Google Ads, Meta Ads (Facebook, Instagram), TikTok, LinkedIn, Microsoft, Reddit and X Ads through the hosted AdKit MCP: launch campaigns, ad sets and ads as drafts, pull performance reports with breakdowns, browse competitor ads in the Meta, Google and LinkedIn ad libraries, and generate ad creatives. Built for people who run several ad accounts. Agent Plugins v1 package (plugin.json + mcp.json), configuration only; OAuth uses pinned mcp-remote@0.1.49 over npx stdio, so Node.js 20.18.1+ and npm are required. Disclosure — creates and edits real ad campaigns that spend your ad budgets (creates are drafts until you approve publishing); the package marks the adkit server untrusted, so Hermes asks before every tool the server does not annotate as read-only and refuses them in cron and headless runs. Every tool call goes to mcp.adkit.so; sign-in runs npx mcp-remote@0.1.49 from the npm registry, which stores its OAuth tokens in ~/.mcp-auth. The tool set is served by the remote server at runtime and is not covered by the pinned sha.
Manus-style planning flow — the agent plans in steps and marks them as it works, with a live desktop pane.

Markdown wiki as Hermes long-term memory: plain files you and the agent edit together (Obsidian-compatible, git-versionable), local SQLite FTS5 search with optional qmd hybrid retrieval. Inspired by the Karpathy LLM wiki. Disclosure — reads every Markdown file under the wiki folder you set (wiki_path, outside HERMES_HOME; untrusted_dirs, default raw/, excluded) and injects up to ~1,400 characters of matching excerpts into each turn; the agent appends dated notes only under <wiki>/<memory_dir> (default wiki/memory), and additions to Hermes's built-in memory are mirrored there by default (mirror_builtin_memory), so they land in a folder you may commit or sync; keeps an index at HERMES_HOME/hwiki-index.sqlite and config in HERMES_HOME/hwiki.json, and adds the wiki folder to hermes backup. Cron and subagent runs get read-only recall. No network with the default fts5 backend; the optional qmd backend runs the separately installed qmd CLI (npm @tobilu/qmd, Node ≥22), whose vector modes download local models (~0.3–1.6 GB).

Markdown-first long-term memory shared across your coding agents: a local memtomem MCP server plus six memory skills (index, recall, remember, search, setup, status). Notes live in ~/.memtomem and are searchable from Hermes, Claude Code, Codex CLI and Kimi Code. Runs at user scope. Disclosure — the server is launched with `uvx --python 3.12` and downloaded from PyPI (memtomem[onnx]==0.6.9) on first start, with Python 3.12 if uv cannot find one; it runs as a stdio MCP server for the session and reads the directories you ask it to index. With a fresh BM25-only configuration nothing else leaves the machine; an existing memtomem configuration may enable Hugging Face model downloads, a remote embedding or LLM provider, Cohere reranking or search webhooks. At startup the server also reads the nearest .env found upward from its installed location inside uv's cache (normally ~/.env), setting variables not already present, outside Hermes's MCP environment filtering.

Marketplace-aware LLM routing for Surp — live prices for all models, provider TPS and trusted flags, mid-chat seller switching, secret masking, and approval-gated paid chat. Disclosure — the messages passed to surp_chat and SURP_API_KEY go to the surp.ivc.lol gateway, run by the individual developer ivcained (operator page https://surp.ivc.lol/operator, terms https://surp.ivc.lol/terms; not affiliated with Surplus Intelligence), which forwards them to third-party sellers on the Surplus Intelligence marketplace, including sellers not flagged trusted unless trusted_only is set; paid surp_chat calls spend from the user's prepaid Surp balance (USDC on Base, 5 % gateway markup), each behind a per-model Hermes approval prompt (denied in cron and other unattended runs by default) plus a per-request ceiling (max_spend_usd, default $0.05); the price, provider, quote, combo and cache tools call the same gateway without a key; routing preferences are stored under HERMES_HOME/cache/surp-hermes-x402-llm/.

Matrix gateway adapter for Hermes Agent. Connects to a Matrix homeserver via mautrix (with optional E2EE) and relays messages between Matrix rooms/DMs and the Hermes agent. Supports threads, HTML/markdown rendering, native media uploads, mention gating, free-response rooms, and per-room allowlists.

Mattermost gateway adapter for Hermes Agent. Connects to a self-hosted or cloud Mattermost instance via the v4 REST API + WebSocket event stream and relays messages between Mattermost channels/DMs and the Hermes agent. Supports thread-mode replies, native file uploads, channel-scoped allowlists, and home-channel cron delivery.

Mem0 memory provider — server-side LLM fact extraction with semantic search, automatic deduplication and opt-in reranking, in platform, self-hosted or local OSS mode. Maintained by Mem0; the same provider that shipped in-tree. Disclosure — conversation turns and recall queries go to the configured Mem0 backend (api.mem0.ai in platform mode); at this pin the mem0ai library's anonymous PostHog usage telemetry stays on unless MEM0_TELEMETRY=false is set; `hermes memory setup` can start Docker (pgvector) and Ollama containers for local mode.

Memanto memory agent — typed long-term memory (remember/recall/answer) with auto-recall, turn capture, and RAG answers. Disclosure — each user turn (as a recall query), completed user+assistant turns, Hermes memory writes and memanto_answer questions are sent to Moorcheh cloud (api.moorcheh.ai) under a per-profile agent namespace by default; requires MOORCHEH_API_KEY; settings in $HERMES_HOME/memanto.json.
Memobase memory provider — self-hosted user profile + event timeline recall, with hybrid BM25/vector/entity retrieval and automatic per-turn prefetch.

Memoria Cloud memory provider with scoped recall, explicit memory tools and opt-in background capture. Disclosure — sends recall queries and explicit memory operations to api.thememoria.ai by default (or a configured self-hosted origin). When enabled, auto capture uploads completed user/assistant text for fact extraction, excluding tool results and media. A local SQLite outbox stores pending text; credentials are resolved through the active Hermes profile's MEMORIA_API_KEY secret.

Memory Wiki dashboard tab and opt-in native Desktop page: browsable subject pages and daily logs derived from local session history, plus a read-only Persistent Memory (MEMORY.md / USER.md) audit panel.

Memory from the coding sessions already on this machine — Claude Code, Codex, Cursor, Hermes and the other agents deja reads, including history from before it was installed. No model, no API key, no server. Disclosure — runs the separately installed, unpinned deja binary (brew install deja-vu) as a subprocess; deja reads Claude Code, Codex, Cursor, Hermes and other agents' local transcript files, keeps its index under ~/.cache/deja, and recalled text from those agents is injected into Hermes turns; nothing leaves the machine.

Memory provider that archives the direct user/assistant transcript into a ctx knowledge store before every compaction, deterministically and with no LLM in the path, and hands the resulting block IDs to the compaction summary so the exact wording stays recoverable. Best-effort on any supported Hermes; with compression.checkpoint_required on Hermes 0.21.1+ it uses the fail-closed pre-compress checkpoint contract (#94639) and blocks compaction until the checkpoint is durable. Disclosure — the turns about to be compacted (tool results and system prompts excluded, secrets redacted twice) are written through Hermes' MCP dispatch to the ctx server you configure in mcp_servers; the plugin holds no credentials, makes no other network calls and has no telemetry; it imports the core modules agent.redact, tools.registry and hermes_cli.config.

Meshy AI's own MCP server (pinned @meshy-ai/meshy-mcp-server@0.6.5) for text, image and multi-image to 3D, texturing, remeshing, rigging, animation, concept images and 3D-print prep, with a bundled meshy-3d workflow skill. In Hermes Desktop: inline 3D cards with a download and convert menu, a gallery of recent generations and saved models (with a "Made from" history), image sets, and a credit chip in the status bar. Every credit-spending call goes through Hermes's approval prompt with its estimated cost, and a 200-credit limit per chat makes it ask again. Needs MESHY_API_KEY and Node.js 18+. Disclosure — first start downloads the pinned server from npm through npx; it sends prompts and the images or models you or the agent name to Meshy's API (api.meshy.ai) under your key, gets only MESHY_API_KEY from your profile, and sends no analytics (its User-Agent names Hermes and its version). Downloads go to the plugin's data folder or the folder the agent names (never over an existing file); the Desktop backend fetches only from Meshy's asset hosts. The skill's helper scripts (model stats, preview render, optional Blender hand-off) run locally through the terminal tool.
Meta Model API image generation backend (muse-image). OpenAI-compatible /v1/images/generations. Saves images to $HERMES_HOME/cache/generated/images/.

Meta web search — routes web_search through the server-side web_search tool on Meta's Responses API (Muse Spark); search-only. Disclosure — each search is a separate billed Meta Model API call (per-query web search fee plus tokens) on MODEL_API_KEY.
MetaMask Agent Wallet for Hermes — chat-only setup, reads, and approval-gated transfers/swaps/signatures, a gated Guard Mode policy editor, and a background 2FA watcher. Keys stay in MetaMask.

Meters and a gate for a long-running agent — 25 subsystem state files (energy, fatigue, circadian phase, motivation, novelty, attention, conflict, values, open questions), one folded brain-state.json the rest of the agent reads, four maintenance passes that keep it honest, and a read-only PROCEED / CAUTION / VETO decision gate whose refusals name the numbers behind them. Provides the mind-kit skill, which seeds the files, produces the aggregate, schedules the passes and teaches the gate. Disclosure — portable Agent Plugins v1 package; it registers no hooks, no tools and no middleware, makes no network calls, and reads and writes state files only under the agent directory you choose, where a subsystem that has stopped updating reports stale instead of asserting an old number. No dependencies beyond the Python standard library (two shell scripts for the scheduled passes). Its scripts, when the agent or operator runs them, read and write JSON state under the directory chosen with MIND_AGENT_DIR (default an agent/ folder inside the plugin's own install dir), read HERMES_HOME/cron/executions.db for cron counts, and execute scripts/batch-maintenance.sh or scripts/verify-invariants.py from that agent directory if present; no network egress and no LLM calls.
Metronix memory provider for Hermes with prefetch recall and built-in memory write-through.

Microsoft Teams gateway adapter for Hermes Agent. Connects to Microsoft Teams via the Bot Framework and relays messages between Teams chats (personal DMs, group chats, channel posts) and the Hermes agent. Supports Adaptive Card approval prompts.
Microsoft Teams meeting pipeline plugin with durable runtime state and operator CLI flows for Graph-backed transcript-first meeting summaries.

Microsoft-Decision-1 (Azure AI Foundry System One) decision provider for bounded agent decisions. Registers typed-decision tools (decision_noul, decision_choice, decision_score, decide) that preserve full probability distributions, plus an opt-in pre_tool_call hook that requests human approval for known-risk calls without sending their arguments to Azure. Reference implementation of the typed decision-provider runtime in #113008. Disclosure — the four decision tools send the caller-supplied state/questions text to the Azure Foundry endpoint you set in AZURE_FOUNDRY_BASE_URL (nothing is sent while it is unset); with MS_DECISION_GATE=1 the pre_tool_call gate sends only a coarse operation label for known-risk tool calls to that endpoint and routes them to Hermes's human approval prompt (MS_DECISION_GATE_MODE=block hard-denies instead); the labelled eval corpus under tests/ contains literal destructive commands as should-refuse examples.
MindGraph — semantic graph memory with hybrid retrieval, goal/decision tracking, and cross-document synthesis.

Minecraft gateway adapter for Hermes Agent. Spawns a Mineflayer bot that joins a Minecraft server, wanders around, and relays chat messages between players and the Hermes agent. Supports offline and Microsoft-authenticated accounts.

Mini-Plexamp for Hermes Desktop: statusbar player for your Plex music library — likes synced to Liked Songs, custom playlists with rename/delete, shuffle + repeat, sleep timer, queue editing, OS media keys. Needs only Plex Media Server. Zero API keys, zero model tokens. Disclosure — talks only to the Plex Media Server you configure (default http://127.0.0.1:32400), sending your Plex token in the request URL as Plex requires; the token is stored in Desktop plugin storage, and the optional "Get token…" button reads the Plex `.LocalAdminToken` file you pick. Likes and playlist create/rename/delete write to your Plex server. No agent tools, no telemetry.
MiniMax (Hailuo) video generation -- Hailuo 2.3/02 and S2V-01 models via MiniMax platform. Async task API. Supports text-to-video, image-to-video, and subject-reference-to-video.
MiniMax image generation -- Image-01 models via MiniMax platform. Supports text-to-image and image-to-image with subject reference.
MiniMax web search via the Token Plan API — keyed, no CAPTCHA

Mirrors Hermes Desktop, CLI, TUI and ACP conversations into Discord: one public thread per session in a channel you choose, one post per turn (your message and the reply), so work started on a desktop can be followed from the phone. Posting runs on a background thread and never delays or breaks a turn. Disclosure — register() adds one post_llm_call hook; every turn's text (your message and the final reply, not tool calls or outputs) is sent to the Discord REST API (discord.com) using the bot token you configure, after Hermes's redact_for_egress plus a local token-pattern filter (fail-closed: nothing is sent if the redactor is unavailable); mentions are disabled. The bot token is read only via agent.secret_scope.get_secret (an UnscopedSecretError under multiplexing skips the turn); no external command is ever run. Each turn reads the session's title and source from $HERMES_HOME/state.db read-only; session-to-thread ids are stored (mode 0600) in $HERMES_HOME/state/session-mirror.json. The optional `hermes session-mirror backfill` CLI command reads $HERMES_HOME/state.db read-only and replays past sessions through the same redaction. No other files, telemetry or long-running processes beyond one daemon sender thread.

Mixar's own desktop MCP server over stdio, with a Mixar workflow skill: build and edit 3D scenes, generate models, textures, rigs and animation with AI, render, and export game-ready assets for Unity, Unreal and Godot. Requires Mixar 4.2.1+ on macOS, Windows or Linux, signed in with Connect MCP turned on, on the same computer as Hermes. Disclosure — runs the launcher the installed Mixar app writes at ~/.mixar/connector/mixar-mcp (%USERPROFILE%\.mixar\connector\mixar-mcp.cmd on Windows), which reads Mixar's own files under ~/.mixar/; tools execute arbitrary Python inside Mixar with your privileges; a tool call can start the installed Mixar app, which stays open after Hermes exits; calls go over loopback to Mixar, which forwards them to api.mixar.app under the signed-in account; generation prompts and reference images go to the AI provider running the chosen model; Mixar's backend keeps diagnostic records of MCP tool calls (inputs and results) and deletes them within 30 days; AI generation and create_layered_material spend Mixar credits, declared to Hermes as cost ranges with a 500-credit spend limit per chat; the plugin stores no credentials, ships no binaries, sends no telemetry and never updates itself; the optional MIXAR_MCP_LAUNCHER variable makes it run the program it names; at install Hermes looks for Mixar (macOS: Mixar.app in /Applications and ~/Applications; Windows: the installed-apps entry or %ProgramFiles%\Mixar; Linux: a mixar command on PATH or Mixar's launcher) and refuses the install when it is missing or, on macOS and Windows, older than 4.2.1.

Model leaderboard for Hermes Desktop: a full /model-leaderboard page that ranks any OpenRouter model for a chosen Hermes profile — context window, prices, Artificial Analysis indices and curated SWE-bench Verified / LiveCodeBench — with per-profile criteria, six score views (cards, table, score bars, histograms, heatmap, quality-vs-cost Pareto frontier), an OpenRouter news feed (new models, price changes, promos) and a documented REST surface under /api/plugins/model-leaderboard/. Disclosure — outbound HTTPS to OpenRouter's public model API (catalogue and pricing) on a 60 s poll and a forced refresh every 10 minutes while the page is visible, and to Hugging Face's public model API (safetensors metadata, for parameter counts) on demand and cached; reads the installed Hermes profiles' own config.yaml files once, to seed the tracked list from the models those profiles declare; keeps its state in <hermes home>/plugin-data/model-leaderboard/ (seeded from the JSON shipped with the plugin), which LLM_DASH_DATA / LLM_DASH_CACHE_TTL can move or tune; the optional "Auto-fill criteria" action runs on the host LLM facade (ctx.llm.complete_structured), so it spends the user's configured model tokens; ships one read-only skill (model-leaderboard:refresh-benchmarks) whose only write is a POST to its own /benchmarks route; no API keys of its own, no writes outside its data directory.

Model-aware prompt rewriting with quality scoring, analytics, and coaching. Disclosure — the default auto mode rewrites every user message of 5+ words through your configured model (one extra LLM call per turn) before the agent sees it.
Monitor Hermes token usage, notify at thresholds, and freeze tool/gateway activity at configured limits.
Move data across cloud storage and exchange end-to-end encrypted messages, files and media between agents with Beam Network (Bittensor SN105).

MrScraper page retrieval, Google search, and account usage via direct HTTP APIs. Disclosure — page and search requests can consume paid account tokens; target URLs, search queries, and request options are sent to MrScraper.

Multi-model fusion router for Hermes: detects the model fleet your harnesses (Hermes, Codex, Claude, Grok) actually have installed and builds a Frontier -> Middle Manager -> Frontier routing structure with pinned models and provenance from execution records. `hermes fusion teams|validate|plan|run|index|report|status`.

Multi-provider usage/balance for the Hermes Desktop status bar — shows live usage for OpenCode, OpenRouter, DeepSeek, Kimi, NovitaAI, ZAI, Alibaba, Arcee, plus gateway-native Claude/Codex/Cursor/Nous.

Multi-provider web search, URL extraction, quality reports, and opt-in research mode. Disclosure — reads the operator's HERMES_HOME/config.yaml (read-only) for its own Desktop settings block (country, language, max_results, auto_routing, provider_order, searxng_url, donsetch_bin) and, in its status command, the web backend and keyless_rescue settings, and checks (without opening it) whether a pre-5.1 .env file exists in its plugin folder or HERMES_HOME/plugins, to tell upgraders where their keys went; may spawn an operator-configured local donsetch CLI as a subprocess (argv, no shell).

Multi-repo GitHub issues & PRs in an Orca-style Tasks view for Hermes Desktop. Disclosure — uses your logged-in `gh` CLI and `git` through Hermes Desktop's shell bridge, or a GitHub token you paste in the panel (stored unencrypted in Desktop plugin storage, sent only to api.github.com); scans your configured clone folders for GitHub repos and reads skill names under ~/.hermes; polls the active-session list of every Hermes profile every 10 seconds for status chips; approve, close, reopen, comment and merge act on GitHub from the panel; creates git worktrees and opens Hermes sessions seeded with the issue/PR title and body as fenced untrusted text, and without a shell bridge asks the agent to run the worktree git commands.
Muse Spark in Hermes billed to the Muse Code monthly login (device-code login, no API key).

NATS JetStream event bus: agents publish events (nats_publish), pull one batch (nats_fetch), and wake on subject matches — live-session watches or wake routes (config-declared or runtime-registered via jetstream_wake) with durable consumers, manual ack, an idempotent wake ledger and rate rails; an opt-in lifecycle tap mirrors Hermes events onto hermes.> subjects. Disclosure — connects only to the NATS servers in your own config (no third-party calls, no telemetry); the platform adapter holds persistent subscriptions and reconnect loops for the gateway's lifetime; token/nkey/user-pass secrets come from ${VAR} references read via the profile-scoped secret scope and a configured creds file is read from its path, never written or rotated; wake routes render event payloads into prompts that start gateway turns or fire an existing cron job (optionally under another named profile), the agent itself can add up to 16 durable wake routes with jetstream_wake that persist in plugin data across restarts (subject still limited to subscribe_allowed, no cron-job or cross-profile targets), and jetstream_watch injects matching events into the live session when allow_gateway_injection is on, so keep subscribe_allowed scoped to trusted publishers.

NVIDIA App control through its local MCP server: overlay capture and state, driver status and release notes, game optimization, and app launch. Requires NVIDIA App 11.0 or newer on Windows; the install is refused when the app is absent, and the tools appear while the app's service is running. The plugin reads the endpoint and token NVIDIA App publishes in its own McpServer server.json on every connection, so a changed port or token needs no reconfiguration. Disclosure: the tools read and change NVIDIA App settings on this machine; nothing leaves loopback.

NVIDIA Broadcast control through its local MCP gateway: camera, microphone and speaker effects, Studio Voice profiles, device selection, camera resolution, and effects on local media files. Requires NVIDIA Broadcast 2.3 or newer on Windows (2.2 and older have no gateway); the install is refused when the app is absent, and the tools appear while NVIDIA Broadcast is running in the user's desktop session. Disclosure: the tools change live audio and video effects on this machine; nothing leaves loopback.

Named network exits for the agent's browser: ask it to browse from another country and it switches, then verifies by reading back the address the far end actually saw, never trusting a label. Any VPN, WireGuard config or proxy works as a local exit; gluetun containers are discovered automatically and one can be brought up on demand. VPN credentials never reach the agent, the chat or the model. Disclosure -- a root-owned helper, installed out of band by the user through a narrow exact-path sudoers rule, is the only thing that reads the credentials and writes them to a root-only file (the agent names a country, never the key), and it pulls the gluetun image pinned by digest; the helper manages gluetun Docker containers, bringing exits up and down; the plugin registers a tool_execution middleware that holds browser_* calls when no verified exit is up (the kill switch, and optional cross-provider failover); it verifies exits by calling public IP-geolocation services (ipinfo, ifconfig.co, ip2location, cloudflare); credential entry is CLI-only, with no model tool for it -- `hermes vpn provider <name> --set` (interactive) or `--from-ref`, which resolves a WireGuard config from pass/gopass or a host file host-side and never returns it to the model; opening a .onion needs `hermes vpn allow-onion`, a terminal command a person runs (no model tool) that turns off Hermes's own internal-address check so onion names resolve and restarts Hermes, and the plugin never writes that setting itself; the active profile comes from the plugin context (ctx.profile_name), not a private core import.

Names the one skill from your live roster that fits the turn, before the model call — typed routing via TypeSafe Jev (one choice over the roster plus gate booleans, then a re-read of the shortlist with per-candidate fits), with both thresholds applied in code. Says nothing when nothing fits; opt-in, fail-open, stdlib only, no Node; no redirects, proxy env ignored, payload capped. Disclosure — on eligible turns it sends your message (up to 4,000 chars) plus skill names and short SKILL.md excerpts from your local roster to TypeSafe, OpenRouter, or your configured gateway, using your key. With backend auto an OpenRouter key is used automatically when no TypeSafe key is set, and the OpenRouter route also reads Hermes' OpenRouter credential pool (auth.json) when OPENROUTER_API_KEY is absent, rotating that pool's entries through the core pool API.

Native Anatomy community gallery with search, local favorites and explicit sandboxed standalone playback. Disclosure — when opened it fetches gallery metadata and thumbnails from a third-party GitHub repository (wheresryan22/anatomy-community, resolved at runtime from its mutable previews branch via api.github.com and raw.githubusercontent.com). "Open figure in Hermes" downloads that community figure's HTML and runs its JavaScript inside the Desktop SDK sandbox (opaque origin, scripts only), and "Browse Ryan's website" embeds skills.wheresryan.sh the same way. Favorites and filters stay in Desktop-local plugin storage; no credentials or Hermes data are sent.

Native BYOK Soniox text-to-speech and asynchronous speech-to-text providers with configurable languages and voices, automatic STT language detection, and Hermes voice-bubble support. Disclosure — TTS sends reply text and synthesis settings to tts-rt.soniox.com; STT uploads audio, optional language hints, and optional prompt context to api.soniox.com, then best-effort deletes the remote transcription and uploaded file. SONIOX_API_KEY is resolved through Hermes' active-profile secret scope. No telemetry, shell commands, background processes, or stored credentials.

Native Beads (bd) work-graph plugin: fixed-argv adapter, scoped ready frontier, claim with read-back, guarded writes. Six tools over an explicit store path + actor; honest exit-code map incl. stale-13; plain bd stays fully sufficient (escape hatch). No desktop pane ships yet.

Native Discord Rich Presence (RPC) integration for Hermes Agent — real-time session, model, token, and tool tracking with local-only IPC. Disclosure — publishes your most recent session title (or, in full title mode, the workspace folder name), model name and token total to the local Discord client as Rich Presence every 3 s (visible to other Discord users); opt-in settings also publish the git branch and a "View Repository" button with the public github.com/gitlab.com remote URL (credentials, ports and other hosts stripped); reads ~/.hermes/state.db read-only; reads the active workspace's .git/HEAD and .git/config read-only to resolve repository and branch; on Linux may scan running Discord processes' environment via psutil to find XDG_RUNTIME_DIR; writes a small presence-ownership file in XDG_RUNTIME_DIR (or the system temp dir) and, under herdr, queries the local HERDR_SOCKET_PATH socket for pane focus.

Native Hermes Agent plugin that runs the local Atoll notch monitor for Hermes session and turn status on macOS. Disclosure — macOS only. Starts a detached Node daemon on every Hermes session that reads state.db read-only and sends session titles, model/profile/token stats and a ≤96-char redacted preview of your latest request to the third-party Atoll notch app over localhost. hermes notch setup clones and builds the author's Atoll fork (github.com/himanusia/Atoll at a pinned commit, not reviewed here) with Xcode and installs an unnotarized app to ~/Applications. Node deps install via Hermes's npm ci prompt. Run hermes notch stop before removing.

Native Hermes port of Claude SEO 2.4.2: 45 SEO workflow and specialist skills, a credential-scoped hermes_seo_run tool, an isolated Python runtime, and advisory JSON-LD feedback. Derived from Claude SEO 2.4.2 (MIT; FLOW prompt materials CC BY 4.0). Disclosure — derived from Claude SEO 2.4.2 (MIT; FLOW prompt materials CC BY 4.0); the hermes_seo_run tool starts local subprocesses in the Hermes host process, not a Docker terminal sandbox, and model-supplied script arguments may name host paths, so it can read host files (the Gemini image-edit utility uploads the named file to Google, the IndexNow utility reads a URL-list file); `hermes seo setup` downloads Python packages from PyPI within version ranges into a private environment and optionally Chromium through Playwright; audits fetch user-selected websites; separately configured providers (Moz, Bing Webmaster, Keywords Everywhere, Google APIs, Matomo, DataForSEO, IndexNow, Google Gemini) receive the data sent to them and may incur charges; skills ask before paid or mutating calls but the tool does not enforce approvals; Gemini images are saved to ~/Documents/nanobanana_generated, and other runtime state stays in Hermes plugin data storage; provider keys are read from the active Hermes profile and passed only to the script that needs them; Google OAuth workflows are disabled; no telemetry, bundled credentials, background process or self-updater.
Native Hermes tools for a configurable local capability index: search/get/neighbors plus local usage feedback/reporting.

Native Kiro model provider over HTTPS with AWS Builder ID / IAM Identity Center device login. Disclosure — dynamically registers an AWS OIDC public client named `hermes-kiro` during login and stores OAuth grants in Hermes' profile-scoped auth.json credential pool.

Native TTS Buddy speech provider using the existing TTS Buddy CLI, with offline voice selection, MP3 generation, Hermes voice-message conversion and exact-job recovery, plus terminal-only account deletion through CLI 0.16.0+. Disclosure — runs the user-installed `ttsbuddy` CLI (argument array, speech text on stdin), which sends the text and voice settings to TTS Buddy, downloads the hosted audio and uses the account's quota. Credentials come from the profile's `TTSBUDDY_API_KEY` secret or, when the user selects `cli_config_dir`, from that CLI profile's own saved login, which the CLI may read and update. The model-callable `ttsbuddy_recover` tool downloads an existing job to a new MP3 path the model chooses (never overwrites). The terminal command `hermes ttsbuddy account delete` can permanently delete the TTS Buddy account, its hosted files and identity, and cancel subscriptions, after `--yes` and a fresh email code entered at a hidden prompt or protected stdin.

Native XMemo memory provider for Hermes Agent — durable, identity-aware cross-session memory with semantic search. Disclosure — cloud memory provider: sends each user prompt (for recall and the search tools), model-written memories and mirrored built-in Hermes memory writes, plus a stable install ID, to xmemo.dev (Yonro Co., Ltd.); keeps a local SQLite cache of recalled results and a queue of unsent writes in $HERMES_HOME/xmemo_cache.db, partitioned by a hashed account identity; reads the key from XMEMO_KEY (also MEMORY_OS_API_KEY / MEMORY_OS_MCP_TOKEN) and, if none is set, falls back to the xmemo login token in ~/.config/xmemo/credentials.json (a catalog rule 11 deviation kept for existing users); workflow and destructive tools and timeline capture are off by default and opt-in.

Nerve is a supervisory nervous system for Hermes Agent with provider-neutral Jev, Laya, and OpenJev Reflex backends, evidence-backed Kanban supervision, context governance, token-budget trajectory control, and durable SSH workers. Disclosure — the default Reflex backend is hosted Jev; with the default settings (enabled / admission_enabled on) each turn's user prompt (up to 12k characters) and redacted tool/result previews are sent to the configured Jev provider (OpenRouter Decisions / TypeSafe Jev) using your OPENROUTER_API_KEY or TYPESAFE_API_KEY, spending your credits on every turn. Laya and OpenJev can be configured as local/self-hosted backends. The operator-only nerve setup CLI can copy a local HermesContextBus checkout into HERMES_HOME/plugins/hermes-context-bus and runs hermes plugins enable/disable for that plugin when a profile is saved; the model cannot trigger this.
NetBox change management: query DCIM/IPAM objects, build a reviewed field-level diff, apply with a journal and roll back.

NetMind OpenAI-compatible model provider with a bundled model catalog. Disclosure — registers one model provider at import and nothing else (no tools, hooks, commands or threads); chat requests go to https://api.netmind.ai/inference-api/v1 through Hermes' own client with NETMIND_API_KEY, which Hermes reads; the plugin itself opens no connections, reads and writes no files and starts no processes.

Next-step suggestions under the Hermes Desktop composer after each turn: local Ollama inference, per-session state, target routing (session, new tab, bots, kanban), tiny-model capacity profiles, EN/DE UI. No API keys. Disclosure — after every agent turn, sends the last 8 messages (each cut to 200 chars) plus the working directory to Ollama on localhost; clicking a suggestion immediately submits it as a prompt in the current session, a new session, or another profile's session, or creates a kanban card, and for non-current targets also attaches the working directory and the last 6 messages (on by default, can be turned off under Targets).

Nextcloud Talk platform adapter for Hermes Agent, in two modes behind one plugin: a webhook bot (Nextcloud Talk Bot API, HMAC-SHA256 signed, with an explicit body-size cap and a nonce-replay cache ahead of payload parsing) and a real Nextcloud user account (app password, long-polling the Chat REST API, with federation-invite support, per-room mention/watch/free modes, and an agent-to-agent loop guard plus active-listening context for multi-agent rooms). Mode is picked automatically by which credential is configured. No extra SDKs -- aiohttp for bot mode, httpx for user mode, both already Hermes dependencies. Disclosure — Connects to your Nextcloud server either as a Talk bot (HMAC-verified webhook listener, 127.0.0.1:18797 by default) or as a real Nextcloud user with an app password (long-polls the Chat API and auto-accepts federation invites only from NEXTCLOUD_TALK_ALLOWED_INVITERS); in user mode, unanswered room messages from allowed senders (up to 40 per room by default) and, for rooms listed in NEXTCLOUD_TALK_ROOM_MODES or with room_rules_all_rooms on, the room description are added to the agent's next turn in that room.

Nine AI provider balances in one desktop widget — live balance/usage and quota reads, token-based spend estimates with off-peak price windows, drop alerts, and an anime mascot per provider with rotating flavour lines (DeepSeek, MiniMax, GLM, Kimi, MiMo, ChatGPT, Claude, Gemini, Grok). Fully English UI. Desktop-only: desktop/plugin.js inside the plugin SDK surface; no agent tools, hooks, middleware or env vars. Keys are entered in the widget's settings page and stored in plugin-scoped storage; the widget only calls those providers' official APIs. Ported from MeteorNOX/DeepSeek-Balance-Whale-Widget (MIT). Disclosure — API keys you enter in the widget's settings are stored in plaintext in Desktop plugin storage (not Hermes' secret store); while the widget is on, the Desktop renderer polls the balance/usage endpoint of the provider matching your current model every 60 s with that provider's key (api.deepseek.com, api.minimaxi.com / api.minimax.io, open.bigmodel.cn / api.z.ai, api.moonshot.cn / api.moonshot.ai, api.kimi.com, token-plan-cn.xiaomimimo.com, api.openai.com, api.anthropic.com, generativelanguage.googleapis.com with the key in the URL, api.x.ai); each key goes only to its own provider; draws a floating widget over the app window.

No-Limit Texas Hold 'Em for Hermes Desktop: play with three isolated Hermes profile agents using play chips only. Agent decisions use configured models and may consume provider tokens; this is a local game, not gambling software. Disclosure — each opponent is a zero-tool Hermes agent run in-process under the local Hermes profile you select for it, using that profile's configured provider credentials and spending its tokens; reads every local profile's name, model and avatar for the picker; stores the table (including hole cards) in plugin-data/agent-hold-em/table.json.
Notes, checklists and documents beside Hermes that your agent can read and update safely, with revision checks and undo for AI edits.
Nous Portal usage widget for the Hermes desktop statusbar — remaining credits plus plan-usage percentage, with portal detail on hover.

OKLCH accent colour picker for the Hermes Desktop status bar: drag it and the whole theme retints live, with palette commands to reset to the theme default or copy the current colour. A theme-authoring tool; the colour is scratch state and is never persisted. Desktop-only (desktop/plugin.js inside the plugin SDK surface); no agent tools, hooks, middleware or env vars.

Observability + budget guardrails for Hermes Agent — tokens, cost, latency, tool calls per session and cron job. Persists to local SQLite. Exposes /stats and /budget slash commands. Disclosure — records per-session tokens, cost, latency, tool names and sender/profile ids (no message text) in ~/.hermes/telemetry/telemetry.db; fetches public model pricing from openrouter.ai/api/v1/models on first load and at most once a day; in the default enforce mode first load writes a $5/day, $100/month global budget to telemetry/budget.yaml, and a hard breach blocks every tool call and pauses the over-budget cron job until the window resets (set plugins.entries.hermes-telemetry.settings.mode: observe to record without enforcing); the optional standalone dashboard server binds 127.0.0.1 with no auth.

Observe-with-approval Telegram Business Mode (secretary bot): Hermes drafts replies to your customers' messages and DMs each draft to you with Send, Edit and Discard buttons; nothing reaches a customer until you tap Send. A Hermes Labs plugin: built by Nous Research, not supported. Disclosure — each customer message is sent to your active Hermes model to draft the reply, and drafts and connection records are stored locally in <HERMES_HOME>/telegram-business/state.db.
Octen web search with query-focused highlights and page extraction.

Official Blender Lab MCP server over stdio, pinned to upstream v1.0.3, with a Blender workflow skill. Needs Git and uv; Blender 5.1+ is not needed at install. The skill opens Blender itself when a task needs it and, after you agree, installs Blender and Blender Lab's MCP add-on. First startup downloads Python dependencies; prepare the uv environment before connecting. Disclosure — tools execute arbitrary Python in Blender with your privileges; the skill starts Blender with online access for that session only (your saved preference is unchanged), and the add-on's local server on port 9876 has no password, so any program on this computer can use it while Blender is open; only after you agree does the skill download Blender from download.blender.org (about 400 MB, about 1.5 GB unpacked), check it against blender.org's sha256 list and install it in your own folder without administrator rights (Linux ~/.local/opt, macOS ~/Applications, Windows %LOCALAPPDATA%\Programs\Blender Foundation; never over an existing Blender), and download the v1.0.3 add-on, check its hash and install or enable it; first start downloads the pinned Blender Lab MCP server and its Python dependencies with uv. Server discovery does not prove scene readiness.

Official Hermes Agent integration for Frihet — discoverability, setup, diagnostics, and operating guidance for the Frihet MCP. Zero duplicated tools; the canonical Frihet MCP surface stays in @frihet/mcp-server and the remote endpoint https://mcp.frihet.io/mcp. Disclosure — /frihet setup and /frihet doctor send an unauthenticated MCP initialize to mcp.frihet.io (or FRIHET_MCP_URL); /frihet doctor also makes one read-only list_invoices call through Hermes's MCP client once you grant plugins.entries.frihet.mcp_allowlist; reads ~/.hermes/config.yaml only to check that an mcp_servers.frihet block exists; the pre_tool_call hook prompts before Frihet MCP calls it classifies as irreversible or unknown, but reads and draft-first creates pass without a prompt unless the server sets trust: untrusted.

Offline conversation customization with one-click presets and plugin-owned settings. Disclosure — enabled by default; injects a stylesheet that restyles the Desktop chat transcript (width, fonts, spacing, optional colours) keyed on app data-slot selectors, so a Desktop update can break the styling; settings stay in plugin storage, no network.

Offline scam gate. Blocks known-bad links and payments before a tool runs, and asks a human when it cannot see the destination. Disclosure — blocks agent tool calls that would edit Hermes config/profiles/plugins/hooks or turn approvals off, and with approvals off turns its "ask" into a block (setting when_approvals_off: allow restores asks); keeps its signing key and ask log under ~/.local/state/scamgate and phishing feeds under ~/.cache/scamgate (not per-profile); feeds download only when you run `scamgate update-feeds` (openphish.com, Phishing-Database on GitHub, optional urlhaus); optional SCAMGATE_RDAP=live sends each checked link's domain to its RDAP registry.

Oh My Hermes (OMH) bridge: routing hints and role context for OMH workflow skills, per-task delegation model routing, plan todos and a status tool, a Hermes Desktop status pane (off until enabled), bounded evidence probes that keep prepared work apart from observed results, and a file-backed memory provider. Disclosure — omh_delegate_route writes delegation.model/provider/reasoning_effort in $HERMES_HOME/config.yaml and the session hooks restore them; omh_gather_evidence runs allowlisted checks (python -m unittest with reporting flags only, python -m compileall, git diff --check, omh doctor/probe/docs/release checks) via subprocess on the host, outside any sandboxed terminal backend and without Hermes' terminal approval, in the agent working directory or below it, so it runs whatever test code that directory holds; omh_team (only with the separate OMH core package installed) asks once through the Hermes approval prompt for an exact list of up to 8 check commands from an accepted plan, then runs them on the host as each helper returns; omh_jev_ask posts model-supplied state and questions to api.typesafe.ai (openrouter.ai only when the operator opts in via ~/.omh/jev/settings.json) with the user's own TYPESAFE_API_KEY or OPENROUTER_API_KEY, only in a turn where the user names Jev; opt-in egress_attempts (re-registers chosen core tools, needs the operator's tool-override grant) and browser_adapter (vetoes core browser_* tools) settings; reads session and cost metadata from state.db read-only; state lives under ~/.omh and <project>/.omh.
Ollama Cloud web search + content extraction via Ollama's native REST API. Search returns web results; extract fetches page content. Reuses OLLAMA_API_KEY (https://ollama.com/settings/keys).
OmniVoice TTS provider for Hermes Agent

One /crew message becomes verified work on the kanban board. A coordinator owns every card until its proof command exits 0 - one writer per card, an independent verifier, a hard token budget per card, and a live local dashboard of every card, run and tool call. Disclosure — install.py creates four crew-* profiles cloned from your chat profile (including its .env provider keys and memories), deletes non-crew skills in them, updates crew in other profiles and on Linux starts a loopback dashboard service (127.0.0.1:8799, transcript excerpts; --publish serves it to one tailnet login), restarting it when an upgrade changes the plugin code; it never approves shell hooks itself, but on a terminal offers (y/N) to open each profile's Hermes so Hermes asks for hook consent, first revoking approvals whose hook script changed; on native Windows the service and the optional nightly cron are skipped and the dashboard is started by hand, and proofs run in Git for Windows's bash; a Crew tab in the Hermes dashboard and a native Crew page in Hermes Desktop build that board inside the Hermes backend, including its transcript excerpts, each live card's step count and last tool name, and its acknowledge, Unstuck, Retry, Proof and Stop actions, under /api/plugins/crew/ to anyone with dashboard access; a detached coordinator makes read-only model decisions and runs card proof commands unattended with a scrubbed env, flagged or changed proofs only after the owner answers /crew-proof; card reports and questions are sent to the originating chat via hermes send; agent-written per-role lessons are injected into later crew turns.

One install: the Desktop model picker and the OR Picker composer provider. Checking a model here is what the composer lists. Disclosure — the optional OpenRouter management key is stored in plaintext in Desktop localStorage; the plugin reads OPENROUTER_API_KEY from your environment, Hermes secret store or HERMES_HOME/.env and sends it only to openrouter.ai (credits, usage, and the Test-model button, which spends credits).

One managed home for agent drafts: a per-session scratchpad of named buffers the agent edits in place instead of writing a new temp file per revision.
