Buffers live under plugin-data/devkit/, open in the Desktop code viewer, are promoted to real files only through write_file, and are removed when their chat is deleted. A Scratchpad tab beside Files groups chats by date like the chat sidebar; click a chat to open it, click a file to view or edit it in a workspace tab, and delete or clear drafts. Disclosure — adds a short placement rule (about 120 tokens) to each turn's user message; reads state.db read-only once an hour from a background thread to find deleted chats, and also removes folders idle longer than idle_days (default 90) using its own stamps; deletes only its own folders under plugin-data/devkit/; no network calls, credentials or third-party services.

One time zone in your Hermes Desktop status bar, every other zone you work with a click away. Click the time for a drop-up of your enabled zones; Edit zones lists standard IANA zones with live UTC offsets. Desktop-only (desktop/plugin.js inside the plugin SDK surface); no network, agent tools, hooks, middleware or env vars.

One titlebar button, next to HUD mode, that opens and hides the built-in browser: the same action as Ctrl+Shift+L. Label follows the active UI language. Front-end only: no agent calls, no network, no API keys. Disclosure — works by pressing the browser shortcut (Ctrl/⌘+Shift+L); breaks if the user rebinds it.

One-click access to the Hermes Web Dashboard (127.0.0.1:9119) from the Desktop app — sidebar row, in-app page that loads itself when the server comes up, and a status-bar chip with a live dot. Front-end only: no agent calls, no tokens, no API keys.

One-use HTTPS forms for missing environment secrets, native encrypted Browser Vault logins/TOTP setup keys and payment cards, protected hosted payment-field filling, nested HTTPS verification codes/passcodes, and approved secret operations outside chat and LLM input. Disclosure — /senv setup supplies a skill using sudo for host packages and TLS setup after approval; the TLS listener binds all interfaces by default; pre_gateway_dispatch observes gateway messages to bind commands to their sender. In interactive Telegram sessions, secure_env_vault saves logins or fills a code field through the captured browser supervisor without explicitly submitting the site form. Explicit parent payment/nested-code targeting requires compatible host task/profile ownership and browser-generation evidence and fails closed without it; this is not a general fix for native Vault named-tab selection. Payment filling requires separate native consent and exact document/control guards; explicit resume requires existing nonempty values to match Vault. Site input callbacks, especially 3-D Secure, may authorize or auto-submit an operation. Unknown outcomes require external verification before retry. secure_operation executes administrator-allowlisted, SHA-256-pinned external Python consumers with gateway privileges; consumers are trusted, not sandboxed, and none are enabled by default. Secret input is not persisted by this mode; consumers must enforce their own handling policy. Links are bearer authorization, not submitter identity; cancellation cannot stop an already-running consumer.

Open your signed-in YouTube Home recommendations and Shorts in the existing Hermes Desktop Browser beside your conversation, without pasting video URLs or launching an external browser. Desktop-only SDK launcher; no agent tools, hooks, middleware or API keys. Disclosure — explicit user clicks load YouTube and its normal service/CDN requests in the native Browser; this plugin does not read credentials, cookies, recommendations or watch history. No telemetry, shell commands, backend service or self-updater. Uses the native preview toggle (Hide for an already-open destination), not a dedicated PIP player.

Open-source marketing toolkit for agencies and in-house teams, one listing with three skill groups and 207 skills registered as Hermes skills: Digital Marketing Pro (strategy, SEO/AEO/GEO, paid media, CRM, analytics; 164 skills), ContentForge (fact-checked long-form content with a run auditor; 22 skills) and SocialForge (a content calendar to images, carousels, video and copy; 21 skills). Skills only: no tools, hooks or background processes. Disclosure — Skills only (no tools, hooks or MCP servers). The optional scripts the skills run call third-party APIs (ad, CRM, e-mail, Slack, LLM and image/video providers) only when run, using the user's own keys from environment variables. Live writes need the user's typed yes. For writes the plugin sends itself, the script creates a single-use approval record when it prepares the write, and the agent approves that record after the yes, so Hermes does not prompt before those script runs. Writes through MCP tools rely on the typed yes alone. Paid image and video generation is quoted first. refresh_models.py reads your Anthropic, OpenAI, Gemini and (strategy group) Evolink keys. Keys and data live outside the Hermes profile: SocialForge stores API keys in plain text, plus a copy of any Google service-account file, in ~/socialforge-workspace; brand data goes to ~/.claude-marketing; deliverables are copied to ~/Documents/DigitalMarketingPro and ~/Documents/ContentForge. Nothing installs unless the user says yes; installs are exact-pinned pip packages into the Python that runs the script, plus Playwright's Chromium download. See the README and each group's PRIVACY.md.
OpenAI image generation backed by ChatGPT/Codex OAuth (gpt-image-2 via the native Codex images/generations and images/edits endpoints). Saves generated images to $HERMES_HOME/cache/generated/images/.
OpenAI image generation backend (GPT Image 2 and GPT Image 2.5 Flare/Sunburst). Saves generated images to $HERMES_HOME/cache/generated/images/.

OpenAI native web search — declares the Responses API server-side ``web_search`` built-in instead of running a client-side search. Requires the Codex Responses transport plus openai-codex OAuth (``hermes auth add openai-codex``).

OpenClawCash managed EVM and Solana wallets for AI agents — thin bridge to the OpenClawCash agent API. Disclosure — payments plugin for the OpenClawCash custodial wallet service (openclawcash.com); the model can create wallets and send EVM/Solana transfers from wallets reachable by OPENCLAWCASH_AGENT_KEY with no Hermes confirmation prompt; tool arguments go to openclawcash.com, and wallet_create also sends OPENCLAWCASH_EXPORT_PASSPHRASE to that API.

OpenPaths model provider for Hermes: OpenAI-compatible inference at openpaths.io with auto, auto-easy-task, auto-medium-task, auto-hard-task and auto-think task-tier routes plus GPT, Claude, Gemini and DeepSeek models, live /models listing, and Hermes reasoning effort mapped to OpenPaths reasoning_effort. Disclosure — prompts, tool schemas, tool results and conversation context are sent to openpaths.io with your OPENPATHS_API_KEY and forwarded to the upstream model vendors it routes to; the plugin makes no other network calls and registers no tools or hooks.

OpenRouter + Nous Portal image generation. Chat-completions image output (reference-grounded) plus OpenRouter's Dedicated Image API (/images/generations) for gpt-image-2, Krea 2, Qwen Image 3 Pro, MAI-Image-2.5 and Grok Imagine — exact per-model aspect ratios, resolution/quality/background/seed/n, up to 16 reference images. Text-to-image and image-to-image.

OpenRouter API-key spend and recorded chat costs in USD/INR. Disclosure — sends the configured OpenRouter key (OPENROUTER_API_KEY, or the variable named in api_key_env) only to openrouter.ai's read-only key and generation accounting endpoints, and fetches public USD/INR rates from api.frankfurter.dev unless a manual rate is set; middleware on every LLM request records ids, model, token counts and reported cost (no prompt or reply text) to its own ledger; the dashboard reads accounting metadata (session ids, token counts, billing provider) read-only from the state.db and OpenRouter Spend ledger of every profile under the Hermes root.
OpenRouter speech-to-text and text-to-speech providers for Hermes Agent (stt.provider / tts.provider = openrouter).

OpenRouter video generation backend. Every generative model on the /api/v1/videos API (Veo, Sora, Kling, Seedance, Wan, Hailuo, Grok Imagine, FLUX Video, …) — text-to-video, image-to-video and reference-to-video; catalog and per-model limits discovered live.
OpenSpec CLI tools for spec-driven development workflows

OpenTelemetry for Hermes Agent: sessions, LLM and API calls, tool calls, sub-agents and approvals as OTLP traces, metrics and logs to any OTLP backend. Disclosure — sends span data including prompts, tool arguments and tool output only to backends you configure (a backends: list, an OTEL_* variable, or LANGSMITH_TRACING=true); by default content_capture is full and unclipped (preview clips to 1200 chars, off sends none); vendor SDK keys already in the environment are used only after that opt-in; with nothing configured it keeps a local owner-only SQLite store under $HERMES_HOME and sends nothing; installs opentelemetry-api, -sdk, -exporter-otlp-proto-http (>=1.35,<2) and PyYAML.

Operating skill for Hermes cron: lifecycle rules (pause vs disable vs remove, `in 30m` vs `30m`), four ways to avoid needless LLM runs (no_agent, wakeAgent pre-check, monitor, [SILENT]), verify-after-change, a layered runbook and a read-only doctor that complements `hermes cron doctor` and reports one error across several jobs as one scheduler fault and a cron store that cannot be written. Portable Agent Plugins v1 package (plugin.json + skills/); no tools, hooks, middleware or env vars. Disclosure — skill only, no network; the bundled doctor reads ~/.hermes/cron/jobs.json, ticker stamps and executions.db (or a named profile's store with --profile) read-only, checks the cron directory's permissions and free space without writing, and runs the local hermes cron doctor (argument list, no shell), whose job loader may repair malformed jobs.json entries (--no-builtin skips it).
Opper, the EU-hosted AI gateway (700+ models behind one OpenAI-compatible API), as a model provider

Opt-in background scheduling for host-known delegated sessions, supported cron execution and explicit worker profiles using an existing Adaptive Inference gateway. Interactive and explicitly classified requests retain their routing; model, tools, prompts, output limits and credentials are unchanged. Disclosure: adds only X-Adaptive-Class on an exactly configured chat-completions endpoint. No network calls, file access, processes, telemetry or credential handling in plugin code. Uses a bounded in-memory session index. Cron detection requires the newer public execution-identity capability; auxiliary routing is an explicit provider configuration, not an auxiliary middleware claim.

Opt-in bounded idle prompt warming for explicitly allowlisted OpenAI-compatible text-chat endpoints. Sends potentially billable requests; no tool execution or conversation writes. Does not support Codex/Responses or native Anthropic. Authenticated endpoints use optional HERMES_SESSION_WARMER_API_KEY.

Opt-in idle/daily gateway conversation resets. Reads the existing session_reset block (mode idle | daily | both, idle_minutes, at_hour) and starts a fresh session on the first inbound message past the boundary. No timers, no background writes.

OptChat-style endless memory for Hermes: an append-only verbatim log plus a binary summary tree, exposed as recall through the MemoryProvider ABC. Background compactor builds the tree with a cheap auxiliary model (call_llm task optchat_compact); prefetch returns a fixed-budget view of the whole history; optchat_zoom/optchat_date tools open any line down to the verbatim message. Disclosure — every turn's user messages, agent replies, tool calls and tool results (each result capped at 30,000 characters, after Hermes's secret redaction) are appended permanently to unencrypted owner-only files under $HERMES_HOME/optchat/, with no deletion or retention limit; a background compactor sends those messages and the surrounding summary view to your auxiliary model route (task optchat_compact) for summarization; each turn injects up to view_budget_chars (default 16,000) of that history into the model context.

Outbound WhatsApp tools through GOWA: registers GOWA's native MCP server and adds device listing, pairing, and removal. Setup can connect an existing server or explicitly install pinned GOWA v9.5.0 as a loopback-only authenticated native user service on Linux x86_64, macOS x86_64/arm64, or Windows x86_64. Disclosure — agents can send messages and mutate WhatsApp state through the linked account; session databases grant account access. The plugin does not ingest incoming messages or configure webhooks.

Owner-approved universal phone pairing and bundled read-only Live Operations reporting for selected Hermes profiles. Disclosure — paired phones get broad fleet:operator access over the internet, including cron jobs (unattended runs), Kanban task dispatch and media reads, and see live session titles/previews and subagent goals from the profiles you select for reporting; any messaging account you make an owner (with a one-time claim code from `hermes fleet claim`) can create pairing links and approve phones from a private chat, so that account's security is your host's security. Runs an explicitly activated background connector/reverse proxy behind your HTTPS origin and may launch a local Hermes backend; legacy QR flow opens a private local browser. Keeps an owner-only control socket in the system temp directory, plus pairing/owner state and shared local snapshots; reads selected profiles' session registries through private read-only imports. `hermes fleet reporting configure --apply` edits the selected profiles' config.yaml (with a backup). Local idle/retirement maintenance is explicit and not exposed to phones. Reporting adds no control power.
Oxylabs AI Studio web search and extraction provider for Hermes Agent. Requires OXYLABS_API_KEY (sign up at https://aistudio.oxylabs.io/api-key).

Paid web extract over TOON: web_extract pays a TOON node about $0.001 per page from a local payer sidecar; the node fetches through an Anyone network exit and returns markdown with a wuzzy/crawl v1 content hash. Disclosure — with TOON_PAYER_URL set and web.extract_backend toon, every web_extract URL goes to the user's anonfetch payer sidecar and spends about $0.001 from its TOON payment channel with no per-call confirmation; the sidecar's daily cap and origin allowlist are the only spending controls; pages are fetched through Anyone network exits.

Pairs this machine's Hermes bots with the AI Chipmunk mobile app from inside Hermes Desktop — pick a bot, get the reachable host, profile and API key as a scannable code. Registers a `hermes aichipmunk` CLI command, a desktop page and a dashboard API; no tools or hooks. Disclosure — on an explicit confirmed "Switch to Tailscale" it adds a persistent tailscale serve handler putting the API server's own port (plain HTTP inside the tailnet, API_SERVER_KEY auth) onto the tailnet; on a machine with no Tailscale CLI it instead runs hermes config set platforms.api_server.host <tailnet IP> on the owning profile and restarts that gateway; reads API_SERVER_KEY from every profile's .env on this machine on each status poll (masked in lists, the full key only in the pairing link and QR returned to an authenticated dashboard caller, which may be the phone over a published dashboard); shells out to the tailscale and hermes CLIs and probes only this machine's own /health; no third-party network calls.

Parallel AI task orchestrator. Paste a task list into the desktop panel; Hermes phases it into dependency-ordered groups through the agent_batch_plan / agent_batch_phase tools (or you group it yourself in one click), then each phase dispatches one independent coding agent per task to a GitHub Actions workflow in a repo you name — own branch, own PR — and the panel tracks the runs and the PRs. GITHUB_TOKEN is the only required credential; AGENT_BATCH_REPO, AGENT_BATCH_WORKFLOW, AGENT_BATCH_MODEL and AGENT_BATCH_STATE are optional (the last is a directory override for the plan file, not a secret) and each can be set per plan in the panel instead. Disclosure — Hermes can read and rewrite the stored phase plan through the agent_batch_plan / agent_batch_phase tools, but dispatch is always a confirmed click in the panel. Each dispatch fires a GitHub workflow_dispatch with your GITHUB_TOKEN (Actions + pull-requests write) on the repo you name. The workflow you copy into that repo installs third-party coding-agent CLIs (cline by default; the others are unpinned npm packages) and runs them unattended, with auto-approve / skip-permissions, repo write access and your provider secrets. They push real branches and open real PRs, and your task text and repository code go to that runner's model vendor. LLM cost belongs to the runner: cline spends Cline Credits or a BYOK key, opencode free models need its zen relay, kilo needs an active Kilo Go subscription (keyless CI runs fail), and claude-code / codex / dsh need their own keys.
Parallel.ai web search + content extraction. Search returns objective-tuned results; extract uses the async SDK for parallel page fetches. Requires PARALLEL_API_KEY — sign up at https://parallel.ai.

Pay supported HTTP 402 MPP challenges on Tempo through mpp_fetch and in-process HTTPX clients. Uses a dedicated wallet. Disclosure — with MPP_ALLOWED_ORIGINS unset, any supported HTTP 402 MPP challenge returned to core HTTPX traffic (not only mpp_fetch) is auto-paid from the Tempo wallet with no per-payment cap or confirmation; the origin allowlist is the operator's control.

Payer-side freight reconciliation: import carrier bills and trip ledgers into a deterministic local core (SQLite, WAL, no cloud), re-calculate against contracted rates and produce evidence-linked difference lists for human review — 14 MCP tools over uvx stdio (engine pinned to the immutable commit e8cd259c, release v0.4.1), with 3 bilingual workflow skills bundled. Portable Agent Plugins v1 package (mcp.json + skills/); needs uv on PATH. Never approves payments, sends messages or writes back to ERP/TMS; final confirmations route through a local admin page the model cannot reach. Disclosure — the optional freight-admin page listens on 127.0.0.1 and is where a human confirms mappings, rules, matches and exports; nothing leaves the machine.

Penny core memory and private notes for Hermes. Disclosure — automatic recall sends the first 4,000 characters of each nontrivial local prompt to app.mypenny.ai as a search query, and the agent can save notes there through penny_remember without a Hermes approval prompt; works only in local CLI/TUI conversations (cron, subagents and gateways are refused); login is a manual command that registers its own OAuth client with clerk.mypenny.ai and briefly listens on 127.0.0.1 for the callback; tokens are kept in <HERMES_HOME>/penny/auth.json (owner-only) and are not removed on uninstall; no raw transcript upload, telemetry or other-client credential reuse.

Per-call cost ledger for Hermes Desktop: every model call Hermes makes is recorded from the observer hooks (provider, model, tokens, duration, outcome) and paired with the charge the billing provider actually took; works with no billing account, priced by Hermes' own estimate where the price book knows the model. English or Vietnamese; dong or dollars. Disclosure — three observer hooks (post_api_request, post_auxiliary_call, api_request_error) record per-call metadata from every profile in the install (session id, platform, task, provider, model, token counts, duration, finish reason, context length; never prompt, response or tool-argument text) into one shared SQLite ledger at <install root>/plugin-data/call-ledger/calls.sqlite, and import this plugin's own older per-profile ledgers into it once. It caches the vilao.ai model list there and the USD-to-VND rate under the active profile's plugin-data/call-ledger. Network is GET-only: vilao.ai (wallet balance, per-request usage, consumer keys) with VILAO_PAT read through Hermes's secret scope (vilao issues one full-scope token per account, including wallet writes; this plugin only reads), the public vilao.ai model list with no credential, and open.er-api.com for the dollar rate. The first full billing pull pages back through up to ten years of the account's usage. Nothing runs while the Desktop page is closed. Derived from hermes-resetwatch (Adolanium, MIT).

Per-call delegation across your own subscriptions. The model sends each subagent to a named route with delegate_to(route, goal, context); each route pins a provider Hermes already knows (Claude, Codex or Antigravity subscription plugins, ACP provider plugins) and a model. delegate_task, by contrast, uses the one target in config.yaml. Subagents launch through ctx.subagent_lifecycle. A child counts as out of quota only on an unambiguous provider error or a measured window at 100 %, and the route never switches on its own: a policy decides whether the parent asks you, picks another route, or waits. Disclosure: a pre_tool_call hook blocks delegate_task spawns while routes are configured (list/steer/stop pass); an api_request_error hook records quota errors in memory. Quota is read with Hermes' fetch_account_usage (Anthropic and OpenAI Codex) on /ohx quota and after a provider error. No other network egress, no files written.
Per-job progress updates in chat for jobs Hermes hands off to other machines (coding agents, CI, scripts), with per-job mute and follow and no model calls.

Per-process throttle for Lightning AI (https://lightning.ai/api/v1) keeping LLM requests within the ~15 requests/min limit, using an in-memory token bucket. Gates only calls whose provider or base_url points at Lightning AI; no-op otherwise. Disclosure — registers one llm_execution middleware and nothing else; no network calls, files, or processes of its own.

Per-provider quota and balance readout in the Hermes desktop status bar. Per-provider chips with eye toggles, a popover with every quota window, reset times, balance and key-cap amounts, near-limit amber tint, a desktop notification per threshold crossing, and burn-rate projections (ETA to reset or depletion). Providers: OpenCode Go, OpenAI Codex, OpenRouter, plus Anthropic, GitHub Copilot, Nous, Z.AI, Kimi, MiniMax and DeepSeek when configured. Disclosure — resolves provider credentials read-only (Hermes account-usage helpers and profile secrets, else the profile's .env and the vendor CLI login files ~/.codex/auth.json, ~/.claude/.credentials.json and ~/.local/share/opencode/auth.json) and sends each only to that provider's usage endpoint; the GitHub Copilot check presents the VS Code / Copilot client identity. No subprocesses, no telemetry.

Per-turn LLM routing: on each matching turn a TypeSafe Jev classifier call (api.typesafe.ai) receives turn-shape features plus the first 1200 chars of the last user message (shadow mode included) and labels it free/paid; high-confidence routine turns are downgraded to the provider's configured free rung, strategic mid-rung turns on Nous are escalated to the configured premium rung after a 2-token billed credit probe (Nous only, fail-closed). Fail-open, shadow-by-default, per-provider rungs from the user's lane2_config.json (leaderboard resolver script optional). Probe model id is fixed in code (z-ai/glm-5.3-flash). Disclosure — once you list models in ~/.hermes/jev/lane2_config.json, the first call of each matching turn sends message/tool counts and the first 1,200 characters of the last user message (send_excerpt, on by default) to TypeSafe Jev at api.typesafe.ai with your JEVI_API_KEY, in shadow mode as well as live; in live mode Jev's answer switches the request (and every later call of that turn, via an llm_execution wrapper) to the free, flash or premium model you configured on the same provider; with escalation set up on Nous it sends a 2-token billed ping to the Nous inference API with NOUS_API_KEY at most every 5 minutes; every turn appends a decision row (with that excerpt on routed turns) to ~/.hermes/jev/lane2-live.jsonl, which is never rotated.

Per-turn cost classifier across three model tiers (Quick / Standard / Expert): rates each user turn from configurable best_for lists and rewrites the outgoing request's model through the llm_request middleware, biased to keep the previous tier unless the turn changes shape, with escalate_model for tool failures. Disclosure — the plugin rewrites the model field of every outgoing request for a classified session, picking between three configured model ids that must all belong to the session's own provider (a foreign-provider tier is refused and the session model stands); it makes one bounded auxiliary classifier call through the host's plugin LLM route on each classified turn (up to about 12,000 characters of recent conversation plus the prompt), reading its model ids from config.json next to the plugin, MODEL_PICKER_CONFIG, or MODEL_PICKER_* env, and falls back to the host's primary model; routing decisions, with the first 120 characters of each classified prompt, are logged to $HERMES_HOME/logs/model-picker.log; a classifier-driven tier change can ask the context engine to compact the transcript before the switch, and escalate_model replaces the next request's context with a model-written handoff summary plus the recent tail; that engine registers only when the host config sets context.engine: model-picker.

Per-turn model AND reasoning-effort routing, decided by TypeSafe Jev, which rewrites the outgoing Ollama:Cloud provider request itself via the llm_request middleware. Every other catalog router picks a model and stops, and the two entries that touch reasoning effort move it by hand; this one decides both per turn. Ollama:Cloud only — no other provider is routed, and every failure path leaves the request byte-identical to a plugin-disabled run. Disclosure — sends the current user message and up to 4 previous turns to OpenRouter's Decisions API (typesafe/jev, billed to your OpenRouter key) on every routed turn.

Per-turn model routing for the request that is about to go out. Jev reads the turn, picks the tier it deserves, and the plugin rewrites the provider request onto that model, including the reasoning level when the request carries one. Shadow by default, with notify, confirm and auto modes, a strip under the composer for the turn that was just routed, and a spend ledger. A pick on another provider is reported rather than sent, because a plugin cannot open a second provider client. Disclosure — once a routing JSON is configured, every turn (shadow mode included) sends the current message, up to 4,000 characters of recent user/assistant turns, the active model name, an estimated context size and the spend/budget snapshot to TypeSafe (api.typesafe.ai, endpoint overridable in that JSON), and the jev_route tool and /jev-routing route send their text the same way; in auto mode it rewrites the model and reasoning level on outgoing requests, and in Hermes Desktop the auto mode and the approve row also switch the session's model, including onto another provider (core's expensive-model confirmation is shown to the user, never answered automatically).
Perplexity Search API web search and query-relevant page snippets. Requires PERPLEXITY_API_KEY — get one at https://www.perplexity.ai/account/api.

Persistent agent memory over a mnemostack service or a local Qdrant — hybrid recall (vector + lexical + graph), verbatim capture with self-echo suppression, and soft retraction. Multi-tenant when pointed at a shared authenticated service; the tenant is resolved server-side from the service key. Disclosure — the pinned directory is a discovery shim; the provider code installs from PyPI at the version pinned in plugin.yaml pip_dependencies (hermes-mnemostack==1.0.3) into the Hermes venv. Configured via MNEMOSTACK_* env vars; no key is required for a purely local Qdrant setup.

Persistent long-term conversations across session boundaries via structured handoff briefs and token monitoring. Disclosure — stores handoff briefs (topic, work in progress, decisions, open questions, next step; in aggressive mode auto-built from the first 200 characters of recent user messages) as plain JSON under HERMES_HOME/long-conversations/ and injects the pending brief into the first turn of the next session for the same chat or user (CLI briefs stay in one local scope and are not shown to messaging users); the model can change the plugin's settings with long_conv_config_set; an opt-in HERMES_LONG_CONV_BETA_LOG writes a local event log; no network calls.

Persistent memory for Hermes. Canonicalizes duplicate memories, surfaces contradictions between structured or recognized single-valued claims for review, and returns a why_retrieved reason list with every recall. Embedded by default: no server, no token, no GPU. Optional HTTP backend for HA clusters; pluggable embedders (bundled potion-2M default).

Persistent memory for agents, shared across tools: save preferences, decisions and lessons and recall them later by natural-language search; rating a recalled memory as helpful or misleading re-ranks what comes back next; shared rooms (beta) let several people's agents work from one memory. Portable Agent Plugins v1 package (plugin.json + mcp.json + skills/) pointing at the hosted Mnemoverse MCP server (Streamable HTTP, OAuth 2.1 + DCR); the two bundled skills load under a namespaced name. Disclosure — hosted-only connector; Hermes runs no code from the package (scripts/ holds the repository's own CI checks). Every tool call goes to the vendor's remote MCP server at mcp.mnemoverse.com (authorization server auth.mnemoverse.com, browser sign-in on console.mnemoverse.com); memories the agent writes are stored in the signed-in user's Mnemoverse account, and recalled memories are pulled into the session context. OAuth tokens are held and refreshed by Hermes, never by the package. No telemetry, background process or self-update code.
Persistent session file diffs, run comparisons, and individual edit history in Hermes Desktop.

Persistent, wallet-scoped long-term memory for Hermes: remember, semantic recall, versioned update, history and approved hard delete, backed by the hosted Wicked Memory service, plus skills for using it and for connecting the Wicked MCP server. Works with no setup (a wallet is generated on first use; search uses the service's shared free key). Disclosure — sends the memory text and search queries the agent chooses to memory.wickedapi.com (or your configured base_url), each request signed by the agent's wallet, plus one GET to /v1/status on first use to read the published community key; stores a generated private key unencrypted in the plugin data dir unless you supply WICKED_MEMORY_PRIVATE_KEY; no shell commands, no background processes, no telemetry; every wicked_memory_forget asks for human approval. The bundled wicked-suite-mcp skill walks you through adding the author's hosted Wicked MCP server (https://mcp.wickedapi.com/mcp, 75 tools, some x402-priced); that server is a separate manual step and is not covered by this pin.

Personal daily newspaper for Hermes: gathers weather, calendar, AQI, curated 36-hour news (timestamped Reddit RSS + X + web search, per-story QR codes), and newsletter digests, renders one 8.5x11 newsprint page, and prints it every morning via a cron job.
Personalizable rice-style Home page with draggable, resizable glass widgets for Hermes Web and Desktop.

Phone notifications, questions and approvals through Pushary's native Hermes approval transport, with optional per-tool gates. Disclosure — approval transport and per-tool gates hand dangerous-command approvals to whoever holds the devices or Slack channel paired to your Pushary account (fails closed); messages queued in the Pushary app or Mac notch are injected into the next turn as operator instructions and wait in ~/.pushary/run/hermes-commands; sends session events with a machine id (~/.pushary/machine-id when present, else a hashed hostname) on every turn, the redacted command and description of each approval it carries, the redacted reason when Hermes marks a turn failed (max 200 characters), redacted gated-tool arguments and pushary_remind reminder text to pushary.com; reads PUSHARY_API_KEY only through Hermes.

Photon Spectrum gateway adapter for Hermes Agent. Connects to iMessage (and other Spectrum interfaces) through Photon's managed Spectrum platform. Both directions run over the `spectrum-ts` SDK's long-lived gRPC stream via a small supervised Node sidecar — inbound messages arrive on the SDK's `app.messages` stream (no webhook, no public URL, no signing secret), and outbound messages are sent over the same sidecar.
The plugin ships with a `hermes photon` CLI for the one-time device login + project + user setup. Runtime credentials are written to ``~/.hermes/.env`` (``PHOTON_PROJECT_ID`` = the Spectrum project id, ``PHOTON_PROJECT_SECRET``) like every other channel, with management metadata (device token, dashboard project id) in ``~/.hermes/auth.json``. Photon's free shared-line model lets users get started without a paid plan.
Pick the profile for a new chat right in the composer, next to the model pill, and see which profile a running chat belongs to.

Pick the sound Hermes Desktop plays when a turn finishes: one of the 14 built-in presets or your own audio file (mp3, wav, ogg), with an optional different sound during night hours. Files stay in the plugin's local storage. Desktop-only (desktop/plugin.js inside the plugin SDK surface); no agent tools, hooks, middleware or env vars.

Pick up where you left off: up to 10 cards (5 by default) of unfinished work from your recent Hermes chats, project folders and files, each with where you stopped and a one-click next step. Adapted from Herald OS by Luke (iamlukethedev), MIT. Disclosure — after explicit in-app consent (stored per profile), each Refresh reads recent chats from every profile's session store (read-only; profiles the user skips in Settings are never opened) and sends chat excerpts and metadata, project/file names and paths, git branch/changed-file names and recent commit subjects to the current profile's Hermes LLM route (the auxiliary title-generation model, main provider unless configured); runs read-only git and, on macOS, Spotlight `mdfind`; never reads document contents; writes only $HERMES_HOME/pickup/. The "Next step" button can submit a model-written prompt straight into the card's chat in one click. The optional install.sh, when asked, adds the plugin to every profile's plugins.enabled (undone exactly by uninstall.sh).

Picks the reasoning effort for every prompt: a fast judge (Jev/TypeSafe, a local OpenAI-compatible model, or any custom API) reads the next message once per turn and rewrites the request's reasoning effort before it ships — easy questions run cheap, hard jobs get high. Port of effortless for Claude Code. Disclosure — sends the next message (≤4000 chars) plus a short recent-conversation excerpt (≤1600 chars) to the configured judge endpoint (default api.typesafe.ai for Jev; a local or custom OpenAI-compatible API otherwise), solely to pick the effort; the optional model_map setting (off by default) also switches the turn's model to the one you map to the verdict; keeps recent per-turn token counts in its own plugin state; no telemetry; secrets resolved only through Hermes' secret scope; stdlib-only, no pip dependencies.
Pin or unpin sessions from their row with supported desktop SDK actions.

Pinned glowing chip + fire-themed panel with live subscription-quota windows (remaining %, reset countdown, burn-rate pace and run-out forecast with sparkline history) for every provider Hermes reports usage for. 12 color themes and fonts, RU/EN, zero dependencies, works on Windows. Disclosure — runs hermes usage --json through the Desktop gateway (cli.exec) every 1–15 minutes and sweeps up to 8 providers every 15 minutes; each run queries that provider's usage endpoint with the credential Hermes already holds. Reads the composer's selected provider from Desktop localStorage. No network calls of its own.

Plan, build and run LinkedIn and email outreach in LinkedCamp through LinkedCamp's hosted MCP server (Streamable HTTP at https://mcp.linkedcamp.com/mcp, OAuth sign-in with the account's API key, no keys in config): campaigns, audience search URLs, multi-step sequences, leads, unified inbox and AI-drafted replies, sending-account health, analytics, reply agents, and agency sub-accounts. Bundles the linkedcamp-outreach workflow skill. Agent Plugins v1 package (plugin.json + mcp.json + skills/), configuration only. Disclosure — every tool call goes to LinkedCamp's hosted server (mcp.linkedcamp.com) and acts on the user's LinkedCamp account; the tool set is served by that server at runtime and is not covered by the pinned sha. Sign-in runs the pinned mcp-remote@0.1.49 through npx (Node.js 20.18.1+ and npm required), which opens a browser and a local callback port on first use and stores OAuth tokens under ~/.mcp-auth. Some tools reach real people (campaign_launch starts outreach, message_send delivers at once); the package marks the server untrusted, so Hermes asks before every tool the server does not mark read-only and blocks them in unattended runs.

Plan, launch, watch and compare WOOF weather simulations on your own NVIDIA GPU: size runs with WOOF's own planner, launch them locally or on an ssh/WSL GPU host, get maps in the chat while the forecast runs, compare physics or resolution, run multi-arm research campaigns and score runs against radar and surface observations. Disclosure — runs need Linux x86_64 with an NVIDIA GPU (plan-only elsewhere); the user-run hermes woof install pip-installs recast-woof>=1.0.0,<1.1 into ~/woof-env and downloads WOOF tables and optional geography (about 1.6 GB); runs execute the WOOF CLI as detached background jobs writing to ~/woof-runs and fetch public weather data; run events are pushed into the chat as user-role messages; the optional serve/ scripts download llama.cpp and a Qwen GGUF and start an unauthenticated local model server.

Practice Lincoln-Douglas debate. A case workbench helps a student build their own case section by section (resolution analysis, value and criterion, contentions, evidence, blocks) with a coach that gives real help and asks hard questions but never writes the case. A topic briefing maps a new resolution for both sides. A full NSDA practice round (AC, cross-examination, NC, 1AR, NR, 2AR, with prep time) runs against an AI opponent at three levels, followed by a ballot from a lay, traditional or flow judge. A fallacies guide, drill and spotter work on the student's own case and on other people's arguments. Cases are kept in a library with Word, text and backup-file export. Every model call goes to the user's own Hermes model through the plugin LLM helper. Debate Workbench is an independent community plugin. It is not made or endorsed by Nous Research or the National Speech & Debate Association. Disclosure — one network call of its own: when the user adds a topic source link, it fetches that one public web page (http or https, public addresses only, checked on every redirect, 20-second timeout, first 30,000 characters of text kept); no credentials, telemetry, shell commands, background processes or self-updates; registers no tools, hooks or middleware, only a Desktop page and a dashboard API; stores cases, rounds, ballots and briefings in $HERMES_HOME/plugin-data/ld-workbench/; reads a .docx or .txt case file or a backup file only when the user picks one; writes an export only to a path the user picks in the save dialog, inside their home folder; the optional dictation button uses the speech recognition built into the desktop app's browser engine when that engine provides it, which may send the audio to that engine's speech service; no private Hermes imports.
Pre-release Microsoft 365 Graph tools for Outlook, SharePoint, OneDrive, Calendar, Teams, To Do, and Planner.

Prepare, slice, preflight and export 3D prints with stock OrcaSlicer profiles. Includes explicit printer upload/control, camera snapshots and monitoring through supported protocols. Protocol and hardware limits are documented. Independent of OrcaSlicer and Nous Research. Disclosure — executes the installed local slicer and exposes printer upload, start, pause, resume and cancel; agent-supplied confirmation is not independent human authentication. Printer/camera credentials are read from ORCA_*/HERMES_ORCA_* environment variables named in tool arguments (HTTPS required unless allow_plaintext_credentials is set); plugin state lives in ~/.hermes-orca (HERMES_ORCA_HOME), outside HERMES_HOME.

Preview, publish, and manage websites hosted on Showly from Hermes Agent, through the hosted Showly MCP server (Streamable HTTP). Portable Agent Plugins v1 package (mcp.json + skills/). Disclosure — tool calls go to Showly's hosted MCP server at mcp.showly.ai. The bundled showly-hosting skill makes Showly the default for any deploy, preview or share request that names no provider, and new links default to public (anyone with the link). The showly-reports skill runs a bundled local Node.js renderer (vendored answer-me-with-html 0.4.14, upstream self-update check removed) through the shell and uploads the report directory to Showly when sharing is requested. Sign-in is out of band: `npx @showly/mcp-server login --to hermes` (unpinned) writes MCP_SHOWLY_API_KEY into ~/.hermes/config.yaml.
Prism OpenAI-compatible inference with long-context DeepSeek models.

Privacy-first agent email inboxes and workspace automation through hosted Mermail MCP. Portable Agent Plugins v1 package (mcp.json + skills/, seventeen skills bundled); authenticate with OAuth via `hermes mcp login mermail`. No credentials are stored in mcp.json. Disclosure — the bundled skills also expose Mermail's paybox wallet tools over the hosted MCP (x402 payments, xStocks trading, standing grants); the skills allow the agent to move funds without a same-turn confirmation when your message already states exact terms, so spending controls live on your Mermail account, not in Hermes.

Private AgentPlaybooks memory for Hermes: bounded keyword recall across personal and team sources, exact native memory-write mirroring, archive and history. Disclosure — keywords derived from each turn's query are sent to the configured AgentPlaybooks service for recall from your personal and configured team playbooks; explicit native memory writes are mirrored there. Defaults to agentplaybooks.ai over HTTPS; localhost HTTP is supported, and remote intranet HTTP requires an explicit opt-in that sends the API key unencrypted. Team and shared playbooks are configured explicitly: the agent can write, archive and permanently delete entries in configured team playbooks (shared playbooks are read-only), and teammates' entries are recalled into context.

Private Yandex Alice voice input for Hermes, with replies in Telegram. Disclosure — off until you set enabled: true and allow_gateway_injection: true; then, while the Telegram gateway is connected, it listens on 127.0.0.1 (port 8788 by default) for webhooks forwarded by your own HTTPS reverse proxy. The secret URL path (ALICE_WEBHOOK_SECRET) is the only authentication: Yandex request signatures are not checked, and the skill and account IDs in the request can be forged by anyone who has the URL. Each accepted request becomes a user message in one fixed Telegram DM session and runs with that session's tools; approvals stay in Telegram and slash commands are refused. Leaving owner_user_id empty accepts any Alice account presenting the URL.

Private library for the finished documents agents make (self-contained HTML, Markdown, SVG, PNG, WebP), with an Artifacts dashboard tab and explicit, expiring, revocable guest links for one artifact each. Early public preview. Disclosure — the plugin is a client of a separate Artifacts service you run yourself from the same repository (not installed by the plugin): six tools and the dashboard tab send artifact bytes and metadata to HERMES_ARTIFACTS_URL with the machine credential HERMES_ARTIFACTS_TOKEN, resolved through Hermes secret scope, held server-side and never sent to the browser. artifact_publish reads a resolved local path only after Hermes read-policy and supported-extension checks; an explicit kind must match. artifact_download checks raw and resolved destinations against Hermes write policy, refuses approval-required paths even with overwrite=true, and writes atomically through a temporary sibling. File policy is defense in depth, not filesystem isolation. Sharing creates a public bearer link on your service; revocation cannot recall copies. Stores no data and no credentials of its own; no hooks, background processes or telemetry.

Process hygiene for agent machines — finds the background processes your agent left behind (dev servers, tunnels, watchers, nohup jobs) using evidence signals (ppid=1 reparent, port listener via /proc/net/tcp{,6}, dev-server traits, TTL exceeded) and attributes them to the originating tool call via agent-ledger's ledger when present. Dry-run by default: nothing is killed until you write policy_mode=enforce; system daemons and host/VM management agents are exempt by name, a user-editable whitelist covers your real infrastructure, and each kill re-reads the cmdline first (SIGTERM, 2s, SIGKILL with PID-reuse check). stdlib-only, fails open. Disclosure — inside Hermes it only appends terminal commands that look like they start background work (first 300 characters, which can include inline secrets) to plugin-data/agent-janitor/spawns.jsonl, and reads agent-ledger's ledger.db read-only when present. Killing is a separate CLI you run yourself (janitor_cli.py sweep): after you write "enforce" to plugin-data/agent-janitor/policy_mode it sends SIGTERM then SIGKILL to every process re-parented to PID 1 for over a minute that is not on its built-in exempt list or your whitelist, whoever started it (for example a tmux server or a nohup'd hermes gateway), including other users' processes when run as root. Dry-run first; the dry-run list is the kill list.
Profile-scoped document OCR for Hermes Desktop and HUD, with a guarded per-profile Windows service.

Prompt-customizable desktop dashboard with live host metrics, session activity, clocks, calendars, and text widgets. Disclosure — polls ~/monitoring-dashboard on the desktop device through the Desktop native file bridge, and its Reset command moves only the dashboard's own page/panel marker files in that folder to the OS trash (never dashboard.json or the folder); host metrics and session activity stay on the machine.

Proton Mail, Calendar, Contacts and Drive for a Hermes Agent, through an MIT-licensed client built from Proton's own open-source Go libraries (go-srp, go-proton-api) — no Proton Bridge and no paid plan. Reads, searches and sends mail (attachments, scheduled send, labels, folders), manages calendar events and RSVPs, contacts (signed/encrypted vCards), and Drive (upload, download, move, rename, trash, public share links). Sign-in runs in a terminal via `hermes proton login` and the account password is never taken through chat; sending is refused until a recipient allowlist is set and every send is gated by Hermes's pre_tool_call approval. Disclosure — talks to Proton's private, undocumented web API over the network; stores a per-account session file (0600) holding OAuth-style tokens and the derived key passphrase (never the password) under the profile's plugin-data folder, and on first load copies any sessions from the standalone client's `~/.config/protonlite` into it; reads local files you approve for attachments and Drive uploads and writes downloaded attachments and Drive files under that plugin-data folder; shells out to gpg for calendar/Drive key provisioning; `proton_schedule_followup` creates one-shot Hermes cron jobs (read-only Proton toolset) that run unattended and deliver to your home channel; no self-update, no downloaded binaries, no telemetry.

Proton Pass secret source: resolves pass://vault/item/field references (mapped source "protonpass") or every env-var-titled item of one vault (bulk source "protonpass_vault") into environment variables at startup through the user's own pass-cli, beside the built-in Bitwarden and 1Password sources, with a hermes protonpass setup/status/token/set/remove/sync/disable CLI. Stdlib-only, no Python deps. Disclosure — when enabled, runs the user-installed pass-cli (argv only, allowlisted env, 30 s per call), which talks to Proton's API; a personal access token or AI-agent token is read from Hermes' env and passed only to the pass-cli login child's environment (never argv); writes a 0700 session dir under cache/protonpass and a 0600 value cache (cache_ttl_seconds: 0 disables); no self-update, no downloaded binaries, no telemetry, no background process.

Provider-native Claude and Codex remaining allowance windows in the Hermes Desktop status bar. Disclosure — spawns the local `codex app-server` and `claude auth status` CLIs and reads the Claude OAuth token read-only through Hermes core; the optional install.sh (not part of the catalog install) edits the statusLine in ~/.claude/settings.json; macOS only.

Provider-neutral subscription quota matrix panel — each provider's subscription window as a single time x quota row (elapsed vs remaining at a glance), with UI-side show/hide per provider row. Disclosure — reads provider keys from the current profile's .env and token presence from its auth.json, and calls each provider's own usage/balance API with that key (Kimi, GLM, MiniMax, Command Code, DeepSeek, xAI management, OpenRouter, Alibaba Cloud BSS, Grok, Codex via Hermes); an optional shared_sources setting reads another profile's .env/auth.json the same way; the token-activity heatmap reads per-day token totals, providers and model names from the state.db of this profile and of every other profile on the install (read-only, no message content, nothing leaves the machine); nothing is written outside this plugin's settings.

Public holidays for 200+ countries and their regions, plus workday checks, workday counts and deadline math (N working days after a date), computed in code instead of by the model. Disclosure — sends HTTPS GET requests to date.nager.at (Nager.Date, free, no key) carrying only a country code and a year; no redirects, 10 s timeout, responses cached in memory only. No credentials, no files written, no shell commands, no hooks, no background processes, no telemetry.

Publish a website, or share files and folders, at a live *.webly.site URL from Hermes Agent with no account, then sign in to claim it, edit it, and publish drafts the person approves through the hosted Webly MCP server (Streamable HTTP). Portable Agent Plugins v1 package (plugin.json + mcp.json + skills/). Disclosure — MCP tool calls go to api.webly.ai/v1/mcp, sending WEBLY_API_KEY as a bearer header when it is set, and the webly server is marked untrusted so Hermes asks before each Webly MCP tool that changes something. The bundled webly skill runs a local Node.js 20+ helper (scripts/webly.mjs) through the shell: it uploads only the files and folders the person asks to publish or share to api.webly.ai (sites are public unless password-protected), runs the project's npm/pnpm/yarn install and build first when the folder has a build script, opens the browser for sign-in and claim, and keeps its anonymous-site token and optional OAuth sign-in in ~/.webly (mode 0600). Its doctor command reads ~/.claude.json, ~/.claude/settings.json and ~/.codex/config.toml only to see whether a webly MCP server is configured there. Publishing, deleting and replacing sites through that helper are gated by skill instructions, not by Hermes approvals. The catalog copy has no update check.
Publish and read private Markdown or HTML reports through your Artifact Relay server.

Publish what Hermes builds (reports, dashboards, briefs, proposals) to a private link that opens in any browser with no account for the viewer, set a passcode or limit it to a company's email addresses, update it in place, and see who opened it and what they commented. Portable Agent Plugins v1 package (mcp.json + skills/). Disclosure — hosted-only connector with no local code; every tool call goes to Stacktree's remote MCP server at api.stacktr.ee (OAuth 2.1 with dynamic client registration, token kept by Hermes); the HTML the model passes to publish_html or update_site is stored in the user's Stacktree account and served at the returned link (unlisted by default, public when a public_slug is set); page titles, open counts and third-party reader comments from that account are read into the session; the remote tools that publish, update, gate, delete pages or email approval requests run without a Hermes approval prompt; the required sign-in step `hermes mcp add stacktree --url https://api.stacktr.ee/mcp --auth oauth` writes a config.yaml server entry that replaces the package's own.

Pushover as an outbound-only gateway platform, plus opt-in agent lifecycle notifications (finished, questions, errors, approvals, kanban blockers, Hermes's sudo password prompt) via Pushover and/or native notify-send, managed with /notifications. Disclosure — sends HTTPS requests to api.pushover.net only, carrying your Pushover app token, user key and notification text (when lifecycle notifications are enabled, excerpts of agent replies, clarify questions, approval commands, the command waiting on the sudo password prompt (redacted by Hermes; never the password) and kanban block reasons; PUSHOVER_NOTIFY_QUESTION=minimal suppresses all but kanban reasons); send_message can address any Pushover user or group key; runs notify-send (argv, no shell) when native notifications are enabled; writes an unrotated log under $HERMES_HOME/logs and settings.json under $HERMES_HOME/plugin-data, and $HERMES_HOME/.env only from the interactive setup wizard. Outbound-only, no inbound or approval path, no telemetry, no background processes.

Puts the names a speech-to-text model mis-hears into the transcription prompt Hermes sends with each voice message: terms you list (globally or per surface) and names found in this profile's memories/USER.md and MEMORY.md, most important last, within the 896 characters Hermes keeps for Whisper-family backends; your stt.prompt stays in front. Notes written in German, Spanish, French, Italian, Dutch, Portuguese or Turkish can be named in the languages setting. Disclosure — register() adds one pre_transcription hook that returns a new prompt string; memory-derived names go only to local backends (faster-whisper, local_command) unless allow_remote is set, and the memory files are not read otherwise; reads at most 256 KB per memory file; no tools, network access, subprocesses or writes; Hermes uploads the prompt with the audio to the configured STT provider.
QQ Bot gateway adapter (Official QQ Bot API v2). WebSocket gateway for inbound events, REST for outbound text and media.

Quote and order custom 3D printed and CNC machined parts from your CAD files through the hosted Make Parts Now MCP server (Streamable HTTP, no sign-in to quote), with the quote-parts workflow skill bundled: upload an STL, STEP, 3MF or OBJ file, get the price and ship date for each production speed (SLS nylon, FDM plastic, CNC aluminum and brass), change the quantity, material or speed, and get a checkout link. Portable Agent Plugins v1 package (mcp.json + skills/), configuration only. Disclosure — hosted-only connector with no local code; every tool call goes to makepartsnow.com. To quote a local file the agent uploads that one CAD file with curl through the terminal tool (Hermes approvals apply) to a one-time upload link, or gives the user an upload page. Nothing is charged in chat: checkout links open Stripe Checkout on makepartsnow.com where the user pays. US shipping only.

Raft gateway adapter for Hermes Agent. Connects to a Raft workspace as an external agent via a local wake-channel bridge. The adapter starts a loopback HTTP endpoint that receives content-free wake hints from the bridge, then injects them into the Hermes gateway session pipeline. The agent reads and sends messages through the Raft CLI — the adapter never touches message bodies or delivery cursors.

Read RSS and Atom feeds and discuss articles in Hermes Desktop. Disclosure — feeds and full articles are fetched with curl through the gateway's shell.exec on the connected Hermes host (public-IPv4 SSRF guard); opt-in AI grading sends article excerpts to your configured model and creates HERMES_HOME/skills/rss-importance-grading/SKILL.md if missing; opt-in image loading fetches publisher images directly from Desktop.

Read one CalDAV calendar collection you run, with list_events and read_event. Disclosure — Sends CALDAV_USER and CALDAV_PASSWORD as Basic auth to your CALDAV_URL, does not follow redirects, and starts no local program. Over plain http that password travels unencrypted. The tools are on for every surface, including gateways, and the plugin has no user list of its own: anyone you allow on your Hermes gateway reads the calendar with your password. Turn a surface off with hermes tools. A watch is a cron job you create yourself with hermes cron create. Each run is at least one model turn, there is no daily cap, and the job stays until you run hermes cron remove. Under plugins.isolation: host the watch cannot run and posts a notice saying so on every run. When the watch can run, it reports a problem on the first run, when the cause changes and again after 23 hours, or on every run when its data directory cannot be written. Each request gives up after 20 seconds without data, and a whole call has no time limit. The watch relies on private parts of Hermes, so an update can stop it. State lives in plugin-data/event-read. Not tested against a vendor-hosted calendar.

Read one public profile and watch one account, with profile_get, author_feed and author_watch. It reads public posts and profiles from the Bluesky social media network, which is built on the AT Protocol (atproto), without signing in. Disclosure — HTTPS GET only to public.api.bsky.app, no API key, and no program on your machine. The tools are on for every surface, including gateways, and ask for no approval: anyone you allow on your gateway can call them. Turn a surface off with hermes tools. While the plugin is enabled, its skill adds one line to the skills index of every session, including surfaces where the tools are turned off. hermes author-feed schedule creates one cron job, a model turn every hour by default (two or more model requests, no daily cap). Delivered to local unless you pass --deliver, so no chat by default. Run hermes author-feed unschedule before removal. A leftover job after the plugin is gone stops with hermes cron remove <id>. Under plugins.isolation: host the watch cannot run and posts a notice saying so on every run. The first run only records what is already there. One run reads at most the latest 3 pages and announces a new post by this account on them. When every row on those pages is new, with no saved post or mark, and the feed still offers another cursor, it also posts a possible-miss notice, at most once in 24 hours while that keeps happening. Replies, including the account's own thread continuations, are not announced. It relies on private Hermes parts, so an update can stop it. State stays in <HERMES_HOME>/plugin-data/author-feed after uninstall.

Read-only Covision meeting, assigned-task, and published-knowledge tools through the Covision Streamable HTTP MCP service, plus a workflow skill. Requires a Covision account, organization connector enablement, and browser OAuth consent; no API key or client secret is stored in the plugin.

Read-only Desktop model map for main, auxiliary, sub-agent and MoA routes. Disclosure — reads the selected profile's full config.yaml through the host's `config.get` (the response includes any credential fields it holds); only model-routing fields are kept and nothing is stored or sent off the machine.

Read-only Hermes Dashboard and Desktop plugin for inspecting built-in, holographic, Mem0, Honcho, Mnemosyne, Hindsight, and ByteRover memory. Disclosure — reads the active profile's memory files, provider configs and provider API keys (keys are never returned to the UI), and on user action sends search/recall/reflect queries with configured bank/peer/user IDs to the configured Mem0, Honcho and Hindsight endpoints (Hindsight Cloud default api.hindsight.vectorize.io) using those keys; ByteRover queries run the local `brv` CLI; for a local embedded Hindsight setup a contents read may start the `hindsight-embed` daemon; no memory is written.

Read-only Hermes Desktop page for the focused chat: the main agent and its subagents, background commands and a Replay of file edits. Disclosure — its local dashboard routes serve the file-edit contents (Replay) and background-command output tails of the chat you view to the Desktop page; reads state.db read-only.
Read-only Hermes Desktop pane for live and past delegated subagent workers.

Read-only Home Assistant Recorder statistics tools (ha_list_statistics and ha_get_statistics). Disclosure — each call opens an authenticated WebSocket connection to the configured Home Assistant instance using the active profile HASS_TOKEN; returned statistic metadata and values become agent tool results and may reach the configured model provider. No telemetry, shell commands, background processes, credential storage or direct database access.

Read-only NextDNS tools - DNS query logs, blocked queries with the blocklist that matched, and aggregate analytics by domain, device, blocklist or protocol. For triaging DNS problems and answering "was this blocked, and by what". Uses the official NextDNS API; makes no configuration changes.

Read-only Unraid monitoring for Hermes Desktop: server metadata, array capacity, Docker containers, virtual machines, and grouped alerts. Disclosure — sends fixed GraphQL queries to the user-configured Unraid host and stores a VIEWER key through Hermes secret scope; no telemetry, background process, shell, SSH, MCP, or mutations.

Read-only access to your own Apple Health data through a self-hosted HealthRelay receiver. Portable Agent Plugins v1 package with one stdio MCP server (ten read-only tools, including intake evidence; no raw SQL, no write tools) and three skills for setup, review and troubleshooting. Requires your own HealthRelay receiver (health-bridge) and an iPhone app you sign yourself; the plugin ships neither. Disclosure — exposes your Apple Health data, read-only, from your own receiver database to whichever model you run, so use a local model or one you trust with health data; runs the separately installed health-bridge binary from PATH; the setup skill can install the receiver from the author's git tag with uv tool install.

Read-only audit of local TLS posture — certificate validity, key strength, deprecated protocols, weak cipher suites, and the certificate each server's configuration points at. Disclosure — reads a fixed list of system certificate and nginx/Apache config paths under / (or a caller-supplied prefix); makes no network connections and runs no subprocesses. If the sibling plugin pcs-security-core is installed, its copy of the shared contract is loaded in preference to the bundled one.

Read-only dashboard tab and model-free /duty and hermes duty summaries for waiting conversations, unanswered messages, running turns, undelivered background results and failing cron jobs. Supports all 17 dashboard languages, including right-to-left Arabic. Disclosure — opens HERMES_HOME/state.db with SQLite mode=ro (sessions, messages, turn leases, async delegations, goals) and reads cron/jobs.json and gateway_state.json; writes only HERMES_HOME/duty-board/dismissed.json for dashboard dismissals. Chat requires in-process Hermes 0.21.7+ and a configured owner; shared-chat summaries default to counts only. No network calls, no model calls, no credentials, no background processes.

Read-only memory.provider for GBrain (garrytan/gbrain, MIT; not affiliated). After each non-trivial turn it searches a GBrain MCP server (`gbrain serve --http`) in the background and injects up to the configured limit (3 by default, capped at 10) of `[source:slug] title` pointers into the next turn as fallible background context. It never writes to GBrain and adds no tools or hooks. Disclosure — after each non-trivial turn, the first 500 characters of your message are sent to GBRAIN_MCP_URL (default http://127.0.0.1:3131/mcp; plain http to a non-loopback host is refused unless GBRAIN_POINTER_ALLOW_HTTP=1), and the profile's GBrain OAuth client id and secret go to that server's /token endpoint. Redirects and proxy settings are ignored. Only the slug, title and source id of up to 10 results are kept and injected into the next turn as background context; rows GBrain flags as suspected injection are skipped. Tokens and pointers stay in memory only. It never writes to GBrain; no other network calls, no telemetry.

Read-only observability for Hermes Desktop: what each session cost and why, its full trace, recurring tool failures, every profile at a glance, provider quotas and service balances, model comparison with cheaper-route evidence, and instruction-rule grading. Disclosure — reads every profile's state.db read-only plus agent logs, cron/gateway state, config.yaml and .env (key names, and the values of keys an adapter uses); with the credentials Hermes' own resolvers return, calls only each configured vendor's usage or balance endpoint (hosts listed in the README), sending Grok CLI client headers to cli-chat-proxy.grok.com and a Claude Code user-agent to api.anthropic.com; Hermes' resolvers may renew Hermes' Codex, Nous and xAI logins and, when Hermes holds no other Anthropic credential, Claude Code's login; runs the local monid CLI when installed; an Anthropic one-token Claude Haiku probe is off by default; writes no Hermes state itself and sends no session content anywhere.

Read-only paid-media analysis for Google Ads, Meta (Facebook) Ads, Microsoft Ads, LinkedIn Ads, Google Analytics (GA4), Search Console and Merchant Center through the hosted HYPD MCP. Portable Agent Plugins v1 package with four skills (setup, tool rules, overview, ready-made analyses). OAuth uses pinned mcp-remote@0.1.49 over npx stdio, so Node.js 20.18.1+ and npm are required. Read-only: never changes campaigns, budgets or ads. Disclosure — runs the pinned mcp-remote@0.1.49 through npx (downloaded from npm on first run) as a local bridge to HYPD's hosted MCP server at mcp.hypd.ai; tool arguments and the ad, analytics, Search Console and Merchant Center data HYPD returns pass through HYPD's servers; sign-in is a browser OAuth flow whose tokens mcp-remote stores in ~/.mcp-auth; read-only is HYPD's server-side guarantee, and the analysis templates the skills follow are fetched from HYPD's server at run time.

Read-only pixel-art RPG view of real Hermes Kanban and worker activity, with a live web dashboard tab and an optional native Desktop page. The Desktop page currently supports explicit local connections only; registry and SSH remote connections fail closed until a public SDK connection-lifecycle hook is available. Standalone demo data is synthetic. Disclosure — reads local Hermes data outside its own directory (kanban.db, every profile's state.db, profile.yaml, config.yaml model/effort, logs/agent.log, bot-status.json) on each dashboard poll: every /replay or /events request (about every 10 s while the tab is open) runs the bundled Python extractor as a subprocess (argument list, no shell, 30 s timeout); a background thread samples bot-status.json every 30 s (HERMES_QUEST_SAMPLER=off disables it) and writes bot-status history, checkpoint state, a lock and a random 0600 HMAC key under <hermes_home>/hermes-quest/ (not yet plugin-data); profile names and task titles are hidden unless enabled and only shown to host-authenticated dashboard sessions; the Desktop page works only on an explicit local connection; no network calls beyond the local Hermes backend.

Read-only project inspection and asset audits with playable-slice, asset-production, and verification skills. Disclosure — lists file names and sizes under any absolute project path the agent supplies (skipping hidden, symlinked and credential-named entries), reads that project's project.godot/export_presets.cfg and, on request, hashes asset files; no writes, no shell commands, no network calls.

Read-only status and peer list for a WireGuard server running on the same Windows machine as Hermes. Two tools: vpn_status (service state, tunnel address and port, server public key, per-peer handshake and transfer) and vpn_peers (the peer list only). The plugin runs only wg.exe show, sc.exe query, and one PowerShell adapter lookup; it never changes the tunnel and never reads the tunnel configuration file or any private key material. Windows only (WireGuard for Windows). Disclosure — runs local wg.exe show, sc.exe query and one PowerShell Get-NetIPAddress lookup (read-only, never touches the tunnel config or private key); tool results put peer public keys, allowed IPs and peer endpoint IP addresses into the conversation sent to your model provider.

Readable agent.log viewer in the desktop status bar — a live, colour-coded feed of API calls, tools, turns, fallbacks, warnings and errors, with per-call tokens/latency/cache, stats tables, and a single-dot alert for genuine non-self-healing faults. Follows app theme/language.

Reads one OctoPrint printer. A cron watch reports printer_disconnected (not a pause); error; complete after Printing, Printing from SD, Pausing, Paused, Resuming, or Finishing; paused after Printing, Printing from SD, Pausing, or Resuming; cancelled; and stalled. This plugin can be used with OctoPrint. OctoPrint is a registered trademark owned by Gina Häußge (https://octoprint.org). Disclosure — Talks to the one OctoPrint origin you set in OCTOPRINT_URL with your OCTOPRINT_API_KEY, plus an optional webcam still from the same host, fetched without the key when it is on another port. Over plain http, that key is sent unencrypted. Pause, resume, and cancel ask for Hermes approval every time and are refused under cron, yolo, approvals off, single-query, unattended sessions and plugins.isolation: host, and when those checks cannot run. The plugin has no user list of its own: anyone you allow on your Hermes gateway can ask for a move and approve it. Running hermes tools does not remove the slash command. Answering "always" adds one unused line to config.yaml, and that line does not approve the next move. The optional watch is a cron job you create from the CLI (a model turn every 5 minutes by default) that stays after uninstall until you run unschedule. At that default it is 288 runs a day with no daily cap. The watch needs plugins.isolation: in_process; under host it only posts a notice that it cannot run, on every run. Not tested on a physical printer, with access control off, or with the stock webcam.

Realtime duplex voice chat with the Gemini Live API — a status-bar minibar for the Hermes desktop app (transcript, model catalog, thinking level, session token meter, auto-redial via session resumption). Full-proxy architecture: the plugin backend owns the upstream Live WebSocket and the user's key (requires_env GOOGLE_API_KEY); the desktop UI only talks to localhost and receives single-use ephemeral tokens. No agent tools; desktop-focused, dashboard tab hidden. Disclosure — pressing Start captures microphone audio and streams it through the local backend to generativelanguage.googleapis.com using GOOGLE_API_KEY (or GEMINI_API_KEY) from the environment; input/output transcripts are held in backend memory for the session, and a Gemini session-resumption handle is written to .resume.json inside the plugin's install directory.

Realtime duplex voice with the Gemini Live API, built around handing real work to Hermes. A single control in the composer (not a floating panel): tap, speak, hear the model, and when the ask needs files, a terminal, the web or memory the voice model delegates the job to the api server and keeps talking, reading the outcome aloud when it lands. Three verbs rather than thirty schemas — hermes_task starts, hermes_tasks reads the call's task board, and hermes_task_update denies, steers or stops a task. A task that stops to ask permission reaches the user as a spoken prompt and a "Hermes needs you" indicator with Approve and Deny buttons; only the user's press approves it, never the voice model. Multi-task is one Live session plus a board, not a session per task. Mute drops the uplink without hanging up, and the call survives composer remounts, so opening a session mid-sentence does not kill it. Full-proxy architecture: the plugin backend owns the upstream Live socket and the key, and the renderer is never given either, because the Live API carries the credential in the socket URL. Ships no Python dependencies of its own, which keeps it out of the uv workspace and lets one clone serve several profiles. Tested model behaviour is published in the README, including that gemini-3.8-live-extended-thinking accepts a function declaration and then delegates only about 2 times in 5, which is why gemini-3.8-live is the default. Disclosure — pressing Start captures microphone audio and streams it through the local backend to generativelanguage.googleapis.com using GEMINI_API_KEY from the Hermes home's .env; delegated work runs as a Hermes run in the serving profile's own memory with the profile's full toolset via the local api_server and API_SERVER_KEY, and those runs' results (up to 4000 characters each), the task board and approval prompts are sent back to Gemini as text. Nothing is sent anywhere else and no telemetry is emitted.

Realtime voice for Hermes through terminal, Discord, dashboard and Desktop. Live voice mode (TALK_VOICE_MODE=live, TALK_LIVE_AUTH=subscription) connects with your own Codex OAuth session to the undocumented chatgpt.com/backend-api/codex/realtime/calls endpoint, which is outside the vendor's published API terms and may change or stop working without notice.

Reasserts pinned standing instructions after context compaction. Disclosure — scope=global pins apply to every session sharing the same HERMES_HOME; memlock_setup.py edits config.yaml and .claude/settings.json (with backups) only when you run it.

Recall and save decisions, preferences and facts in your Kumiho Cloud workspace. Portable Agent Plugins v1 package with hosted OAuth MCP and six skills. Disclosure — connects to Kumiho's hosted MCP at https://mcp.kumiho.cloud/mcp (OAuth at control.kumiho.cloud, tokens held by Hermes); memory queries, including an automatic topic lookup near the start of relevant conversations, and approved captures are sent there; the server is marked `trust: untrusted`, so Hermes asks before every tool not annotated read-only. The optional backfill helper reads only files the user names and writes review packets to a new folder; Dream State can create a recurring Hermes cron task when asked (read-only by default). No local server, telemetry or background process.
Record a provisional claim or uncertainty before an evidence-gathering step, then link the actual observation to it.

Records each Hermes session on a UNITARES server you run: one identity per session and one check-in per completed turn, so the agent's working record carries across sessions. Fail-open; never blocks the agent. Disclosure — sends only to the server named in UNITARES_MCP_URL, which you host; there is no default server. Per session it sends your model name and platform; per completed turn a fixed check-in marker (never user, assistant or tool text). Hooks run synchronously, so an unresponsive server can delay a call by roughly 40 seconds (connection plus call timeout). After 3 consecutive failures the plugin stops reporting for that session only, until the session is finalized or reset; it stays fail-open and never blocks the agent. If UNITARES_BEARER is set, it is sent as a request header to that same server only.

Reduce Hermes tool-schema overhead and show selector savings in the dashboard. Disclosure — optional mode jev (off by default; needs TYPESAFE_API_KEY) sends each turn's request text and up to 32 candidate tool names and descriptions to TypeSafe (api.typesafe.ai); all other modes run locally. Optional user-run scripts can patch Hermes core on older Hermes and install a systemd user self-heal unit; the dashboard advisor edits the tool_slimmer section of config.yaml with a backup.

Reference another Hermes session in the Desktop composer with @session — type @ and pick from live session suggestions. Inserts a compact @session:"<title>" reference; nothing is injected into context, the agent resolves it with its own session-search. No more copying session IDs.

Reka as a Hermes model provider: Reka's agent-capable models on Reka's OpenAI-compatible API, each with its context window, tool support and image input declared, and reasoning effort sent as Reka's top-level reasoning_effort. Pick Reka in `hermes model` or use `--provider reka`. Disclosure — registers one model provider at import and nothing else (no tools, hooks, middleware, commands, background work or file access); chat requests (prompts, tool schemas and results, supported user images) and the model list go to https://api.reka.ai/v1 (or REKA_BASE_URL) through Hermes's own client with REKA_API_KEY, which Hermes reads; usage is billed to your Reka account; the plugin itself opens no connections.

Remote Telegram lifecycle notifications for the main Hermes agent: turn start, completion with a bounded final answer, interruption/failure, and user-facing approval requests. Suppresses subagent, Telegram-origin lifecycle, and automatic/smart-approval noise. Outbound-only, no input channel. Disclosure — enabled by default once installed and reuses the core Telegram gateway's TELEGRAM_BOT_TOKEN and TELEGRAM_HOME_CHANNEL when present, so each main-agent turn's final answer (up to 3,200 chars) and approval-request command text (up to 700 chars) from CLI, Desktop and eligible gateway platforms are sent to api.telegram.org for delivery to that one chat; Telegram-origin lifecycle and approval-prompt copies (and, when notify_on_approval_response is enabled, Telegram-origin approval-response copies) are suppressed because the core Telegram gateway already delivers them in that chat; token and state are stored 0600 under HERMES_HOME/telegram-notify.

Render a chart inline in the Hermes Desktop transcript: the model emits ::echarts{labels=... values=...} and the plugin mounts an interactive SVG chart (dataZoom slider, click-to-filter legend, resize-aware, 280-560px height clamp) in the plugin SDK's transcript-directive slot. Disclosure — no network calls, no shell commands, no stored credentials, no environment variables, no background processes, and nothing read or written outside the message it renders; the chart is drawn locally as inline SVG with no third-party libraries.

Requesty LLM gateway as a Hermes model provider (`--provider requesty`, alias `rq`, or Requesty in `hermes model`).
