The picker lists Requesty's managed routing policies (curated routes with failover, `@eu` variants for EU-only hosting); any Requesty model id or org policy also works. `/reasoning` maps onto Requesty's `reasoning_effort` for reasoning-capable models, the Hermes session id is sent as `requesty.trace_id`, and context windows and estimated cost come from the Requesty catalog. Prompt caching is done server-side by Requesty. Disclosure — chat requests go to https://router.requesty.ai/v1 (or REQUESTY_BASE_URL) through Hermes' own client with REQUESTY_API_KEY, which Hermes reads; the plugin itself only fetches Requesty's public model catalogs (/v1/models/managed and /v1/models, no credentials), once per process, sometimes on a short-lived background thread. No attribution headers, telemetry, file access or processes. Supersedes #27908.
Rescues oversized MCP and web tool results before they flood context.

Research competitor ads, clone the winners, and run campaigns through the hosted AdWhispr MCP. Finds brands verified to be advertising in a niche right now, their longest-running Meta and TikTok ads, Instagram content and Google keyword data; clones a proven ad into a finished image or AI video for your brand (free script approval before any credit is charged); and launches paused campaigns on Meta, Google, TikTok, X and ChatGPT Ads. Portable Agent Plugins v1 package with twenty-four workflow skills; OAuth uses pinned mcp-remote@0.1.49 over npx stdio, so Node.js 20.18.1+ and npm are required. Disclosure — creates and edits real ad campaigns that spend your ad budgets (always created paused, two-step confirm server-side) and renders videos that use paid credits; the AdWhispr server is marked untrusted, so Hermes asks before every write or spend tool and refuses them in cron and headless runs. Sends research queries and your brand assets to adwhispr.com; sign-in is OAuth through npx mcp-remote@0.1.49.
Research search for web_search and web_extract — papers, books, patents, standards and Wikipedia, with citable source links (Machine Library API key).

Resolve Hermes environment variables at startup from a single secret file encrypted with the Windows Data Protection API, instead of keeping provider keys in plaintext in .env or auth.json. Config is secrets.dpapi.map, an ENV_VAR -> store-name mapping (bare names or dpapi:// names) plus an optional file path (default <HERMES_HOME>/secrets.dpapi). The file is one DPAPI blob keyed by the current Windows user profile, so it is unreadable by another Windows account and worthless off the machine; it is written by the bundled CLI (python -m hermes_dpapi_secrets set NAME, value read from a prompt or stdin, never from argv) and only read at runtime. Mapped names that are missing or empty are skipped with a warning; a file that is not ours, a blob this user cannot decrypt, or a payload that is not a flat string map is reported as an error with nothing injected. Disclosure - this source decrypts a file for every Hermes process that enables it: resolved values become environment variables of the Hermes process and its children, exactly like .env entries, so anything that can read that environment can see them. User-scope encryption only (the machine-wide flag is never used and is not exposed), and the at-rest protection is a bar for backups, cloud sync and dotfiles, not a boundary against code already running as the same user. Stdlib-only (ctypes): no Python dependencies, no subprocesses, no network calls, no self-update. Windows only. Applying fetched values stays the orchestrator's job; the plugin never writes os.environ itself. Disclosure — decrypts a DPAPI-encrypted secret file (default <HERMES_HOME>/secrets.dpapi) at startup for every Hermes process that enables it, and the resolved values become environment variables of Hermes and its child processes like `.env` entries; the encryption is per Windows user and protects backups, cloud sync and copied files, not against other code running as the same user. Local only: no network calls, no subprocesses.

Resolve Hermes environment variables from the current user's Windows Credential Manager at startup, instead of keeping provider keys in plaintext in .env or auth.json. Config is secrets.wincred.map, an ENV_VAR -> generic-credential-target mapping (bare names or wincred:// names); each value is read with CredReadW in the current user's vault and handed to the secret-source orchestrator, which applies it with the usual precedence, provenance and conflict rules. Values may be UTF-8 or UTF-16LE (cmdkey and the Credential UI write UTF-16); anything that does not decode to text, or that contains interior NULs, is skipped with a warning instead of being injected as a mangled key. Disclosure - this source reads your Windows Credential Manager: only the generic credentials named in the map, with no enumeration of the vault. Resolved values become environment variables of the Hermes process and its children, exactly like .env entries, so anything that can read that environment can see them. The package is read-only and stdlib-only (ctypes): it never creates, updates or deletes credentials, writes no files, starts no subprocesses, makes no network calls and does not self-update. Windows only. Credential Manager is user-scoped, so this raises the at-rest bar for backups, cloud sync and dotfiles; it is not a boundary against code already running as the same user. Applying fetched values stays the orchestrator's job; the plugin never writes os.environ itself. Disclosure — when enabled, reads only the Windows Credential Manager generic credentials named in secrets.wincred.map (no vault enumeration) and injects them as environment variables of the Hermes process and its children, exactly like .env entries; read-only, stdlib ctypes, no subprocesses, no network, no file writes; user-scoped at-rest protection, not a boundary against code already running as the same user.

Reverse engineer programs with REA (rea.tools): native binaries, .NET assemblies, Electron/JavaScript apps, Android packages, firmware and browser/process activity, through REA's MCP server (pinned rea-agents@6.7.0 over npx stdio) with REA's reverse-engineer-anything skill adapted for Hermes. Portable Agent Plugins v1 package (mcp.json + skills/); needs Node.js 22.19+/24.11+/26+ on PATH, plus your own Ghidra, Hopper or IDA for native decompilation. Disclosure — a few REA tools run a command under a PTY, launch or drive an application, change a connected Android device or overwrite a chosen file, and Hermes does not prompt before them; the bundled skill tells the agent to ask first and to skip them in unattended runs.
Review and approve exact text-artifact writes through a local DeadBolt sidecar. Protects this plugin's commit tool only.

Review boards for UI mockups. The agent builds a board from a decisions.json file and your prototype pages; you open it on desktop or phone, mark each decision approve, change or skip, pin comments on the mocks and press Send, and your agent wakes up with the feedback as a markdown digest. Four mock_review tools, the `hermes mockreview` CLI and slash command, and a bundled usage skill. Boards are served from your computer (loopback by default, or your tailnet) or published on here.now. Disclosure — when autostart is on (off until `hermes mockreview setup`), a board web server (127.0.0.1:8790 by default) and one worker thread run inside the gateway process; setting host to 0.0.0.0 exposes every review to your network with no login. Outbound calls: a signed POST to the local Hermes webhook (localhost:8644) on Send, and, only for reviews hosted on here.now, https://here.now/api/v1 with your HERENOW_API_KEY. Secrets are read through Hermes's secret scope only. Runs `bash publish.sh` from the official here-now skill (key in the child environment), `tailscale status --json` and `tailscale serve status --json` (read only; on macOS the Tailscale app's own binary if the symlink crashes) for tailnet hosting, and from `setup` the hermes subcommands `--version`, `gateway status`, `config get/set/unset`, `webhook subscribe`, `webhook remove` (only for a stale self-delivering route, after you confirm) and `plugins validate`. Reviews are stored under $HERMES_HOME/workspace/mock-reviews. No telemetry, no update check, no Python dependencies.
Review pending Hermes memory writes and inspect, add, edit, delete, or AI-compact stored memory from Desktop.
Rewrite a composer draft outside the chat and put the finished prompt back in the field. A prompt library keeps saved prompts, and a one-call model pick does not change the session.

Rich, evidence-backed answer cards — tables, charts, metrics, timelines, sources — rendered inline in the desktop transcript Disclosure — Image and ImageGallery cards load agent-supplied https image URLs (up to 8 per gallery) from any host when the card renders in Desktop
Ring when a Hermes turn finishes so you can leave the window. OS notification, optional chime, and a busy/done chip. Optional "needs you" when approval is waiting. No API keys.

Rocket.Chat gateway adapter for Hermes Agent. Connects to a self-hosted Rocket.Chat instance via the REST API v1 for outbound traffic and the Realtime (DDP) WebSocket for inbound messages. Uses aiohttp (already a Hermes dependency) — no extra packages needed.

Rooms where AI agents of any vendor talk to each other. A room is a URL; agents join, read and post over plain HTTP, with no accounts and no sign-in. Portable Agent Plugins v1 package: the parlor skill plus the hosted parlor MCP server (Streamable HTTP, no authentication, 8 tools). Disclosure — hosted unauthenticated MCP connector at parlor.sh/mcp (tool set is server-controlled, not pinned) plus a curl fallback; messages the agent writes go to parlor.sh or the server in a given room URL and rooms are public to anyone with the link; room tokens are stored under ~/.local/state/parlor; the skill may keep background wait loops running.

Rotate the focused session reasoning effort from the status bar. A dialog sets the levels, colors, and per-level prompt limits. Disclosure — changes the focused session's reasoning effort through the gateway config.set API (core may fall back to writing the global config.yaml when the session id is stale) and auto-demotes the level after the configured number of prompts.

Routes selected Hermes auxiliary tasks (approval, MCP sampling, compression) through bounded Jev decision calls on OpenRouter instead of free-form chat prompts, failing open to the operator's own auxiliary provider for anything it cannot express as a decision. Disclosure — sends redacted approval prompts, MCP tool names and compression transcript blocks to openrouter.ai using your OpenRouter key (read-only); on any error approvals escalate to you, never auto-approve; the default decision_model is a moving alias, pin it.

RuAPI as Hermes model providers on one key: `ruapi` serves Claude models over RuAPI's native Anthropic Messages API (so Hermes' Anthropic prompt caching and thinking apply), and `ruapi-openai` serves GPT, Gemini, DeepSeek, GLM, Qwen, Kimi and other chat models over its OpenAI-compatible API. Each /model picker lists that side's chat models from the account's GET /v1/models list, leaving out image and video models, and context windows and image input are declared for the main models. Maintained by RuAPI. Disclosure — registers two model providers at import and nothing else (no tools, hooks, commands or threads). Prompts, tool schemas and RUAPI_API_KEY go to https://www.ruapi.ai (/v1/messages and /v1/chat/completions) through Hermes' own clients, and RuAPI forwards each request to the upstream vendor serving the model. The model list is Hermes' standard GET https://www.ruapi.ai/v1/models request with the key; the plugin makes no network requests of its own, adds no headers, sends no telemetry, reads or writes no files and stores no credentials.

Rug-pull detection for installed agent skills — fingerprints every file in every skill directory (SHA-256), keeps a profile-local snapshot, and reports exactly which skill files changed, appeared, or vanished since; a skill that mutates after install without the user touching it is the rug-pull signal. A skill directory made unreadable is reported as a finding, never treated as clean. Read-only observer, stdlib-only, zero network calls; blind spots (oversize files, symlinks, permission-denied) are counted and printed, never silent. The wrapper registers an hourly pre_llm_call hook that injects findings into the agent context, plus a /skill-integrity slash command (snapshot | check | show) that creates the baseline snapshot and shows the file-level diff. The CLI supports --state-dir to target the plugin's manifest directly. Skill dirs and state derive from get_hermes_home(), covering non-default profiles. Disclosure — reads (hash-only, read-only) every file under the active profile's skills directory and ~/.claude/skills, stores a mode-0600 snapshot in HERMES_HOME/plugin-data/skill-integrity, and at most hourly injects the names of changed skills into the agent's context.

Rule-based proofreading for Japanese business text: finds and fixes AI-style phrasing (stock phrases, monotonous sentence endings, overused symbols and Markdown, English-calque grammar) with line, column and a fix hint. It checks wording, not authorship, and rarely flags plain model output. A transform_llm_output hook checks every final Japanese answer and only reports by default; opt-in enforce mode rewrites flagged answers with the user's own model and delivers the rewrite only if numbers, names, URLs, code and negation survive and the score drops under the threshold. Disclosure: no network calls of its own; enforce mode sends each flagged answer to the user's configured model (one extra call, a second only when the first rewrite fails the checks or stays over the threshold; extra cost and up to 25 s delay); a read-only post_tool_call hook notes turns with MEDIA: lines so attachments from other plugins are kept; reports stay in process memory on local surfaces only. Disclosure — no network calls of its own; mode report (default) only logs scores; opt-in mode enforce sends each flagged final answer (with finding excerpts) to the user's configured model via ctx.llm (1–3 calls, up to 25 s delay) and replaces the delivered and stored answer when its preservation checks pass, which do not prove meaning is unchanged; reads plugins.hook_callback_timeout via a private read-only Hermes helper; eval/ dev scripts ship in the tree but are never loaded.

Run Google Ads, Meta Ads, TikTok Ads, LinkedIn Ads, GA4, Shopify, HubSpot and 50+ more platforms through Markifact's hosted MCP server. Portable Agent Plugins v1 package with ten skills (operating protocol, write-safety rules, campaign launch, creative rotation, negative sweeps, diagnosis); remote streamable-http with OAuth 2.1 and dynamic client registration, so no Node.js or API keys. Disclosure: creates and edits real ad campaigns that spend your ad budgets; every write is a separate approval-gated operation and the skills instruct confirm-before-spend, but that is enforced by the skills and the server's approval flag, not by Hermes.

Run Hermes as an MCP server: `hermes mcp-serve` lets any MCP client (Claude Code, Claude Desktop, Cursor, Codex) list and read your messaging conversations, poll live events, send messages and answer approvals over stdio. `--tools` (off by default) also exposes Hermes' web, browser, vision, image generation, skills and TTS tools; terminal, file and kanban tools are never exposed. Formerly built into Hermes core as `hermes mcp serve` (MCP clients change their args to ["mcp-serve"]). Disclosure — the connecting MCP client reads the active profile's conversation history (state.db) and can send messages as your connected platform accounts; with `--tools` it also runs Hermes tools under your configured provider credentials, which can spend provider credits. The plugin itself makes no network or model calls beyond those tool calls and sends.

Run Hermes on a Google Antigravity subscription through the official agy CLI, with agy as the model only: a generated custom agent removes agy's built-in tools, Hermes tools are exposed through an inventory-only MCP server with native function calling, and every tool call is handed back to Hermes. Fails closed on any non-Hermes tool step or silent agent fallback; pre-warms agy for fast tool loops. Disclosure — routes inference through Google's official agy CLI and counts against the Antigravity/Gemini subscription agy is signed in to; the plugin never reads, copies or links agy's credential files. agy runs in your real HOME with the gateway's environment; by default the plugin moves the agy conversation records created by its own idle pre-warmed processes under ~/.gemini/antigravity-cli/ to the trash (trash-put from PATH; ANTIGRAVITY_AGY_CLEANUP=off disables) and pre-warms up to 4 idle agy processes (~400 MB each).

Run Hermes on an Antigravity subscription via the official agy CLI (DirectSDK path). Streams tokens progressively, persists multi-turn trajectories via agy --conversation (up to 239k tokens), discovers models dynamically per account, maps thinking effort, reports quota in /usage, and aborts reported native tools. Disclosure — routes inference and /usage quota reads through Google's official agy CLI under your subscription (usage counts against it); links (symlink, else hardlink/copy) the antigravity-oauth-token into a per-session private temp HOME deleted on close; probes OS keyring presence (Linux Secret Service, macOS Keychain, Windows Credential Manager) without reading secrets; on macOS symlinks ~/Library/Keychains for CLI session reuse; never writes to vendor credential stores; strips credential-looking environment variables before spawning agy (name heuristic; ANTIGRAVITY_ENV_STRICT for an allow-list). Disclosure — the opt-in ANTIGRAVITY_DEBUG_PROMPT_DIR env var writes every outgoing prompt (full conversation text) to that directory.

Run Hermes terminal commands in an existing remote Coder workspace. Disclosure — runs terminal commands inside your Coder workspace at CODER_URL using CODER_API_KEY; starts a stopped workspace automatically; forwards only the env vars you list in TERMINAL_CODER_FORWARD_ENV.

Run Hermes terminal, file and execute_code tools in Cloudflare Containers, with the workspace saved to a snapshot when idle. Disclosure — you deploy the bundled Cloudflare Worker to your own account first; running containers is billed by Cloudflare; commands and file contents run in the container at HERMES_CF_ENDPOINT using HERMES_CF_TOKEN; the container has outbound internet by default (ENABLE_INTERNET); host env vars, skills and credentials are not copied into the container; dangerous-command approval stays on.

Run Hermes' built-in browser tools on Browserless cloud browsers: stealth mode, residential proxies, captcha solving and ad blocking, with no local Chrome. One Browserless browser per task; Hermes' agent-browser daemon and CDP supervisor share it through a local CDP multiplexer, and the browser is reconnected after network drops and closed when the task ends. Disclosure — while a browser task runs, starts a background thread with a WebSocket listener on 127.0.0.1 (random port, secret path, local Host header only); connects to Browserless (production-*.browserless.io) with BROWSERLESS_TOKEN, read via get_secret; Browserless usage is metered on your plan, and residential proxy traffic costs more; connections to Browserless carry a browserless-hermes-plugin/<version> User-Agent so Browserless can count plugin usage (opt-out: BROWSERLESS_SOURCE_TAG=false; the browser's own user agent is unchanged); no files written unless BROWSERLESS_MUX_LOG is set; no other telemetry.

Run Hermes' terminal tools inside an existing WSL distro on Windows: one bash -c per command as the distro's default user, over the same files Windows sees at /mnt/<drive>, with no Docker Desktop, no image and no container to start or tear down. A host cwd is translated (C:\Users\me\proj becomes /mnt/c/Users/me/proj, \\wsl.localhost paths become the distro's own paths) and the mount root is asked once with wslpath, so a distro that moved its automount point still gets correct paths. cwd persists across commands, stdin and exit codes ride through wsl.exe, and hermes doctor / setup and the dashboard picker get real rows (wsl.exe path, WSL version, distros present, selected distro). HERMES_WSL_DISTRO and HERMES_WSL_USER select the distro and the user. Disclosure — this is a full-access backend, not a sandbox: when it is the selected backend, everything the terminal tool runs executes as your user inside your distro, with that distro's files, permissions and network access, so dangerous-command approval stays on and Hermes never stops the distro. The plugin itself reads no credentials, stores nothing and makes no network calls; it spawns wsl.exe per command and wslpath once per distro. It rewrites one core-produced string, the trailing cwd marker, because under WSL a command substitution is handed the directory wsl.exe started in rather than the shell's current one (measurements in the repo's VALIDATION.md); nothing in Hermes is patched or rebound at runtime.

Run Hermes' terminal, file and execute_code tools in a Linux container on Microsoft's WSL Containers (wslc) runtime, so Windows users who run WSL Containers get a sandbox without Docker Desktop. Disclosure — the plugin spawns the wslc CLI (one short-lived process per command, plus one long-lived container per environment) and every call runs inside that container; containers have outbound network access unless docker_network is false; persistent sandboxes are left stopped on disk until removed; host environment variables enter the container only when named in docker_forward_env, and only paths listed in docker_volumes are bind-mounted. wslc rejects --cap-drop, --security-opt, --pids-limit, --init and --storage-opt, so this sandbox is not capability-dropped the way the Docker backend's is, container_disk is reported but not enforced, and dangerous-command approval deliberately stays enabled for this backend. The plugin reads no credentials, stores none, and makes no network calls of its own.
Run the Hermes terminal interface in a Hermes Desktop workspace tab.

Runcrate (runcrate.ai) open models via the OpenAI-compatible API at api.runcrate.ai/v1: live model list from /v1/models, DeepSeek V4.1 Flash as the default, and Hermes reasoning settings sent as reasoning_effort. Disclosure: model provider; prompts, tool schemas and RUNCRATE_API_KEY go to api.runcrate.ai, and free requests can be served by third-party model providers under their own terms (runcrate.ai/privacy).

Runtime guardrails, behavioral evaluation, and signed fleet admission for Hermes Agent: a versioned capability policy that blocks or requires approval for model tool calls, paired synthetic behavioral evaluation with no real side effects, and a signed local promotion gate that refuses a model whose evidence does not satisfy signed fleet policy. Hooks-only (no agent tools). Disclosure — Adds approval prompts to tool calls by default (balanced mode): every MCP, connector or other-plugin tool, memory and skill writes, file reads outside the working and temp directories, and network-capable terminal/code commands go to Hermes's approval prompt; strict mode blocks them instead, and opt-in enforced fleet mode blocks all tool calls until the served model name matches the admitted one. The user-run `hermes antidote eval run` command sends synthetic prompts (and the API key you name) to the OpenAI-compatible endpoint you pass, as billed model calls (default suite up to ~170 requests); `model inspect hf:` queries huggingface.co; `fleet keygen` writes unencrypted Ed25519 private keys (mode 0600) to paths you choose.

SMS gateway adapter for Hermes Agent via Twilio. Sends and receives SMS through the Twilio REST API + inbound webhook, relaying texts between phone numbers and the Hermes agent. Markdown is stripped to plain text.

Safe AI Labs as a Hermes model provider (`--provider safeailabs`, or Safe AI Labs in `hermes model`): an OpenAI-compatible API with one endpoint per region, the model list from its /v1/models and the context window of its fallback model declared. Disclosure — registers one model provider at import and nothing else (no tools, hooks, commands or threads); chat requests and the model list go to https://us.api.safeailabs.ai/v1 (or SAFE_AI_BASE_URL) through Hermes' own client with SAFE_AI_KEY, which Hermes reads; the plugin itself opens no connections, reads and writes no files and starts no processes.

Saved chat prompts — click a tray item to insert it into the Hermes composer. Review / Plan / Explain defaults, then your own. No API keys. Disclosure — inserts prompts through Hermes Desktop's internal hermes:composer-insert event (not a public SDK API); stores prompts in $HERMES_HOME/plugin-data/prompt-tray/prompts.json; no network.

Say "make me a <role>" and your agent spawns a complete Bot Mode Bot — name, face, SOUL.md, memory, tools, skills, routines, gateway — tested, with rollback. Then hire a whole crew in one call, ask what is waiting on you, and edit, teach, share and health-check Bots by chatting. Disclosure — spawns the hermes CLI to create and run Bot profiles under HERMES_HOME/profiles/, and installs its own small companion hook plugin (bot-forge-marks, two hooks, no tools) into each Bot profile it manages, enabling it in that profile's config.yaml; never the root profile. Disclosure — when a Bot journals a blocked/failed entry, the plugin emails its title and summary to your own address via the SMTP account in Hermes' EMAIL_* settings (TLS verified; off with notify_blocked or notify_email false); adopt_bots (off by default) installs the companion hook into every profile on load.

Scan code (SAST), dependencies, container images, IaC and SBOMs with Snyk through its first-party MCP server (pinned snyk@1.1306.0 over npx stdio, CLI analytics disabled), with the snyk-security-scan workflow skill bundled. Portable Agent Plugins v1 package (mcp.json + skills/); needs Node.js/npm on PATH and a free Snyk account (browser login via the snyk_auth tool).

Scheduled check that the model you use in Hermes has not quietly got worse: 34 fixed, exactly graded questions (reasoning, instruction following, Japanese, plus your own) run through Hermes cron, each run tested against the same model's own baseline with an exact per-question test and a same-day confirmation run, and a message only for a confirmed drop, a changed served model or a failed measurement. Not yet tried against a real LLM API (checked with a local mock model and real Hermes cron). Disclosure — each check calls your own model through ctx.llm on your bill, capped per check by the plugin (default 120,000 tokens / $0.50, no daily cap; the agent can start checks itself via the model_drift tool, and the scheduled agent turn is extra); price lookup goes through Hermes's pricing code (may fetch OpenRouter/models.dev prices); 10 optional code questions, off by default, run model-written Python in a limited child process (not a hostile-code sandbox) including in unattended cron runs when enabled; `schedule` creates one Hermes cron job that survives plugin removal (run `unschedule` first); writes run history to plugin-data/model-drift-watch; no telemetry.
Scholarly search, citation traversal, grouped counts, and fulltext access through OpenAlex with session spending limits.
Screens user turns and blocks downstream tools on a BLOCK verdict; the original prompt still reaches the model.
SearXNG web search — free, self-hosted, privacy-respecting metasearch engine. Requires SEARXNG_URL pointing at your instance.

Search and book real flights and hotels through the hosted LetsFG MCP server (Streamable HTTP, OAuth 2.1 + DCR), with the letsfg travel-booking workflow skill bundled: fares across airlines and the major travel sites, flexible dates, destinations in a region, bookable hotel rates, then book, follow and stop bookings. Portable Agent Plugins v1 package (skills/ only; the server is added by the sign-in command below). Disclosure — hosted-only connector with no local code: every tool call goes to the vendor's remote MCP server at letsfg.co/mcp. Booking tools act on real money: a booking holds the price on the card saved on the user's LetsFG account (captured only once the airline or hotel confirms, released if it fails); per LetsFG, a booking, paid extra or hotel cancellation starts only when the user presses Approve in an e-mail from LetsFG, never from the conversation, and Hermes itself does not prompt before these tools unless you set `trust: untrusted` on the letsfg MCP server. Card details are only ever entered on letsfg.co, never in the conversation. Traveller details given for a booking (name, date of birth, gender, passport, contact, address) are sent to LetsFG and saved on that account. The server and its OAuth sign-in are added with `hermes mcp add letsfg --url https://letsfg.co/mcp --auth oauth --connect-timeout 300`.

Search archived coding conversations and retrieve exact session revisions through the separately installed Agent Vault macOS app. Launches the app's existing MCP server through sh; reads the authorized archive through its local daemon. Vault handles storage-provider traffic. No bundled binaries, telemetry, credential-file reads, self-updater, or new background service. Disclosure — launches the separately installed Agent Vault app's own bundled Node MCP server (/Applications/Agent Vault.app or VAULT_APP_PATH) through sh with your VAULT_MCP_TOKEN binding token; that server code ships with the app, not in this repository. Its tools return archived conversations from Cursor, Codex, Claude Code and Hermes stored under ~/.vault (or VAULT_HOME) into the model's context, which is sent to your model provider. The app handles its own storage-provider traffic; the plugin adds no telemetry, network calls, credential-file reads or background service.

Search hotels (3M+ hotels) and flights worldwide on MAQAMI, read hotel details and reviews, then send the customer a secure checkout link on book.maqami.co, through the official MAQAMI Travel MCP server (Streamable HTTP at mcp.maqami.co, no account or key), with the maqami-travel-booking skill bundled. Portable Agent Plugins v1 package (mcp.json + skills/). Disclosure — connects to the hosted MAQAMI MCP server at mcp.maqami.co (no key); its tool list is defined by that server, not by the pinned repo. The tool arguments the agent sends go to it: destinations, dates, guests, lead-guest nationality and currency, plus booking ID and email for lookups, amendments and cancellations. Prebook (hotels) and verify (flights) hold a real rate, and the amend and cancel tools change or cancel real bookings (late or non-refundable cancellations are still charged); the skill tells the agent to show the details and get a clear yes before each prebook, amend or cancel. Customers pay only on book.maqami.co; no tool takes card or passport details.

Search mybot.farm, plant/reinstall Hermes packs (Desktop Recruit + CLI), and post GAF listings. Disclosure — plants third-party Hermes profiles (config, SOUL, skills, memories) from mybot.farm sellers with no hash pinning; force/clean delete profiles.

Search one index you run and watch one saved query, with index_search, index_health and index_watch. Disclosure — Sends MEILI_API_KEY as a Bearer token to your MEILI_HOST. Over plain http that key travels unencrypted, and a master or admin key is sent as given, so use a search-only key. The tools are on for every surface, including gateways: anyone you allow on your Hermes gateway can search with your key and approve a watch. Turn a surface off with hermes tools. index_watch schedule creates one cron job that runs a model turn every 15 minutes (two or more model requests when it calls the tool) with no daily cap, and it watches only the first 20 hits. The job stays after uninstall until you run hermes cron remove, with -p and the profile name when the profile is not default. Scheduling and unscheduling ask for Hermes approval every time and are refused under cron, yolo, approvals off, unattended sessions and plugins.isolation: host, where the watch only posts a notice that it cannot run, on every run. Answering "always" adds an unused line to config.yaml. The watch relies on private parts of Hermes, so an update can stop it.

Search products, services and shops listed on GenesisPay and read their verified-purchase reviews through the hosted, read-only GenesisPay Catalog MCP server (Streamable HTTP at https://catalog.genesispay.finance/mcp/catalog, no sign-in, no key), with a catalog skill bundled. Portable Agent Plugins v1 package (mcp.json + skills/), no Python or executables. Disclosure — network calls to catalog.genesispay.finance, operated by GenesisPay (Genesis Technologies): search terms, filters and ids reach that server; no credentials are stored; all four tools are read-only and none pays, orders or changes anything; the tool set is served by the remote MCP server at runtime and is not covered by the pinned sha.

Search the public web, read pages as Markdown, crawl sites, and convert documents in Hermes. No API key required. Disclosure — search queries, submitted URLs and explicitly approved local file uploads go to the public markdown.new service; needs the companion markdown-new CLI (uv tool install from the same repo tag), which the plugin runs as a subprocess with the Hermes process environment.

Search, extract, map, crawl, and research through Tavily hosted MCP, with Tavily skills. The default connection requires TAVILY_API_KEY; supports Hermes-managed OAuth through a native MCP override. Disclosure — Connects to Tavily's hosted MCP server at `mcp.tavily.com` and sends it the search queries, URLs and research prompts the agent issues, authenticated with `TAVILY_API_KEY` or a Hermes-managed Tavily OAuth sign-in.

Secret source plugin that resolves environment variables from an Infisical secret store (cloud or self-hosted) at Hermes startup. Registers a mapped source ("infisical", inf:// references) and a bulk source ("infisical_bulk").

Secret-leak protection for Hermes chats. Scans inbound messages and outbound replies for API keys, tokens, and passwords with a 28-pattern detector registry, redacts them before they reach session storage or the user, and injects safe secret-handling rules so the agent never asks for secrets in chat. Zero dependencies, fully offline detection; pairs with the optional hermes-vault CLI for encrypted storage. Disclosure — rewrites inbound user messages (regex secret redaction, may false-positive on password-like strings), injects a secret-handling prompt each conversation and rewrites assistant replies that ask for secrets; outbound replies are value-redacted with the same registry (regex-based, so a shape no detector covers passes through), with findings logged as detector name plus SHA-256 fingerprint and never the raw value. The vaultknox tool is inert unless the separate vaultknox pip package is installed, its write gate is a tool argument the model sets, and a vault policy that authorises raw consume_token returns the plaintext to the model.

Security for agents: checks every tool call and model request before it runs against a curated, verifiable threat graph (prompt injection, dangerous commands, malicious packages, unsafe skills, phishing and drainer indicators) and local rules that keep an agent away from wallet stores, seed phrases, private keys and exchange API keys. Audit mode records; block mode refuses. Can share privacy-safe threat reports with an open community graph once the user turns sharing on (off by default); community findings only ever flag. Hooks only: no tools, no middleware. Disclosure — hooks see every tool call and model request; `hermes blackbox setup` installs Node (via a checksum-pinned nvm installer) if missing, the OriginTrail DKG node from npm (checksum-pinned) and Blazegraph in Docker or Oxigraph, registers the DKG node and the dashboard as login services (systemd/LaunchAgent), and joins the DKG peer-to-peer network; package installs are looked up on api.osv.dev (name and version); community threat reports signed by a local reporter key (threat identifiers, including domains of fetched pages that served a verified injection) are shared to the community graph only after you turn sharing on (off by default); the optional LLM reviewer sends the current turn's user and tool text to OpenAI or Anthropic; `blackbox attach` copies the plugin into the Hermes homes/profiles and OpenClaw workspaces you name and enables it in their config (automatic attaching is off unless you set `auto_attach: true`); `hermes blackbox chat` creates an `agent-blackbox` profile cloned from the current one (config.yaml and .env); the dashboard runs on 127.0.0.1:9700.

Security guardrails for Hermes tool calls: per-call authorization, so a prompt injection cannot make the agent do more than you allowed. Each call is checked against a signed, expiring permission slip (a warrant) before the handler runs, down to the arguments (file paths, search queries, spending limits), and every decision lands in a local audit log. Give cron jobs, delegate_task subagents and gateway users their own policy.
Disclosure — hermes-tenuo is a no-op until a warrant is configured and blocks every tool call in a kanban worker that has no per-task warrant; it appends every tool call's name and full arguments to $HERMES_HOME/tenuo/audit.jsonl (disable with audit_log: false); when TENUO_CONNECT_TOKEN or TENUO_CONTROL_PLANE_URL are set, the bundled tenuo SDK (compiled Rust core) streams those decisions, including arguments, to that control plane.

Selection-definition lookup for Hermes Desktop. Select any text, get an AI definition with sources in a popup. Renders the definition inline, runnable code aside. Backend is a stateless hermes insight CLI; panel, providers, and one-click model picking are configurable. Disclosure — definitions are generated with your configured provider keys (the selected term, your format template and optional web-search results are sent to that provider) via a short-lived `hermes insight` CLI run; no background process remains. When web search is on it also queries your configured searxng instance and fetches result thumbnails from their image hosts, inlining them into the panel; nothing is fetched without a searxng URL.

Self-hosted AI investment committee — skills for portfolio review, a decision ledger, and a 4-role LLM committee (macro / quant / risk / CIO) that debates a symbol. Disclosure — the skills run the openinvest backend from PyPI via uvx (pinned in run.sh) and keep portfolio, ledger, committee records and any keys you add in plaintext under ~/openInvest (or $INVEST_HOME); it fetches public market data and RSS news, and on the Direct path / daily report sends your portfolio and wealth context to the LLM you configure (default api.deepseek.com) and, if installed, to the agy or gemini CLI for a second opinion; news ingestion can trigger extra committee runs (LLM spend). The MCP tools are a server you add to config.yaml yourself (the printed snippet runs the plugin's pinned run.sh with `trust: untrusted`, so Hermes asks before ledger writes); buy/sell/deposit/withdraw only edit the local ledger — it never connects to a broker or places orders.

Self-hosted long-term memory through a post-cortex daemon (https://github.com/julymetodiev/post-cortex): typed records (decisions, fixed problems, code changes) in an entity graph with local semantic search. Recalls related records from the profile's workspace before each turn, puts the user card and the workspace's project card in the system prompt, mirrors built-in memory writes as records, and adds post_cortex_search, post_cortex_record and post_cortex_context (graph neighbours and reverse dependencies of named components) plus the post-cortex:memory skill. Records and captured turns carry the author hermes:<profile>. Profiles are mapped to shared workspaces by name glob, so a team of profiles recalls each other's records. Disclosure — talks only to the post-cortex daemon at the configured URL (default http://127.0.0.1:3737; a remote daemon over plain HTTP should sit on a private network or behind TLS): each non-trivial user prompt (up to 2,000 characters) is sent as a search query, and built-in memory writes and post_cortex_record calls are sent as records; with the opt-in capture setting (off by default) each completed turn of the primary agent is sent too: the user's message (with the sender's display name when Hermes knows it), the final reply, tool names and file paths, never tool output; nothing goes to third parties. Disclosure — the daemon stores records (and captured turns, deleted after its message_retention_days) in its own database and redacts credentials, e-mail addresses, phone numbers and public IPv4 addresses on write. Disclosure — PCX_TOKEN (and optionally PCX_URL) is read through the Hermes secret scope; the only local state is $HERMES_HOME/post-cortex.json (0600, never holds the token). No threads or processes of its own (capture runs on Hermes' sync worker), no shell commands, no deletes in post-cortex; cron and subagent runs never write automatically.

Self-hosted vector memory (Qdrant + TurboQuant compression) with auto-discovered knowledge realms, semantic search across conversations and ingested documents, and a slumber pipeline for memory consolidation. v1.1.0 adds optional per-session injection dedup with char-budget gate, decision/evaluation memory-type promotion (slower decay for load-bearing turns), prompt-injection sanitization on read, configurable system-prompt template, export/import memories as JSON, and a /memex8 slash command. New memory behaviours are opt-in; /memex8 export|import is confined to $HERMES_HOME/plugin-data/memex8 unless enable_export_import=true. Disclosure — auto-stores a truncated copy (first 300 chars) of every user and assistant turn, plus per-message previews of the whole transcript at session end and before context compression, to the memex8 server at MEMEX8_BASE_URL (self-hosted; default http://localhost:8080) using MEMEX8_API_KEY.
Self-memory and replacement models for Hermes agents. Remember your work. Train your replacement.

Self-owned long-term memory backed by the agent-memory-es service (Elasticsearch). Three agent tools — recall, retain, reflect — over episodic/ semantic/procedural tiers with hybrid BM25+kNN recall and server-enforced private/team/common visibility. Requires a running agent-memory-es instance. Disclosure — each user prompt (as a recall query), each user message and Hermes memory writes are sent to the agent-memory-es service at AMES_SERVICE_URL (default localhost:8123) with AMES_SERVICE_KEY; the model may store facts in shared team/common visibility tiers.
Sendblue iMessage / SMS integration. Provides typing indicators, async daemon routing, and Active LLM Tools for SMS dispatch.
SerpApi web, Maps, News, Shopping, Hotels, Flights, and Travel Explore for Hermes Agent.
Serply web search provider for Hermes Agent. Google web results via the Serply SERP API. Requires SERPLY_API_KEY (sign up at https://serply.io).

Session Analyzer — per-session analytics for the Hermes desktop app: full page at /session-dashboard with token/cache/cost aggregates, tool-call breakdown, file changes, failure groups, and Ask AI (copies a ready-to-run analysis prompt into a fresh draft chat). Read-only over state.db.

Session command tray — shell commands the Hermes agent ran via the terminal tool (success and failure). Desktop pane and /commands. No API keys. Disclosure — records terminal commands with exit code, workdir and a 160-char redacted output preview to $HERMES_HOME/plugin-data/command-tray/state.json; the Desktop pane inserts text through Hermes Desktop's internal hermes:composer-insert event (not a public SDK API) with clipboard fallback; no network.
Session file tray — paths the Hermes agent touched via read_file, write_file, or patch. Desktop pane and /files. No API keys.

Session pane for Hermes Desktop: Firefox-style session groups with project grouping, list/grid views, Ctrl+Scroll session cycling with a HUD, session-row styling and a built-in settings page. All timers are ctx-owned intervals disposed on unload (live-session poll ~30 s, session refresh ~45 s, project cache 60 s, activity expiry 30 s). The standalone full build in this repo (full/plugin.js, install.sh) is not part of this catalog entry. Contact: info@agantila.com. Disclosure — SDK-only Desktop plugin: reads the local Hermes gateway through public RPCs (projects.tree, projects.list, session.list, session.active_list, session.context_breakdown) and, on your actions, writes through public RPCs (projects.create/update/add_folder/remove_folder/set_primary/set_active/delete, session.create, session.cwd.set, session.title, session.branch_stored, session.archive, session.close, session.delete); captures Ctrl+mouse-wheel across the app (browser zoom suppressed except over canvases, editors and zoomable images) to cycle sessions; settings and groups stay in the app's local plugin storage; no outbound network, no shell commands, no credentials, no self-update.
Session source tray — URLs the Hermes agent opened via web_search, web_extract, or browser_navigate. Desktop pane and /sources. No search backend of its own and no API keys.
Set a color for each session and show an idle glyph to make rows easier to scan.

Set up and diagnose Moonlight game streaming (Sunshine host <-> Moonlight client) between machines that run Hermes. One tool, action-based: discover hosts on the tailnet/LAN, preflight ports, install+start Sunshine, pair clients, verify encoders, and launch a stream. Writes to remote machines only over SSH and only when the action says so. Disclosure — runs shell commands as your user on this machine and, over SSH, on hosts you name (BatchMode, your existing keys); `install` runs `sudo` with your package manager to install `sunshine` or `moonlight-qt` without a Hermes approval prompt; `configure`/`start` rewrite Sunshine's config (with a backup) and restart its user service; `discover` reads `tailscale status` and port-probes your tailnet peers; `launch` starts a Moonlight process. No credentials stored, no telemetry.
Setup helper for managed Pubky agents. The launcher syncs agent state, including conversation database snapshots and portable configuration, to your remote Pubky homeserver.

Seven read-only tools. Disclosure — Seven read-only tools for Gensyn Delphi prediction markets; no funds move and nothing is signed or sent. Needs Node.js 20.18+ and a manual `npm ci --ignore-scripts` in the plugin folder (installs the pinned @gensyn-ai/gensyn-delphi-sdk and its locked npm deps) before the tools work. Runs a local Node subprocess per call (25 s deadline, not a sandbox). Sends your DELPHI_API_ACCESS_KEY only to delphi-api.gensyn.ai (testnet) or api.delphi.fyi (mainnet); history and quotes read api.goldsky.com and gensyn-testnet/mainnet.g.alchemy.com without the key, and quotes use a throwaway in-memory key the SDK requires. Tools are on for every surface by default, including messaging gateways, where anyone admitted can run these reads on the owner's key (rate limit 30 requests per minute per process); disable per surface with `hermes tools`.

Share Hermes Desktop conversations as long PNG screenshots, self-contained HTML, or Markdown — per-turn selection, turn gutter, search, per-turn collapsing and session metadata. The Hermes Desktop counterpart of dsh-share. Disclosure — makes no network calls; reads the conversation you share (and the session list, for its title) through the gateway's session.history / session.info / session.list RPCs; writes to the clipboard or downloads a file only when you trigger an export. HTML exports keep the conversation's image and link URLs, which load when the file is opened.

Shared fleet memory for Hermes agents: every connected agent learns from all other agents connected to the memory, wherever they run. Sessions across machines and harnesses are distilled into one common brain overnight — what one learns, the whole fleet recalls. Pushes a compact per-turn recall index (entries lazy-load via hicortex_get), injects fresh lessons plus a per-agent standing context block at session start — lesson blocks are delimited and carry an explicit reference-data framing line and provenance header — and exposes the full 9-tool memory surface (search, get, recent, ingest, lessons, index, graph, update, delete) through the shared server. The same server also serves Claude Code, OpenClaw, Pi and opencode agents, so mixed-harness fleets share one brain. Stdlib-only, no pip dependencies. Requires a running Hicortex server (npx @gamaze/hicortex init on any machine); data flow: each user message is sent to your configured Hicortex server for recall (default http://localhost:8787); session distillation runs on the server. Disclosure — sends every user message (and profile name) to your configured Hicortex server each turn for recall, default http://localhost:8787, plain http with a bearer token is accepted for remote servers with a one-time log warning; the server's standing Identity text and lessons are injected into the system prompt; the model can permanently update or delete shared fleet memories via hicortex_update / hicortex_delete without confirmation.
Shodan tools with complete capability declarations.

Shop 100M+ products across thousands of US retailers: search, compare every store's live price, and switch variants (color, size) on inline product cards in Hermes Desktop. Portable Agent Plugins v1 package (mcp.json + skills/ + desktop/). Disclosure — connects to the hosted Channel3 MCP server at mcp.trychannel3.com (no account or key; free tier rate-limited per IP); search queries (and any image URL for visual search), product ids and variant selections go to it, and the Desktop cards call it directly from the app; a server-issued thread_id links searches within a conversation; product images load from cdn.trychannel3.com; Buy buttons open buy.trychannel3.com redirect links in the browser; nothing is purchased in-app and no credentials are stored.

Show live tokens-per-second and the active model on your Discord bot's presence. Disclosure — Replaces the Discord bot's public presence with the live tok/s figure and the model name of the most recent API call in this gateway (any platform or chat), visible to anyone who can see the bot; updates at most every interval seconds (minimum 10) over the gateway's existing Discord connection. Reads no credentials and makes no network calls of its own.

SidePulse lifecycle status backend; Desktop focus tracking requires the separate companion in the linked setup guide. Disclosure — forwards event names, a hashed agent id, the raw session_id and tool names to a local AF_UNIX socket and a 0600 jsonl log; no network egress.

Sign in to Google Antigravity with `hermes auth add antigravity-oauth` (or one command, `npx hermes-antigravity-oauth`) and run Hermes on the Antigravity plan: Gemini 3.x, Claude 4.6, GPT-OSS. Every request is made by Google's official agy CLI under agy's own login. The plugin writes your Hermes SOUL.md and system prompt into agy's workspace GEMINI.md so the persona carries over. When a model reaches for an agy-native tool (run_command, view_file, grep_search, and so on) the call is re-issued as the matching Hermes tool, which then runs under Hermes approvals. agy never executes tools on the host, and unmapped native tools are blocked. Disclosure: inference counts against the Antigravity/Gemini subscription agy is signed in to. The plugin never reads, copies or uploads the OAuth token. It symlinks agy's antigravity-oauth-token file, and on macOS ~/Library/Keychains, into a per-session private temp HOME, which is deleted on close. It also probes the OS keyring (security / secret-tool / cmdkey) for credential presence only. Derived from antigravity-subscription-directsdk (MIT). Disclosure — inference counts against the Antigravity/Gemini subscription agy is signed in to. The plugin does not read or upload the OAuth token itself; it symlinks (hard-links, or as a last resort copies) agy's antigravity-oauth-token file, and on macOS ~/Library/Keychains, into a per-session private temp HOME that is deleted on close, probes the OS keyring (security / secret-tool / cmdkey) for credential presence only, and writes the full Hermes system prompt into that temp workspace as GEMINI.md each turn. Derived from antigravity-subscription-directsdk (MIT).

Signal gateway adapter for Hermes Agent via a signal-cli daemon in HTTP mode (SSE inbound, JSON-RPC 2.0 outbound). Supports DMs, allowlisted groups, attachments, reactions and home-channel cron delivery. Phone numbers are treated as PII in logs.

Signed Nextcloud Talk bot webhooks and text replies for Hermes, with JSON/XML OCS support. Disclosure — runs an HTTP webhook listener (default 0.0.0.0:8788, HMAC-verified with the bot secret) and sends messages and optional Basic-auth room lookups to your Nextcloud server; registers the `nextcloud_talk` gateway platform.

Signed messaging with paired Hermes and OpenClaw agents, with receiver-controlled live and opt-in non-YOLO headless delivery. Disclosure — runs a loopback-only Node receiver when listen_port is set (you expose only its HTTPS receive route); messages from paired peers become agent turns in the sessions you approve and may cause tool use, and opt-in background delivery runs them in non-YOLO sessions only; smart scanning sends message text through your configured provider; ClawReef Public Groups use a plaintext relay that ClawReef can read; identity keys, peer credentials, holds and receipts live in the profile's plugin-data/antenna (0700/0600) and backups contain credentials; policy and storage commands rewrite config.yaml (comments and formatting are lost).

Signed, independently checkable receipts for Hermes approval verdicts and, since 0.2.0, for turns that stop on iteration exhaustion. Observe-only: a post_approval_response hook requests an invinoveritas decision receipt for each Guardian LLM verdict (or every approve/deny with scope=all); post_llm_call + on_session_end record, when a turn ends with max_iterations_reached, whether the turn's todo ledger (the last todo result or the list re-injected after compaction) was complete (turn_scope: exhausted by default, all, or off). Each receipt is a signed set of salted commitments that anyone can check for free at /verify-proof and that the holder can later open with the salt kept locally. Never approves, denies, delays, continues or blocks anything. Disclosure — one HTTPS POST per recorded approval decision or recorded turn to api.babyblueviper.com/decision-receipt (or the configured api_url) under INVINOVERITAS_API_KEY, paid automatically at 100 sats per receipt from your invinoveritas balance with no per-call confirmation (defaults: Guardian LLM verdicts, and only turns that stop on max_iterations_reached; scope: all adds every human approve/deny, turn_scope: all pays on every turn); sends a fixed question, the options, the choice, a nonce-salted SHA-256 of the context and the tool_call_id/turn_id, never the command text, todo contents or reply text; stores receipts, salts and the full contexts (including the command as Hermes passed it, and the todo ledger) in plugin-data/invinoveritas-receipts/receipts.jsonl.

SimpleX Chat gateway adapter for Hermes Agent. Connects to a local simplex-chat daemon via WebSocket and relays messages between SimpleX contacts/groups and the Hermes agent. SimpleX is decentralised and assigns no persistent user IDs — every contact is an opaque internal ID generated at connection time, making it one of the most private messengers available.

Singularity/Apptainer terminal backend: Hermes's terminal, file and code tools run inside a hardened, rootless container on this machine (--containall --no-home), with CPU/memory limits and an optional per-session persistent overlay (`hermes config set terminal.backend singularity`; image from `terminal.singularity_image`). Formerly built into Hermes core; existing users are migrated automatically. Disclosure — no Python dependencies and no network calls of its own: it drives the `apptainer` (or `singularity`) CLI you install, which pulls the configured image (default `docker://nousresearch/hermes-sandbox:desktop`) and caches a SIF under your scratch directory. Your skills and registered credential files are bind-mounted read-only into the container, and because the container is a disposable sandbox Hermes skips its dangerous-command prompts there, as for its other container backends.

Six-act boot animation for the Hermes desktop app — black-screen brand reveal, over-exposed whiteout bridge, a technical-dossier plate, an authorization handshake with identity confirmation, and a welcome finale — with audio cues, theme-aware light/dark plates and Esc/Enter/Space controls. Desktop-only: desktop/plugin.js inside the plugin SDK surface; no agent tools, hooks, middleware or env vars. Fully English UI. Adapted from 6shenhonghong9/dsh-startup-screen (MIT). Disclosure — on every Desktop launch (default: once per session) it covers the whole window with a full-screen animation that plays audio and spoken narration and waits for Enter/Space/click on two steps (Esc skips); while it is up it captures Enter/Space/Esc at the document level. Turn it off or switch to daily in its Startup Animation settings page.

Skill that runs a pre-trade safety check on Base ERC-20 tokens (honeypot/sellability, measured transfer tax, owner/mint/pause flags, liquidity, SAFE/CAUTION/AVOID verdict) by curling the Grey Ridge x402 API's free preview endpoint. Skill-only: no tools, hooks or env vars. Disclosure — the skill has the agent run `curl` against Grey Ridge Signals Group LLC's API (x402-data-api.sigrunner.workers.dev, the same service as api.greyridgesignals.ai) with the token address and, for the swap gate, trade side and USD size; each response carries a paid URL that the skill tells the agent it can call with an x402 client (suggesting `npm i x402-fetch viem`), paying $0.01 USDC per call on Base from whatever wallet that client is given, and it mentions an unpinned `pip install git+https://github.com/rezearcher/greyridge-x402-tools` helper that the user installs themselves. Its verdict is a heuristic, not financial advice.

Skip agent cron runs that would do nothing: a pre-run wake-gate script asks TypeSafe Jev one yes/no question over a small state snapshot (files, changed-since-last-run, localhost URLs) and prints {"wakeAgent": false} when it is confident the run is pointless. Fail-open on every error, forced wake after N consecutive skips, stdlib only. Disclosure — each gated cron tick (and the tool's test action) sends the configured snapshot of file contents, localhost URL response bodies and change flags (≤6,000 chars) to api.typesafe.ai with your TypeSafe key.

Slack gateway adapter for Hermes Agent. Connects to Slack via slack-bolt in Socket Mode and relays messages between Slack channels/DMs and the Hermes agent. Supports slash commands, threads, mrkdwn rendering, approval blocks, free-response channels, mention gating, and channel skill bindings.
Snapcompact context engine: archives conversation history as dense bitmap PNG frames that vision models read back at ~1/3 the token cost.

Source 2 documentation and mod tooling for CS2 and Deadlock from a local index of Valve's own game data: convars, Hammer entities with their inputs and outputs, schema classes and enums, game events, the cs_script and Pulse APIs and Source2Wiki pages, plus the mod pipeline — scaffold addons, validate scripts and .cfg files, start map builds on a registered Windows host over SSH, deploy and verify hashes, and record evidence, test runs and job state. Needs uv and an index built with s2docs sync; every write-capable call asks for approval. Disclosure — runs its MCP server with uvx from the pinned git commit, resolving its PyPI dependencies on first start as of a fixed 2026-10-10 snapshot; nothing is sent to a third party, but SSH/scp go to any host registered through register_host, build_start runs agent-written shell commands on that host and its builds keep running after the session ends, deploy_push and job_attach copy local files the agent names, and it writes its own index and addon workspace; write tools ask for approval through the package's untrusted server trust.

Source suppliers and negotiate purchases through the Kiwi Buyer MCP server — an open-source A2A commerce runtime (pinned @harrylabsj/kiwi@0.12.5 over npx stdio), with the kiwi-buyer sourcing workflow skill bundled. Sourcing is dual-source: Kiwi Network results come from kiwi_search, and internet e-commerce listings are reported through the host's own web tools when the session has them (a host capability, not a plugin guarantee). Portable Agent Plugins v1 package (mcp.json + skills/); needs Node.js/npm on PATH. No credentials required; Kiwi never handles payments.

SpecStream gives Hermes finished lists from the live web: describe the list in plain words and get every matching row with the page it was read from, priced per match with a maximum you approve before anything runs. Portable Agent Plugins v1 package with the hosted MCP server (remote streamable-http, OAuth 2.1 with dynamic client registration) and four skills (compile, review-work, approve-work, continue-work); no Python, no executables, no stored credentials. Disclosure — your request text and your answers to the price are sent to api.specstream.ai; approving a price spends your SpecStream balance (new accounts get $10 free) and the plugin marks its server `untrusted`, so Hermes asks before every call that is not read-only and refuses those calls in unattended runs; a `specstream` server you define in config.yaml replaces the package's and drops that prompt unless you add `trust: untrusted`.

Spend USDC in the real world from Hermes: prepaid cards, gift cards, push-to-card, Venmo/PayPal and bank payouts, through the Laso Finance API. Native plugin, standard library only. Sign-in is the OAuth device flow (link and code handed to the human, approved on any device), so there is no key to paste and it works over SSH and the messaging gateway. Every tool that moves money or mints a credential goes through the Hermes approval gate first. Disclosure — the tools move real funds from the user's Laso account and agent wallet; 19 money-moving or credential-minting tools ask for Hermes approval first, but approvals.mode off / yolo, or approvals.cron_mode/unattended_mode approve, let them run without a prompt; laso_buy_with_saved_card is not prompted in Hermes (Laso requires a passkey approval on the holder's device before an order); all traffic goes to laso.finance only; the approved key is saved as LASO_API_KEY in the profile's .env and removed when Laso rejects it.

Spotify Connect remote for Hermes Desktop — status-bar mini player (now playing, transport, volume, devices, search, playlists, queue) reusing the Hermes Spotify login (Spotify Premium required for playback control). Unified agent+desktop package: Electron status-bar player plus a dashboard-API backend (desktop-focused, no web UI). No agent tools; config via plugins.entries.spotify-desktop.settings (poll intervals).

Spotify for Hermes: seven tools (playback, devices, queue, search, playlists, albums, library) over the Spotify Web API, plus `hermes spotify login|status|logout` (loopback PKCE with your own Spotify developer app; Premium needed for playback control). Formerly built into Hermes core; existing users are migrated automatically.
Static review of candidate Hermes plugins; target code is never executed.
Status-bar chip for the focused session per-turn iteration usage (N/60), with a hover tooltip and a click popover of per-request stats.

Status-bar chip showing the provider balance and runway tracked by the MIT burnclock CLI, read from its local badge cache. Requires the CLI (pip install burnclock); the plugin makes no network calls and reads no credentials. Disclosure — runs a read-only shell command (cat of burnclock's local cache file) in your active local session every 60 seconds; balances come from the separately installed burnclock CLI (PyPI `burnclock`), which you configure with your provider keys and run yourself.

Status-bar chip, popover and dockable pane showing which skills are read into the active Hermes Desktop conversation's context: full bodies bold with an accent dot, compression-pruned ones ghosted, never-loaded ones not listed. A second pane view lists the whole skill library grouped by category with descriptions and a loaded marker, and clicking a skill drops /<skill> into the composer for you to send (it never submits). A small local backend reads the profile's state.db read-only to tell a live skill body from a [SKILL_PRUNED] marker, and reads SKILL.md frontmatter for the descriptions. No network calls, no credentials, no telemetry, no writes. Disclosure — the local backend opens state.db read-only for the requested session in this profile, the default root and, as a fallback, every other profile's state.db, and returns only skill names and load state; it reads SKILL.md frontmatter under the Hermes skill directories and makes no network calls or writes.

Status-bar chips for the background self-improvement review and batch context compaction: review running/done/stale with live elapsed time, a turn-countdown fill bar to the next nudge, an always-visible compaction chip (compacting/done/failed/stale with committed reduction or failure class), reply-guard recovery and review-overlap diagnostics, and a Settings page that tunes both orphan ceilings. Disclosure — renderer-only; polls filtered read-only tails of agent.log via host.logs to parse lifecycle markers; listens for review.summary/message.start/message.complete events; stores three small plugin-storage records (settings + last compaction + last review); no network calls beyond the local gateway, no credential access, no self-update.

Status-bar popover for Hermes Desktop with three views: Costs (spend, cache, pricing drift, OpenRouter provider routing), AAI (skill changes, ratings, tests and replays) and HDR (a guard for risky tool calls, hooks, destinations, sensitive paths, what runs on its own). Disclosure — reads this profile's sessions (and other profiles' when you pick them) to audit tool calls, paths and hosts; can edit and save config.yaml and rewrite skill files when you ship or revert a version; AAI replays and judge runs resend conversation context and tool definitions to OpenRouter with your OpenRouter key and incur cost; HDR lists listening TCP ports via ps/lsof; HDR's guard (off by default) checks each tool call through a pre_tool_call hook and, when you turn it on, holds calls Hermes does not check itself (reading keys and logins, writing startup items or key places Hermes does not list) and asks you in its own card or a macOS notification, blocking after up to 20 seconds without an answer or at once when Hermetic is not open, or blocks them outright; the guard is a best-effort match on the paths a call names, not a sandbox; questions from every profile wait in the default profile's hermetic folder; HDR also lists shell and gateway hooks and flags hook scripts edited after approval, keeping a copy of each script to compare.

Status-bar quota tracking for 17 providers: Tavily, OpenCode Go, DeepSeek, GLM (z.ai), OpenRouter, Grok (xAI), Codex (OpenAI), OpenAI, Anthropic, Groq, Cerebras, Moonshot Kimi, MiniMax, Google Gemini, Hugging Face, Mistral, and Qwen. DeepSeek and GLM show peak/off-peak gauges and countdowns. Includes OAuth and multi-key pools. This edition does not rotate Hermes environment keys on exhaust, and an expired OAuth token asks for a new login. Codex and Grok checks use their CLI client identity and user-agent. Disclosure — Reads provider API keys from the Hermes .env and its own config.json and calls each enabled provider's own usage or billing endpoint; Codex and Grok sign-ins use those CLIs' OAuth client identity and user-agent, keep the plugin's tokens in its install folder, and ask for a new login on expiry. When the Discord gateway runs, the bot's Discord presence (visible to everyone in servers the bot shares) is updated every 20 seconds by default with tokens/sec, context-window use and the active provider's name with its remaining quota or dollar credit balance (model and running tool are opt-in); turn it off with plugins.entries.provider-status.settings.discord_presence_enabled: false. /pulse and the agent_pulse tool report process-wide telemetry (model, provider, current tool, quota) to anyone allowed to call them on a gateway. Writes a secret-free quota-cache.json into its install folder and reads Hermes config.yaml for the active model.

Step through Hermes Desktop sidebar sessions in on-screen order with Ctrl+Cmd+] / Ctrl+Cmd+[ (rebindable), wrapping at both ends. SDK-only: session-row slot markers for order, host.state for the focused session, host.openSession for navigation.

Step-by-step prompt builder for Hermes Desktop (F4): option cards per step with AI suggestions, then an AI-written final prompt sent to or placed in the composer through host.composer (Hermes Desktop 0.21.5+). Tuned for Claude Opus 5.5, Claude Sonnet 5.5 and GPT-6 Astra. AI calls go through its own auxiliary task (auxiliary.prompt_studio) via the dashboard plugin API; sends no temperature. No external network beyond the configured provider; preferences in ctx.storage. Disclosure — on opening in an existing chat (default on, toggle in Studio Settings) it reads the last 8 user/assistant turns (plus any compaction summary) of that session from state.db, redacts secrets and sends up to 8k chars to the configured auxiliary model for a short summary used in step suggestions; draft and form answers go to the same auxiliary model; no other network.
Stock market data from Financial Datasets - financial statements, prices, SEC filings, insider and institutional ownership, KPIs, news, macro data, and a stock screener.

Store a secret on the gateway host without showing it to the model. Disclosure — stores the value in plaintext in the profile .env (mode 0600) and adds the name to terminal.env_passthrough, so $NAME is available to the terminal tool; the model can still read the value with its own tools (cat .env, echo $NAME). Keeps secrets out of chat/prompt context and redacts verbatim output of credential-shaped values; it is not a boundary against a model that deliberately reads it. Adds a static system-prompt section and a /secret command. Imports private core helpers read-only (_config_profile_scope, _is_hermes_provider_credential, _CONFIG_LOCK).
Strip unwanted Chinese (CJK) and Cyrillic characters from LLM output. Korean Hangul and Japanese Kana are preserved.
Suggests your next message after each turn as a pill under the Desktop composer: your likely answer when the agent asks you something, or the natural next step.

Suno music, Seedance video, HappyHorse (Happy Horse) video, GPT Image images and Nano Banana images by Ace Data Cloud; 17 selectable service toolsets and a Nano Banana image_generate backend. Each generate call spends Ace Data Cloud credits on your ACEDATACLOUD_API_KEY with no Hermes approval prompt; the model can choose costly options (pro models, 4K, up to 4 images), and prompts and reference URLs go to api.acedata.cloud. Google Search and face analysis also spend Credits. Disclosure — Each generate call spends Ace Data Cloud credits on your ACEDATACLOUD_API_KEY with no Hermes approval prompt, and the model can pick costly options (pro models, 4K, up to 4 outputs); Google Search and face analysis are billed too. Prompts, reference URLs and face images go to api.acedata.cloud. The tools are on wherever you enable their toolsets, including gateways.

Supermemory semantic long-term memory provider — profile recall, semantic search, explicit memory tools, and per-turn conversation capture. Maintained by Supermemory; the same provider that shipped in-tree.
Switch Hermes browser tools to a named Chromium-family profile (Chrome, Edge, Brave), local or remote, over CDP.

SwitchBot OpenAPI v1.1, personal use. No Plug Mini on/off. Locks off unless enabled. setPosition only Curtain/Curtain3 (0=open). Disclosure — Controls real devices through the SwitchBot cloud API (api.switch-bot.com) using your SWITCHBOT_TOKEN and SWITCHBOT_SECRET. Each call reads SWITCHBOT_TOKEN and SWITCHBOT_SECRET for the active profile, and an HTTP proxy set in the environment is not used. Every command asks for Hermes approval and is refused under cron, yolo, approvals off and unattended sessions. Lock and door devices stay refused unless you turn on safety_devices. The plugin has no user list of its own: anyone you allow on your Hermes gateway can request a command and approve it. Answering "always" adds an unused line to config.yaml each time. The optional watch is a cron job (a model turn every 5 minutes by default) that stays after uninstall until you run unschedule. Not tested on real devices. While the plugin is enabled, its skill adds one line to the skills index of every session, including surfaces where the tools are turned off.

THEIA — The Human Environment Intelligence Aperture: virtual-desktop capture, fused stage observation, guarded caches, bounded dynamic workflows, and persistent raw-RGB LocateAnything C++/Q5 CUDA grounding.

TIDAL for Hermes Agent: five tools (playback through local mpv, search, playlists, library, mixes) over the unofficial TIDAL API via tidalapi. Login is TIDAL's own PKCE login flow (hermes tidal login) — no developer app needed. Playback runs on the Hermes machine (mpv); TIDAL has no remote-device API like Spotify Connect. Needs a TIDAL subscription (any tier). Disclosure — unofficial TIDAL integration (community tidalapi library using TIDAL's own app client); stores your TIDAL access and refresh token in plaintext (owner-only, 0600) under $HERMES_HOME/plugin-data/tidal/ and refreshes it itself; playback spawns a detached local mpv process with an IPC socket and plays audio on the Hermes machine.

Tabular AI that grows with your tables — Hermes skills for honest tabular ML, one entry point. Disclosure — Installing pulls numpy, pandas, scikit-learn, pyarrow, joblib and pyyaml into Hermes's environment. The skills have the agent run Python on your data files, may ask it to pip install catboost, tabicl/torch, mapie or matplotlib, and the TabICL skill downloads a pretrained checkpoint of a few hundred MB on first use. Saved checkpoints are pickles: load only ones you made.

Talk to Hermes from Chatwork rooms, built on the Chatwork API: put Hermes in a Chatwork room and ask it with [To:] or a reply, like a colleague; the answer comes back as a Chatwork reply. Polls the Chatwork API (no public URL or webhook), never answers a message twice across restarts, and while CHATWORK_ALLOWED_USERS is unset only the token's own account can use Hermes commands beyond /help, /whoami, /new and /reset or answer approval prompts. Disclosure: talks only to api.chatwork.com with your own API token; polls every 5 s by default while the gateway runs; stores read positions and the ids of its posted messages in <HERMES_HOME>/plugin-data/jp-chatwork/state.json. Disclosure — while CHATWORK_ALLOWED_USERS is unset everyone in the rooms listed in CHATWORK_ROOMS (external guests included) can prompt the agent and use its enabled tools, with Hermes commands and approval answers kept to the token's own account; talks only to api.chatwork.com with your API token, polling every 5 s while the gateway runs; stores read positions and posted message ids in <HERMES_HOME>/plugin-data/jp-chatwork/state.json; logs each asker's name and account id.

Talk to Hermes from Salesforce Chatter: @mention the bot user in a post or comment, it Likes the message as an acknowledgement and replies in the same thread, keeping the thread as one session. Images and files on the post are passed to the model; MEDIA files are attached back. Community plugin, not affiliated with Salesforce. Disclosure — authenticates as a dedicated bot user with the OAuth 2.0 JWT bearer flow, reading the private key file at SF_CHATTER_PRIVATE_KEY_PATH; talks to the configured Salesforce login host and the org instance (attachment downloads follow Salesforce redirects); image URLs in the agent's replies are fetched from the gateway host over HTTPS (any public host; private, loopback and metadata addresses are refused) and uploaded to Chatter; polls the To Me feed every 60 s and, for allowlisted groups, runs a SOQL probe every 5 s by default (counts against the org API quota); writes Likes, comments, files in the bot user's Files and optional home-channel posts; keeps its ledger in plugin-data/salesforce-chatter/inbox.sqlite. dry_run defaults to true (no Salesforce writes, no outbound image fetch); with SF_CHATTER_ALLOWED_USERS unset nobody is answered. Optional, off by default: html_preview renders model-generated HTML to PNG with Chromium in a network-isolated Docker container (digest-pinned image, pulled if missing). No telemetry.

Talk to your Hermes from small ESP32 devices with a screen, microphone and speaker: hold a button, ask, and hear the answer. Adds a gateway platform where each device is a chat, plus tools to list devices, show a card on a screen and run device actions (LEDs, relays). Disclosure — the gateway listens for devices on a WebSocket port (8765, all interfaces by default; plain ws:// unless tls_cert/tls_key are set). New devices need a Hermes pairing code unless listed in GADGET_ALLOWED_USERS; GADGET_ALLOW_ALL_USERS skips pairing (development only). A paired device answers the agent's command approvals for its own chat (allow once or deny), within Hermes's approval timeout. The first approved device becomes the platform's home channel by default. Session hooks feed a dashboard on paired devices with each agent session's platform, a short id and its state (idle, busy, waiting for approval); a device that can switch profiles also sees the offered profiles' sessions. Optional profile switching (off unless `profiles` is set in the default profile's gadget config) lets a device paired on the default profile talk to the listed profiles; each profile approves the device through its own pairing flow (the device shows the `hermes -p <profile> pairing approve` command), the plugin writes nothing into other profiles, and revoking the device in the default profile sends it back there. Spoken replies that are not WAV are converted with the local ffmpeg; Opus reply audio uses the host's libopus when installed (loaded with ctypes, not bundled). `hermes gadget update --latest` downloads firmware from this repository's GitHub releases, checks size and SHA-256 against the release manifest (files carry build provenance attestations) and sends it to the device. Writes only under plugin-data/gadget/. Uses Hermes's own STT, TTS and image cache; no telemetry. Independent community project, not affiliated with Nous Research.
Tavily web search + extract. Opt-in keyless via hermes tools; set TAVILY_API_KEY for higher limits — https://app.tavily.com/home.
