Teaches Hermes's built-in secret redactor 71 more vendor credential formats (HashiCorp Vault, Doppler, Amazon Bedrock, Atlassian, Cloudflare, Supabase, Tailscale, Docker Hub, JFrog Artifactory, CircleCI, HubSpot, PostHog, Grafana, Sentry, Shopify and others) through register_redaction_patterns, so those tokens are masked in logs, tool output and model-bound text like the built-in ones. Disclosure — register() makes one call, ctx.register_redaction_patterns; no tools, hooks, network access, subprocesses, files or environment variables; the patterns can only add masks, and security.redact_secrets: false still turns redaction off.

TeamoRouter as Hermes model providers on one key: `teamorouter` serves Claude models over TeamoRouter's native Anthropic Messages API (so Hermes' Anthropic prompt caching and thinking apply), and `teamorouter-openai` serves GPT, Gemini, DeepSeek, GLM and Grok models over its OpenAI-compatible API. Each /model picker lists that side's tool-capable chat models from TeamoRouter's public catalog, leaving out image, service-tier and free-tier variants, and context windows come from the same catalog. Maintained by TeamoRouter. Disclosure — registers two model providers at import and nothing else (no tools, hooks, commands or threads). Prompts, tool schemas and TEAMOROUTER_API_KEY go to https://api.teamorouter.com (/v1/messages and /v1/chat/completions) through Hermes' own clients, and TeamoRouter forwards each request to the upstream vendor serving the model. The plugin's own request is GET https://api.teamorouter.com/v1/models/pricing, a public endpoint, sent without the key and cached for an hour. `teamorouter-openai` requests carry a fixed `X-Client-Source: hermes-teamorouter-plugin` header (via the profile's default_headers), used only to count traffic from this plugin; Claude requests carry no header from the plugin. No telemetry, no files read or written, no stored credentials, no processes.

Telegram Business secretary: transcribes voice notes, round videos, and speech attachments right in the chat, with Settings and per-chat controls in Telegram's Manage Bot panel, plus opt-in text history (with import from a Telegram export), correspondence stats, and contact dossiers. Disclosure — audio goes to the STT backend Hermes is configured with (local or external); transcript cleanup sends chat text through the host ctx.llm; opt-in dossiers send chat text through the Hermes model task telesec_dossier (default Vercel AI Gateway to Google with zero data retention; an optional message check on the same gateway and optional Cloudflare fact extraction are off by default); an owner-sent /dossier posts that contact's stored dossier (without the owner note, but written with it) into the Business chat for the contact to read; runs local ffprobe/ffmpeg (argument lists, no shell) on attached audio; opt-in dossiers run a gateway background thread; modes, opt-in history, and dossiers are stored 0600 under HERMES_HOME/data/telesec; reads only the numeric bot id prefix of TELEGRAM_BOT_TOKEN; no telemetry.

Telegram client pane for Hermes Desktop: dialogs, message history with image previews and per-post image reload, forum topics, and reviewed send/reply/save/delete/mark-as-read actions via a dedicated Telethon user session (separate from the core gateway bot token). All history is sanitized before rendering. Disclosure — the profile dashboard backend reads dialogs and message history and downloads media for in-page previews (page byte-budgeted and cached in memory); TELEGRAM_API_ID/TELEGRAM_API_HASH come from the profile's Hermes secrets; login challenges stay in process memory; the dedicated Telethon session lives in HERMES_HOME/telegram-plugin-auth/ (directory 0700, .session and its -wal/-shm sidecars 0600), and anyone holding that session file controls the Telegram account; delete removes the selected message for everyone; mutations go prepare -> exact preview -> confirm -> commit -> readback, and the pane's "Confirm actions" switch (on by default) can turn the preview step off; message links open in the system browser (http and https only).

Telegram gateway adapter for Hermes Agent. Connects to Telegram via python-telegram-bot and relays messages between Telegram chats/groups/topics and the Hermes agent. Supports threads/topics, streaming edits, native media, inline keyboards, slash commands, fallback network transport (direct-IP failover), notification modes, mention gating, and per-user/chat allowlists.

Tell Cabinet the job you need done and it answers with the smallest setup that does it (one chat, a skill, a routine, a Bot or a crew), shows which answers led there, then helps you act: add one of botcabinet.com's 20 Bots (each with its test record shown) as a Hermes profile, plan a new Bot line by line, or set up a crew of Bots in a handoff order with blocked Kanban cards. Everything Cabinet makes can be removed again from My Bots, and a Bot that Hermes's own Bots catalog carries is handed over to it, never duplicated. Disclosure — fetches its Bot catalog from https://botcabinet.com/catalog.json on open and Refresh (data only, 2 MB cap) and, after you confirm, creates Hermes profiles whose instructions (SOUL.md) come from that catalog; can create and archive Kanban cards for a crew; deletes only profiles it created that you have not changed; reads ~/.hermes/profiles and hashes profile files to track what it made; calls private Hermes modules (hermes_cli.profiles, kanban_db), so a Hermes update can break it; no shell, credentials, telemetry or self-updates.

Tells the user when a chat is getting too long and hands them a short opener for a fresh chat; the new chat pulls the earlier context itself via session_search, no handover document. Fill level from real provider token counts, measured against Hermes' compaction point by default; notices at 70 % and 90 % (configurable), once each per chat, re-armed after compaction, never in cron, subagent, kanban, batch or webhook runs. Notice in the conversation language, English or German. Disclosure — on the turn that crosses a threshold, pre_llm_call adds a one-turn instruction to that turn's user message (never the system prompt; replayed byte-identical, so prompt caching stays intact); post_api_request stores per-session token counts, model and provider name and which notice fired (no message content) under HERMES_HOME/plugin-data/chat-length/, pruned after 30 days; reads the session title read-only from state.db and the compression settings read-only from config.yaml; no network calls, no tools, no dependencies.

Tencent Yuanbao gateway adapter for Hermes Agent. Connects to Yuanbao IM Bot over a persistent WebSocket (HMAC-signed sign token) and relays DMs and group messages between Yuanbao and the Hermes agent. Supports native media/stickers, DM/group access policies, and home-channel cron delivery.

Terminal backend running agent commands in isolated DeepInfra cloud sandboxes (deep_sands microVMs). Disclosure — runs agent commands in billable DeepInfra cloud sandboxes and uploads your Hermes skills, cache and skill-registered credential files to the sandbox at /workspace/.hermes; dangerous-command approval is skipped inside the sandbox.

Thai (ภาษาไทย) language pack covering all three Hermes UI surfaces — Desktop (5,023/5,030), core CLI/gateway/platforms (3,437/3,437), and the Ink TUI (1,259/1,259) — 9,719/9,725 keys total (99.9%). All three catalogs checked against the English reference with `hermes plugins validate`. Manifest-only plugin: flat nested YAML overlays under locales/, no code, no network, no dependencies. Registering the pack never changes display.language — the user opts in via `hermes config set display.language th`. Disclosure — text-only catalogs (no code, network or dependencies); untranslated keys fall back to English: the 7 array/conditional Desktop keys listed in the repo README, plus strings Hermes added after the pack was built.

The Alt+Tab gesture for Hermes profiles. Hold Ctrl+Alt and tap Tab to cycle through your profiles, release to land on the highlighted one — the same hold-tap-release rhythm as the OS app switcher. (Alt+Tab, Win+Tab and Cmd+Tab are owned by the window manager and cannot be bound by any application, so the gesture lives on ctrl+alt+tab, unclaimed by the OS and by Hermes core.) Each row shows the profile's model and most recent conversation; a working profile shows a spinner. Also opens with a single contributed keybind (Cmd+Alt+P / Ctrl+Alt+P, rebindable in the app's own keybind panel), a status-bar chip, and a palette command. The switch goes through the Desktop's own profile path, so the target profile's backend is activated and its chrome is scoped onto it. Desktop-only (desktop/plugin.js inside the plugin SDK surface); no agent tools, hooks, middleware, env vars, network calls, or stored credentials.

The Hermes desktop app in your browser. `hermes workbench` serves the desktop interface through the Hermes dashboard, for headless servers, VPSes and tablets. Disclosure — community plugin, not a Nous product. On the first `hermes workbench` run and again after each Hermes update it runs `npm install --ignore-scripts` (guided by Hermes's lockfile) and Vite against your Hermes checkout's desktop sources, writing only under ~/.hermes/hermes-workbench and its own plugin dir (the checkout is only read), and starts `hermes dashboard` on loopback when none is running.

The Kimchi coding harness (kimchi.dev) as a Hermes model provider over ACP stdio — spawns kimchi --mode acp keeping the harness's permission prompts on (YOLO opt-in via KIMCHI_ACP_ARGS="--mode acp --yolo"), the harness owns its own auth, and completed tool calls surface as inline bullets in the reply. Disclosure — every turn spawns the local Kimchi CLI (`kimchi --mode acp`, overridable with KIMCHI_ACP_COMMAND / KIMCHI_ACP_ARGS) in Hermes's working directory and hands it the conversation. The harness calls kimchi.dev with its own stored login and runs its own shell, file and web tools. Its permission prompts stay on, and Hermes cancels them, so gated tools don't run, unless you opt in with KIMCHI_ACP_ARGS="--mode acp --yolo", which runs them with no approval prompt (not for shared gateway or cron use). To show setup status, it parses ~/.config/kimchi/config.json (or KIMCHI_CONFIG_PATH) only to check that a key is present; the key is never stored or sent by Hermes.

The athlete's own training and health data from 39 apps (Garmin, Oura, WHOOP, Hevy, Apple Health, Intervals.icu and more) through athletedata's hosted MCP server (Streamable HTTP at https://mcp.athletedata.health/mcp): activities, training load, HRV, sleep, readiness, nutrition, body composition, race predictions, and structured workouts pushed to the athlete's watch. Bundles one skill that tells the agent when to use it. Agent Plugins v1 package (plugin.json + mcp.json + skills/), configuration only. Disclosure — hosted-only connector with no local code: every tool call, with its arguments, goes to mcp.athletedata.health and needs an athletedata account (paid, 7-day free trial) with its API key in ATHLETEDATA_API_KEY; the athlete's health and training data is returned from that server. Write tools (push a workout to the watch, log food, create a Hevy routine) change the athlete's own accounts; the package marks the server untrusted, so Hermes asks before every tool the server does not annotate as read-only. The tool set is served by the remote server at runtime and is not covered by the pinned sha.

The ngrok AI Gateway as a Hermes model provider (`--provider ngrok`, or ngrok AI Gateway in `hermes model`): one access key for all your model providers, with failover. The model list comes live from your gateway, and gateway errors (unrouted model, access-policy and upstream-key failures, out of credit) map onto Hermes' fallback instead of a generic error. Disclosure — registers one model provider at import and nothing else (no tools, hooks, commands or threads); chat requests and the model list go to https://gateway.ngrok.ai/v1 (or NGROK_AI_GATEWAY_BASE_URL) through Hermes' own client with NGROK_AI_GATEWAY_KEY, which Hermes reads; the plugin itself opens no connections, reads and writes no files and starts no processes.

The official Speechify text-to-speech provider (tts.provider: speechify), maintained by Speechify. Simba 3.5 voices in 48 languages with low-latency streaming in voice mode, Opus voice notes for messaging platforms, and a hermes speechify command to list voices and hear a test line. Disclosure — sends the text being spoken, the chosen voice and model, the plugin's name and version (Speechify-Caller attribution headers), and your SPEECHIFY_API_KEY to api.speechify.ai (or the base_url / SPEECHIFY_BASE_URL you configure); synthesis is billed to your Speechify workspace; generated audio is written to Hermes's audio cache; no tools, hooks or middleware; no telemetry.

The xAI API surfaces core does not cover, nothing it already ships (provider, x_search, web search, TTS, STT and Imagine stay in core). Voice module: full-duplex Grok Voice (grok-voice-latest) in the Desktop composer, built like core's GPT-Live mode; the voice model hands real work to Hermes as a normal turn on the open chat (surface voice-live) and reads the result aloud; the backend mints a 300 s xAI client secret so XAI_API_KEY never reaches the renderer. Collections module: one read-only tool, xai_collections_search, over documents the user already indexed in xAI Collections (GET /v1/collections, POST /v1/documents/search). Disclosure — the voice button captures microphone audio and streams it to api.x.ai over a WebSocket; the backend calls api.x.ai once per call with XAI_API_KEY (read through agent.secret_scope) to mint the secret; delegated requests run as normal Hermes turns with the profile's full toolset and approvals, and their final text (up to 3000 characters) plus the last spoken turns are sent back to xAI. Each xai_collections_search call sends the query to api.x.ai with XAI_API_KEY and returns passages into the conversation. Nothing is uploaded, stored or deleted and no telemetry is emitted; xAI bills on the user's key.

TinyFish: the web, built into Hermes. Free Search and Fetch power Hermes's own web_search and web_extract, and when a site needs clicks, forms or a login, a remote browser and the tinyfish_agent web agent handle it. Disclosure — sends search queries, URLs to fetch and tinyfish_agent goals with your TINYFISH_API_KEY to the TinyFish API (*.tinyfish.ai). Browser sessions and tinyfish_agent runs spend TinyFish credits. Under the default `request` policy each one goes through Hermes's approval prompt first (a session/always answer covers every later call; cron and unattended runs are denied unless you allow them). Setting `tinyfish.credit_policy.<feature>: allow` or YOLO skips the prompt. `hermes tinyfish setup` / `browser enable` (run by you) save the key to Hermes .env, set web.search_backend/extract_backend and browser.cloud_provider in config.yaml, enable the web/browser toolsets, and can install the agent-browser CLI after asking.

Title-bar cheatsheet. Describe what you want to do and it points to a real command or a cited passage; live slash commands and plugins, plus cited passages from this install's docs. No runtime network. No self-update. Disclosure — reads the Markdown docs shipped with your Hermes install (website/docs next to hermes_cli) through a local dashboard route and lists your commands, plugins and MCP servers via read-only gateway calls; no network at runtime (doc and GitHub links open in your browser only when clicked).
Today's git digest in the current repo, plus the last failed terminal command the Hermes agent ran. Desktop pane, status chip, optional local LLM summary. Does not watch OS or editor terminals.
Together AI model-provider plugin — OpenAI-compatible API, 270+ serverless open-weight models, live catalog discovery.

Token consumption analytics for Hermes: records exact per-call usage from pre/post_api_request hooks, decomposes every request into categories (system prompt, built-in and per-MCP-server tool schemas, skills, memory, history, tool results, output, reasoning) calibrated to billed totals, and adds a Token Lens dashboard tab plus a Sessions-page card with deterministic and AI-evaluated token-reduction suggestions; `hermes token-lens refresh` runs a suggestion refresh from the CLI. Disclosure — records per-API-call token counts (no message text) from pre/post_api_request hooks into token_lens.db at the Hermes home root (per-call rows kept 90 days, rollups kept), and reads Hermes's state.db read-only for session token totals and, during the optional dashboard history import, message text for estimation only; after 10 recorded sessions it automatically calls your configured main model through Hermes's plugin LLM facade every 5 sessions (up to two calls per refresh, capped at 50,000 tokens by meta_budget_tokens), sending aggregated token statistics plus the names of your enabled MCP servers and plugins, and auto-applies the model's proposed category regex rules and rubric changes (logged to token_lens.EVOLUTION.md; evolve_rules: false turns this off); the dashboard's refresh button spawns a detached `hermes token-lens refresh` process that logs to logs/token-lens-refresh.log; its data paths follow the HERMES_HOME environment variable rather than the active profile, so in a multi-profile gateway every profile records into the launch profile's database; no third-party network calls, no telemetry.

Topic-aware session title tracking for Hermes Agent. Hermes generates the first title by default; AutoTitler follows conversation changes and session close without changing the host title-generation switch. Disclosure — sends excerpts of each conversation (sampled user turns, short assistant replies, compaction summaries) to your Hermes title-generation model in the background, also for up to 200 recent untitled sessions at startup; needs plugins.entries.hermes-auto-titler.llm.allow_task_override (or allow_provider/model_override for a custom route). 0.3 no longer edits config.yaml, but users upgrading from 0.2.x keep auxiliary.title_generation.enabled=false until they re-enable it (/autotitler status shows the fix).

Track package deliveries with the Parcel app (parcelapp.net). List what's on the way, add tracking numbers and look up carrier codes, with a built-in guard for Parcel's strict rate limits. Disclosure — sends tracking numbers, descriptions and optional postcode/order email to api.parcel.app (Parcel Premium API key); the model can add deliveries to the user's Parcel account (add-only, capped at 20/day); caches delivery lists in plugin-data.

Track subscription quotas and reset times in Hermes Desktop. Disclosure — probe.py re-executes itself under the Hermes Python interpreter located via HERMES_PYTHON / VIRTUAL_ENV / the parent process or the Hermes installer's managed venv (HERMES_HOME/installs). Every credential read is read-only and nothing is refreshed or stored: it reads provider API keys from the process environment, the Hermes .env, the Vaultwarden plugin's local secret cache (cache/vaultwarden_cache.json, only when Vaultwarden is the sole enabled secret source, keyed by a hash of BW_SESSION, which is never sent) and Docker s6 container env files; Hermes's saved OAuth logins (auth.json credential pool and HERMES_HOME/.anthropic_oauth.json); and other coding-assistant CLIs' local logins: Claude Code (credentials file, macOS keychain or Windows Credential Manager), Codex, Cursor (macOS keychain and the IDE's state.vscdb, opened read-only), Kimi, Grok, ZCode and Command Code. For GitHub Copilot (on by default) it tries COPILOT_GITHUB_TOKEN / GH_TOKEN / GITHUB_TOKEN (through Hermes get_secret, else the process environment), then the Copilot editor's apps.json / hosts.json, then runs gh auth token (prompts disabled, 3-second limit), trying each token in turn until GitHub accepts one. It sends each key only to its own vendor's usage endpoint, presenting the vendor client's identity headers where a private endpoint expects them (Claude Code and Codex CLI user agents, the Grok CLI client headers, and for Copilot the VS Code / Copilot Chat editor headers on api.github.com/copilot_internal/user, which GitHub does not document); environment variables such as GROK_CLI_CHAT_PROXY_BASE_URL, CLAUDE_CONFIG_DIR, CODEX_HOME and GROK_HOME change which host or file it uses. Usage results are cached under HERMES_HOME/cache/resetwatch, never tokens. It exposes nothing to the model: it is a Desktop page only.

Triage the findings file of a Darkmoon autonomous pentest scan (JSON or SARIF): filter by severity and proof status, get a severity-sorted summary and a pass/fail gate for a release. Read-only and offline: no network, no subprocess, no credentials, standard library only. Darkmoon is open source (GPL-3.0); its web dashboard and remediation agent are Pro and are not used here. Disclosure — reads a local .json or .sarif file at a model-supplied path (10 MB cap) and returns its findings; no network, subprocess or writes

Tripo 3D tools on Tripo's v3 API (openapi.tripo3d.ai). Text, photo or multiview to 3D, image edits, retexturing, splitting into parts, Smart UV, auto-rigging, preset animations, retopology, format conversion (FBX, USDZ, STL, 3MF, OBJ, GLTF) and downloads, with an inline 3D viewer in Hermes Desktop that shows whether a model is really rigged, a library pane that shows where each model came from (the steps behind it, its prompt, a jump back to the chat that made it, and one-click next steps), a local model inspector, and a status-bar chip with the Tripo balance and this chat's spend. Every credit-spending call goes through Hermes's approval prompt with its estimated cost, and a per-chat limit (a setting under Settings → Plugins, default 100 credits) makes it ask again past it. Needs TRIPO_API_KEY. Unofficial; not affiliated with Tripo or VAST. Disclosure — sends prompts and the local images or 3D model files you or the agent name (up to 50 MB; every local-file upload, free calls included, goes through Hermes's approval prompt) to Tripo's API at openapi.tripo3d.ai with TRIPO_API_KEY; saves downloaded models to $HERMES_HOME/tripo/ or a folder the agent picks (never overwriting: a clash gets a " (2)" suffix), and the Desktop viewer's save button copies models into your Downloads/Tripo folder (or the folder set in its settings); keeps a local task history in $HERMES_HOME/tripo/history.json (chat id, tool, prompt, parent task, estimated cost, saved file paths; at most 2,000 tasks, never sent anywhere); the Desktop library opens local .glb/.fbx/.obj/.stl files only from inside your home folder, $HERMES_HOME/tripo/ or the viewer's download folder, and uploads nothing; the status-bar chip reads your Tripo balance every two minutes and after each Tripo tool call; no shell commands, background processes or telemetry.

Tsubasa OpenAI-compatible model provider (tool calling not supported yet). Disclosure — sends prompts and your TSUBASA_API_KEY to api.tsubasa.sh, operated by PalmAndWand; the API currently serves Canada only and answers HTTP 451 to requests from elsewhere.

Turn a pilot-scale eval score into a deployment decision — Wilson intervals, a confidence threshold that routes uncertain cases to a human, and an honest INSUFFICIENT EVIDENCE verdict when the sample cannot support the claim. Disclosure — gonogo_report writes report JSON/HTML to the path the model supplies.

Turn an idea, a photo of an object, or a shop listing into a sliced Bambu Studio project. The agent writes a Blender script, print3d checks the mesh (overhangs, thin walls, fits between parts, likeness to the photo), slices it and says what to fix, until it prints clean; each run also writes a 3D view the agent opens in the Desktop preview pane. Portable Agent Plugins v1 package: one skill and a stdio MCP server run through uvx, so Blender 4.2+, Bambu Studio and uv are required; at install Hermes looks for Blender in the standard locations (/Applications and Steam on macOS; PATH, flatpak, snap and Steam on Linux) and refuses the install without it. Disclosure — runs Blender and the Bambu Studio CLI as local child processes; Blender runs the agent-written Python with your user's permissions, outside Hermes's terminal sandbox, and the server is marked untrusted, so Hermes asks before every tool that runs a script or changes a job (the read-only tools still write preview images and the 3D view under ~/print3d/jobs without asking); installs Pillow and mcp from PyPI; the 3D view loads three.js from cdn.jsdelivr.net; the optional `print3d setup` command (not needed for a catalog install) edits Hermes, Codex, Claude, Cursor and Gemini config files, with backups. Never contacts the printer; no telemetry, no credentials.

Turn any MCP server into a portable Agent Plugin (mcp.json + workflow skill) built from evidence: the server's self-description, your past sessions with it, its docs and a read-only probe. Validates and installs the package in linked mode, and checks a built plugin for server drift and new errors in use. Disclosure: starts the target MCP server to introspect it; reads this profile's state.db read-only; logs redacted mcp__* call summaries locally (log_calls: false turns it off); inline server launches, writes outside its data dir and installs ask for approval.

Twelve Egyptian gods in painted relief and gold leaf: Thoth, Ra, Isis, Osiris, Anubis, Horus, Bastet, Sekhmet, Set, Nut, Ptah and Hathor, as Hermes Desktop themes. Install once, then switch with /skin <name>. Matching terminal skins ship in cli/skins. Disclosure — theme-only desktop plugin: it registers twelve themes through the plugin SDK, and their stylesheets restyle parts of Desktop's own UI (sidebar art, tabs, composer, wordmark) only while one of its themes is active. It also watches Desktop's active theme: when a terminal skin named kemet-<god> is active, it switches Desktop to that god's theme through the SDK's requestTheme. The terminal skins are plain YAML files the user copies into the Hermes skins folder by hand; the plugin does not install them or write any files. Fonts and art are bundled; no network requests, no agent tools or hooks.

Twelve Norse gods carved in runestone and wood: Odin, Thor, Freyja, Loki, Frigg, Baldur, Tyr, Heimdall, Hel, Skadi, Freyr and Bragi, as Hermes Desktop themes. Install once, then switch with /skin <name>. Matching terminal skins ship in cli/skins. Disclosure — theme-only desktop plugin: it registers twelve themes through the plugin SDK, and their stylesheets restyle parts of Desktop's own UI (sidebar art, tabs, composer, wordmark) only while one of its themes is active. It also watches Desktop's active theme: when a terminal skin named asgard-<god> is active, it switches Desktop to that god's theme through the SDK's requestTheme. The terminal skins are plain YAML files the user copies into the Hermes skins folder by hand; the plugin does not install them or write any files. Fonts and art are bundled; no network requests, no agent tools or hooks.
Twenty CRM for Hermes Agent with managed self-hosting, external-instance connectivity, REST, GraphQL, and live schema introspection.

Two extra delegation modes for `delegate_task`, next to the built-in default. Model routes (`delegation.backend: model_map`): the agent picks a named model route per subagent from a list you define (e.g. fast, deep, local). Profile routes (`delegation.backend: profile_routes`): the agent runs a subagent as one of your Hermes profiles, with that profile's own model, credentials, skills and SOUL.md. Only route names and their one-line descriptions reach the model. Adds `hermes delegation config` (pick the mode and edit its routes; `--show` prints the setup) and the `/delegation` slash command (save a mode for the next session, or `--now` to apply it to the current chat). Needs Hermes 0.22.5 or newer, the first release with pluggable delegation providers; Hermes 0.22.0 to 0.22.4 refuses to install it, and on a core older than 0.22.0 it installs, logs one warning and does nothing. Disclosure — no Python dependencies and no network or model calls of its own; subagents run through core's `delegate_task` on the routes you configured. Writes only `delegation.backend` and `delegation.backends.*` (model_map / profile_routes) in the active profile's config.yaml, through core's config writer. A model route's optional `api_key` is stored in config.yaml in plain text (`provider:` keeps keys in .env / auth.json). Listing a profile under profile routes lets this profile's subagents use that profile's credentials, SOUL.md and terminal policy.

TypeSafe (Jev) skill routing: the request is routed before the model call and the one skill from the live roster that fits it is named in a single <skill_relevance> line on the user message — nothing is injected when nothing fits.

TypeSafe Jev (System One) decision tools — atomic yes/no checks, routing, rubric scoring and mixed typed questions with calibrated probabilities, for triage, routing and review gating in coding agents. Disclosure — every tool call sends the model-supplied question/state together with your TYPESAFE_API_KEY to api.typesafe.ai (TypeSafe AI, an independent vendor); the catalog has not verified the plugin author's affiliation with that vendor.

TypeSafe Jev as a judgment layer — a pre-tool gate (shadow by default, enforce escalates) on terminal, write_file and patch asking destructive / exfiltration / impact (a v2 signal set — reads_secrets × sends_outbound, blast_radius, self_advocating — is one setting away), plus a jev_ask tool for typed judgments. Thresholds in code, one JSONL line per decision with the fail-open reason, fail-open on every error path. Stdlib only, no Node; no redirects, proxy env ignored, payload capped; works with TYPESAFE_API_KEY, OPENROUTER_API_KEY, or AI_GATEWAY_API_KEY. Disclosure — each judged call sends the tool name and its redacted arguments (≤600 chars each, ≤12 args) to TypeSafe, OpenRouter, or your configured gateway, using your key; shadow mode only logs. With the default backend auto, OPENROUTER_API_KEY is used automatically whenever it is present and TYPESAFE_API_KEY is not, so tool names and redacted arguments go to openrouter.ai on your main-model OpenRouter key unless backend is set to typesafe or gateway.

TypeSafe Jev semantic governance for Hermes' native Curator: classifies relationships between complete skill packages, produces content-hash-bound, fail-closed consolidation plans, and locally guards background destructive skill_manage calls while Hermes retains control of backups and mutations. A profile-scoped 60-second lifecycle debounce coalesces skill changes into dry refreshes. Disclosure — no egress occurs by default; after allow_content_egress is explicitly enabled, redacted bounded skill content is sent to the configured TypeSafe, OpenRouter, or custom Jev endpoint and may spend provider credits. Automatic refreshes never apply mutations, and missing, stale, or incomplete evidence fails closed.

TypeSafe's Jev decision model as Hermes' smart-approval reviewer only: it cannot generate text and refuses every other task. Supports TypeSafe direct, OpenRouter, and configurable Jev-compatible HTTPS endpoints with optional endpoint-specific authentication; validates typed answers and endpoint/redirect boundaries, redacts command credentials, and records bounded structured audit logs. Disclosure — each command routed to smart approval (redacted best-effort) and the operator's smart-policy text leave the machine for the configured third-party endpoint; provider or validation failures fail closed to ESCALATE.
Typed adapter for the reproducible JACKAL v1.7.3 release: 41 catalog-derived verification tools (exact, numerical, Lean-checked bounded lanes, claim replay).

Unbrowse: websites as APIs. Read any page as clean markdown, run tasks on sites through learned first-party APIs (no browser), and drive a cloud browser with saved logins when nothing matches. Also a web_extract backend and a guard that routes public-web browser_* calls to Unbrowse. Disclosure — hosted service: page URLs, task text and tool arguments are sent to unbrowse.ai with your API key, pages are fetched and site logins are stored on Unbrowse's side, and verified calls bill the Unbrowse account; once UNBROWSE_API_KEY is set the plugin blocks the built-in browser_* tools and web_extract on public URLs by default (settings blockBrowser/blockWebExtract, or UNBROWSE_ALLOW_BUILTIN_BROWSER=1).

Universal human-controlled authentication for Camofox Browser, powered by the Camoufox engine. Supports login, registration, SSO, MFA, OTP, CAPTCHA, and device confirmation. Requires the Camofox backend; never changes an existing Hermes browser provider automatically.

Unofficial Claude Code-inspired theme for Hermes Desktop, with light and dark palettes, rounded composer and side-panel cards, softer sidebar and menus, and a context-window meter beside the model switcher. Not affiliated with, endorsed by, or sponsored by Anthropic or Claude Code. Disclosure — unofficial Claude Code lookalike theme; its stylesheet restyles native Desktop surfaces (user bubbles, composer, file panel, sidebar rows, dropdown menus) and hides the chat backdrop image; the context meter reads session.usage through the SDK; an opt-in accent setting uses setAccentOverride; no network calls of its own.

Unofficial Nord theme for Hermes Desktop with hand-tuned Polar Night (dark) and Snow Storm (light) palettes, Nord terminal colors, Nord code-block syntax colors, and Aurora status colors. Scoped to its own theme; other themes are untouched. Disclosure — its stylesheet recolors Desktop surfaces, code-block syntax colors, status colors, selection and inline code only while Nord is selected, and it switches the active theme to Nord once on first enable; no network calls, file reads or shell commands.

Unofficial OpenCode Zen free-model transport for Hermes. Discovers live zero-cost tool-capable models by intersecting OpenCode Zen and models.dev over HTTPS, persists only the last successful intersection for restart fallback, and bidirectionally translates compatible OpenCode and Hermes tool schemas, calls, choices, and replayed history while Hermes executes tools locally. No OpenCode CLI, Node.js, npm, or npx dependency. Disclosure — prompts, tool schemas, tool results, and other conversation content leave the machine for OpenCode and the selected model provider; model availability, retention, data use, and permission are governed by their current terms.

Unofficial port of the standard T3 Code dark theme for Hermes Desktop. Palette, T3 composer, sidebar thread cards with project and branch, model labels and confirm dialogs. Scoped to its own theme; other themes are untouched. Disclosure — unofficial T3 Code lookalike theme; its stylesheet restyles and hides some native Desktop controls, it reads local session metadata (branch, repo, provider) for sidebar cards, and it switches the active theme once on first enable.

Unofficial reMarkable cloud transfers, library management, backups, typed text, and bounded native notebook rendering. Disclosure — talks to reMarkable cloud with a device token under ~/.hermes/credentials/remarkable/; remarkable_upload sends model-chosen local PDF/EPUB files to your account; the cloud sidecar (Node 22+) and renderer venv are installed only by the human-run setup commands; USB/SSH off by default.

Uptime-Kuma monitoring for agents: the community MCP server for Uptime Kuma v2 (pinned @0.11.18 over npx stdio) with workflow skills for incident review, status digests, and confirmation-gated maintenance. Credentials stay in host-native MCP config (portable Agent Plugins v1 package, mcp.json + skills/; needs Node.js >= 22 on PATH and a Uptime Kuma v2 instance). Disclosure — first run has npx fetch @davidfuchs/mcp-uptime-kuma@0.11.18 (single-maintainer community package) from npm; that server exposes 31 read/WRITE tools against your Uptime Kuma instance, including permanent delete tools the bundled skills never call.

Usage and cost footer appended to every reply — tokens, cache hit rate, cost and context occupancy, plus a per-tool time breakdown showing which tool actually consumed the wall clock. Waiting time (a blocking user prompt) is reported separately and excluded from the active-time denominator. Pure computation, never calls a model; any failure leaves the reply untouched. Disclosure — the usage footer is appended to the stored assistant reply, so it is replayed to the model on later turns and adds tokens to every turn.

Use Hermes Agent from Inline work-chat DMs, chats, and reply threads. Disclosure — the setup wizard can, on explicit opt-in, download https://inline.chat/cli/install.sh and pipe it to sh without a checksum, then run the vendor inline CLI login; on connect the adapter publishes your Hermes slash-command list and the names and descriptions of installed skills to the Inline server (INLINE_SYNC_COMMANDS=false disables); error telemetry is off unless a Sentry DSN is set.

Use the signed-in Aside browser as Hermes's browser when the Aside CLI is installed. Disclosure — runs the local aside CLI to drive your signed-in Aside browser (page text, screenshots, Aside memory, model-written JavaScript via aside_repl) without a Hermes approval prompt; Aside's permission level is a user-only setting (default ask) that covers aside_exec only. Optional pre_tool_call hook blocks Hermes' built-in browser tools while Aside is ready when browser_policy is always. Reads Aside's settings.json for the model list; no telemetry.

Use your Cursor subscription models (Claude Opus/Sonnet 5.5, Composer 2.5, GPT-5.6, Grok) inside Hermes Agent via the Cursor CLI's ACP server (`agent acp`). Install with one command (`npx hermes-cursor-acp`) or `hermes plugins install cursor-acp`. The plugin rewrites `.cursor/cli.json` in an empty private workspace every run with a deny-all list (`Read`, `Write`, `Shell`, `WebFetch`, `Mcp`) to prevent Cursor's native CLI tools from accessing host files. It includes a custom extractor that recovers both flat `{"name", "arguments"}` and inline `<tool_call>` blocks that standard regex bridges drop, retries on concurrent `set_model` calls, and reports `usage=None` so Hermes proactive context compression functions correctly. Disclosure — sends the full conversation, Hermes tool schemas and tool results to Cursor through your locally installed, signed-in Cursor CLI (`agent acp`); Cursor's own tools are fenced by a deny-all `.cursor/cli.json` that the plugin rewrites in a private workspace under `$HERMES_HOME/cache/cursor-acp-workspace` on every start (a differing existing file is backed up to `cli.json.bak`), and Hermes executes every tool call under its own approvals.

Uses local Presidio and spaCy to redact supported PII in outgoing user text. Disclosure — filters Chat Completions user messages and Responses user input locally; system prompts, tool outputs and tool-call arguments are preserved. Fail-open: detector errors, including a missing model, send original text. Install spaCy en_core_web_sm 3.8.0 separately from its GitHub release wheel in the Hermes Python environment before enabling; Hermes installs only the named PyPI dependencies. No runtime model downloads or remote detection.
VK Messenger gateway with community Long Poll, media attachments, allowlists, and project-lane routing.
Vaultwarden / Bitwarden Password Manager (bw CLI) secret source

Vector (vectorapp.io) messaging platform plugin: Hermes becomes a first-class Nostr-based Vector bot (its own nsec/npub identity), relaying DMs through a local Rust sidecar that wraps vector-sdk. First run needs `hermes gateway setup`, which provisions the bot identity (create or import). Disclosure — `hermes gateway setup` downloads a prebuilt vector-bridge binary from github.com/BonesGit/hermes-vector-platform/releases (tag v<version>, sha256 checked against that release's SHA256SUMS; set vector.prebuilt.download: false to build from the bundled Rust source), merges `vector:` settings into ~/.hermes/config.yaml, writes VECTOR_* to ~/.hermes/.env, and publishes a public bot profile (kind-0, bot: true) to Nostr discovery relays.
Vendor-maintained Telnyx inference provider with an authenticated live model catalog, hosted open models, frontier routes, and catalog-derived pricing.
Venice AI web search + extract — privacy-first, zero data retention, $0.01/request.

Verify Jet Browser startup, native input, DOM agreement, and PNG capture inside a network-isolated WPE WebKit container. Disclosure — runs `docker run` (Docker access is root-equivalent on the host) on the digest-pinned image ghcr.io/masakaai/jet-browser@sha256:540a1fec…, pulled from GHCR on first use; the container has no network and only SETUID/SETGID capabilities, but runs with AppArmor and systempaths unconfined and a seccomp profile that allows user-namespace and mount syscalls for WebKit's bubblewrap sandbox; the tool takes no arguments and loads only a built-in local test page.

Vietnamese (Tieng Viet) language pack for Hermes Agent — full UI translation across every surface: core (approval prompts, gateway/slash replies, CLI, tips), TUI, and Desktop catalogs. Checked against the English catalogs with hermes plugins validate. Parser-safe: hard-parsed menu brackets and [Y/n] prompts stay verbatim; placeholders, URLs and CLI flags preserved; multi-line values use real newlines exactly like the English catalogs. Manifest-only plugin, no code execution, no network. Ban dich tieng Viet day du cho toan bo giao dien Hermes Agent. Disclosure — text-only catalogs; registering the pack never changes display.language, the user opts in via config.

View and edit the identity files (SOUL.md, MEMORY.md, USER.md, AGENT.md/HERMES.md) from chat, switch the active profile, and see per-line usage with colour-coded staleness timestamps. Adds six tools, /identity, /identity-switch and /identity-dashboard commands, and a utilization dashboard pane. Disclosure — reads and writes the identity files and a line-utilization record inside the selected profile directory under HERMES_HOME, and can change which profile is active; it performs no network I/O and holds no credentials. Disclosure — the model-callable identity_edit tool rewrites SOUL.md/MEMORY.md/USER.md/AGENT.md and identity_switch_profile writes HERMES_HOME/active_profile.
View and manage Bot Mode agents in a shared office in Hermes Desktop.

Vornik as Hermes's hardened broker and long-term memory: Hermes holds no credentials; privileged work runs in operator-approved workflows on your own Vornik daemon. Disclosure — talks only to the self-hosted Vornik daemon at VORNIK_URL with VORNIK_BROKER_TOKEN (and VORNIK_MEMORY_TOKEN for memory); broker tools let the agent start operator-approved workflows on that daemon (writes are approved by a person in Vornik); when selected as memory provider it sends each turn's user query for recall, mirrors MEMORY.md and USER.md writes to the daemon, and asks the daemon to stop recalling (not delete) a mirrored entry that Hermes removes or replaces (/vornik-memory lists and /vornik-forget forgets what Vornik keeps); artifact tools expose only named outputs allowed by the approved workflow from completed runs and read bounded text or return short-lived binary download links from the daemon; task diagnosis tools (offered only when the daemon advertises companion-progress) return a broker task's execution events and closed error classes as the daemon serves them to a broker key; hermes vornik approvals on writes security.approval.transport (and vornik_companion.approval_namespace) to Hermes config, after which Hermes's own dangerous-command prompts (the redacted command text) are sent through the local vornikctl agent host-approval to the daemon and answered on the paired phone, any failure or a Vornik outage denying the command unless transport_fallback: builtin is set, and the plugin never decides itself; hermes vornik connect runs the local vornikctl, which adds an MCP entry to Hermes config.
Wallaby Token — curated open-weight inference (Kimi K3); adds Wallaby to the hermes model provider list.

Watch over opencode sessions from anywhere: alerts for stopped turns, questions and permissions, plus a dependency-free CLI to reply. Disclosure — the skill has the agent install the ocshepherd CLI from GitHub at a pinned commit and, after asking you, add a cron entry or systemd unit that polls your opencode server; the CLI talks to that server with the password you provide, can reply to its questions and permission prompts, and optionally sends alerts to Telegram or runs a notify command you configure.
Watch your agents inhabit pixel-art realms in Hermes Desktop, with imported scenes and a minimal PW Agents display.
Watchline delivery adapter for Hermes Agent. Polls a Watchline pull channel and forwards matched events into the Hermes gateway as inbound messages.

WeCom / Enterprise WeChat gateway adapter for Hermes Agent. Registers two platforms: ``wecom`` (Smart Robot over WebSocket) and ``wecom_callback`` (self-built apps over an HTTP callback endpoint with AES message crypto). Relays messages between WeCom chats and the Hermes agent.
Weather data, radar/model imagery, and verified meteorological calculations. Built on metrust, rusbie, wrf-rust, rustdar, and ecape-rs.

Web search and page fetching through Keenable's hosted MCP server, with search and research skills: single-site and publish-date filters, result and snippet limits, and page fetches that return only what a prompt asks for. Works without an API key; an optional KEENABLE_API_KEY lifts the keyless rate limits. Adds direct MCP tools beside Hermes's built-in Keenable web backend and leaves web_search / web_extract provider selection unchanged. Disclosure: connects to Keenable's hosted MCP server at `api.keenable.ai` and sends it the search queries, URLs and fetch prompts the agent issues, labelled with the header `X-Keenable-Title: hermes-plugin`; sends `X-API-Key` only when the user adds the optional config.yaml entry with their key.

Web search with Google Search; Google News, Google Images, Google Shopping, Google Video Search and Google Places for research. Use YouTube Search or YouTube Extended Search; retrieve YouTube metadata, YouTube transcripts, YouTube captions and YouTube channel data; get YouTube autocomplete; inspect YouTube trainability as license-label metadata, not training permission. YouTube downloads deliver media to your own storage. One hosted MCP connection and 15 task Skills; bring your own API key and paid FlashData Credits. Disclosure — Connects to FlashData's hosted MCP service (data.flashdata.dev) with your own FLASHDATA_API_KEY; every search, YouTube read or download spends your paid FlashData Credits, and Hermes asks before running only the tools the server does not mark read-only, so most paid searches run without a prompt. The YouTube download tool sends the storage bucket and storage access credentials you supply to FlashData, and those values stay visible in the chat history.

WebSocket platform for your own mobile, desktop or web app: it talks to the agent directly — text, voice, images, video and documents in both directions, approval/clarify/slash cards answered from the app, streaming edits, typing and avatar state events, cron delivery to a chosen device. On request it also answers command-catalog and model-list frames (commands from the agent's own registry, models from its model inventory) so a client renders command and model pickers from the agent's data instead of bundling a snapshot; auto-push after ready is off by default (MOBILE_CATALOG_AFTER_READY=1). Ships TypeScript and Python SDKs, platform guides and an acceptance checklist. Disclosure — opens a listening WebSocket server (plain ws://, no built-in TLS; 127.0.0.1:8787 by default, the wildcard address only when set, behind a wss proxy) guarded by MOBILE_TOKEN plus optional per-device tokens; anyone holding an unbound token can chat with the agent, run slash commands and answer the approval and clarify cards of the device id they connect as; device_id=token entries bind a token to one device. deliver frames are accepted only from loopback peers or MOBILE_DELIVER_TOKENS. Inbound media is written under $HERMES_HOME/mobile-media; secrets are read through Hermes's profile-scoped route; approvals resolve through Hermes's own resolvers; no telemetry, no third-party network calls, no self-update.

Weixin (personal WeChat) gateway adapter for Hermes Agent over Tencent's iLink Bot API. Long-polls getupdates for inbound messages, echoes each peer's context_token on replies, and moves media through the AES-128-ECB encrypted CDN. `hermes gateway setup` performs the iLink QR login.

WhatsApp Business Cloud API adapter for Hermes Agent. Connects to WhatsApp via Meta's official Cloud API (Business account and a public webhook URL required, token-based auth): Graph API for outbound, an aiohttp webhook receiver with X-Hub-Signature-256 verification for inbound. Supports text, media (image/video/audio/document), voice notes, interactive buttons, and DM allowlists. Complements the Baileys bridge (whatsapp) plugin; both share WhatsAppBehaviorMixin.

WhatsApp gateway adapter for Hermes Agent. Connects to WhatsApp via a local Node.js bridge (WhatsApp Web client) over an HTTP API and relays messages between WhatsApp chats and the Hermes agent. Supports DM/group policies, mention gating, free-response chats, and per-user allowlists.

Windows and WSL triage skills for Hermes: processes that survive a quit (orphaned stdio MCP trees, lingering python/uv/node children), WSL-to-Windows interop where an argument reaches cmd.exe as shell syntax, config and encoding traps (UTF-8 BOM, legacy console code pages), and long-path or reserved-name errors. One skill plus a copy-paste command reference; the process, argv and job-object failure modes are pinned to reports #131561, #132069 and #61059 and re-verified against current main. Disclosure — instructions only: no tools, hooks, middleware, network calls or credentials, and the destructive diagnostics are marked and gated on asking the user first.

Windows desktop plugin that switches which Codex login and which Claude subscription account every local Hermes profile uses, with one idle-only, verified restart of the gateway (and, on Hermes before 0.22, of Hermes Desktop). Refuses while any profile is busy, restores the previous selection if a step fails, and writes a receipt that says whether the switch took effect. Disclosure — Windows only. A switch rewrites, through Hermes's own commands, the Codex credential order in every profile's auth.json and the CLAUDE_SUBSCRIPTION_DIRECTSDK_CONFIG_DIR line in every profile's .env, so every profile that has the plugin enabled spends the same selected Codex login and the same Claude login (one Hermes-owned claude-auth folder; no token is copied between profiles). It reads Codex tokens from each profile's auth.json. On Hermes 0.22 and later it stops and restarts the gateway once Hermes's own idle proof and the gateway's drain report idle, and Hermes Desktop stays open and reconnects; on earlier Hermes it also reads the Desktop backends' dashboard session token from their process environment and closes and reopens Hermes Desktop (work started in the seconds after the idle check is cut off). It sends the target Codex token to OpenAI's usage endpoint and Claude login tokens to Anthropic's OAuth profile endpoint (also when the setup screen opens); if the target Claude login has expired it first runs the claude CLI once so the CLI renews its own token, which rotates that login's refresh token. No telemetry and no automatic account rotation.

Windows taskbar badge on the Hermes window when a turn finishes. Calls navigator.setAppBadge on the message.complete event while the window is in the background, and clears it when the window regains focus or another session is opened. Disclosure — no network calls and no data leaves the machine; the badge is drawn by the app's own Electron process, which maps the Chromium Badging API onto the Windows taskbar overlay.

Write-ahead ledger for agent side effects, with an OWASP Agentic Top 10 posture scorer. Disclosure — records the arguments (up to 4000 chars: terminal commands, file contents, MCP args) and a 300-char result digest of every state-changing tool call in a local plaintext SQLite ledger under HERMES_HOME/plugin-data/agent-ledger/ that is never pruned; injects a warning listing this session's unconfirmed calls into the next turn's context; an optional policy engine (off by default; you add policy.json and set policy_mode) can refuse matching tool calls before they run; the optional posture_daily.py script, run from your own cron, sends a score summary to Telegram with the bot token you give it.

Wrong-question diagnosis and study-action loop for parents and students — deterministic local core (SQLite, no cloud), host-model recognition gated by parent confirmation. Portable Agent Plugins v1 package (mcp.json + skills/); good-student MCP server pinned to immutable commit 2469cbb over uvx, with the good-student workflow skill bundled. Needs Python 3.10+ via uv. No credentials required; all data stays on-device and nothing is uploaded.

Wyoming speech-to-text and text-to-speech for a Wyoming server you run (stt/tts provider `wyoming`), plus a wyoming_voice_status tool that lists the server's models and voices. Disclosure — Audio and text to speak go to the WYOMING_* host:port you set over cleartext, unauthenticated TCP (public addresses accepted). Once selected, the providers send speech in every session, including cron and webhooks. Non-WAV audio is converted with your local ffmpeg. wyoming_voice_status asks for approval on each call and refuses under cron, yolo, approvals off, -q and unattended platforms; answering "always" leaves a command_allowlist line in config.yaml. It calls internal Hermes approval, config and write-guard helpers, so a Hermes update can disable the status tool or speech file writes (both fail closed).

X Chat gateway platform: talk to Hermes in X's end-to-end encrypted DMs. Hermes runs as the X account you connect: chat with it in your own self-chat ("message yourself"), or give it a separate account and DM that. Messages are decrypted and encrypted locally with X's official Chat XDK, so X only routes ciphertext. Encrypted media, threaded replies, group mention gating and cron delivery.
YAGNI coding and code-review guidance for Hermes: reduce over-engineering, reuse existing behavior, and preserve requirements. One static prompt section; no tools or hooks.

Yandex Search API as a backend for the built-in web_search (provider name yandex), plus a yandex_generative_search tool for grounded answers with cited sources. Disclosure — sends web_search queries and yandex_generative_search questions to searchapi.api.cloud.yandex.net, or to the base URL in YANDEX_SEARCH_API_URL if you set one, with your YANDEX_API_KEY and YANDEX_FOLDER_ID read through Hermes; the Search API is a paid Yandex Cloud service billed to the folder that owns the key; no other endpoint, no telemetry, no file or shell access, no background process. Independent community plugin, not affiliated with Yandex.
Yolo-Auto: flat-rate OpenAI-compatible API with plan-filtered live model discovery.

You.com skills for live web search, URL content extraction, cited research, finance research, and integration discovery via the You.com MCP servers (api.you.com). Portable Agent Plugins v1 package (mcp.json + skills/, five skills bundled); auth via YDC_API_KEY, OAuth, or MPP/x402 — the free profile works keyless.

Your AI subscriptions and token usage in Hermes Desktop. A page with Overview, Usage and Plans tabs, plus a status-bar chip where you pick which subscriptions to keep. Quota comes from Hermes's own model.options and usage.bars RPCs; the page polls Hermes' cached windows (Hermes refreshes them in its own background threads) and only its Refresh button asks for an explicit refresh; token usage covers Hermes, Claude Code and the Grok CLI, clicking a day shows that day's per-source, per-model and hourly breakdown, and measured tokens per second are shown per model, per day and overall. Disclosure: read-only reads outside the plugin's data - Hermes state.db and models_dev_cache.json, ~/.claude/projects/**/*.jsonl and ~/.grok/logs/unified.jsonl plus ~/.grok/sessions/*/*/summary.json (token counts only). No credential, .env or auth.json reads, no network calls, no shell commands, no background processes, no telemetry.

Your company's memory in Hermes: search decisions, people, customers and projects across every source your team connected to Gurusup (Slack, HubSpot, Notion, uploaded documents and more), with the sources behind each answer. Portable Agent Plugins v1 package (mcp.json + skills/), remote streamable-http with OAuth 2.1, no local code and no API keys. Disclosure — hosted-only MCP connector with no local code: every tool call goes to Gurusup's server at mcp.brain.gurusup.com under the signed-in Gurusup account (OAuth via `hermes mcp add gurusup-brain --url https://mcp.brain.gurusup.com/mcp --auth oauth`; the bundled mcp.json alone yields 401), and answers are limited to what that account can see; write tools save knowledge to the company's Gurusup workspace (add_company_knowledge, skills_publish) and send issue reports or feedback to Gurusup (report_issue, send_feedback), and request_human_info can message a teammate on Slack or phone them when its dispatch flag is set.

Your house and family chore board as Hermes tools, through ChorePilot's own MCP server on this machine, the LAN or Tailscale. Runs appliances (lights, climate, dishwasher/washer/dryer, sprinklers, vacuum and more via Home Assistant, Home Connect, MQTT or a simulator) and keeps a rotating chore board that devices verify. ChorePilot's policy decides every call: water/heat actions wait for the person's own yes in Telegram or the ChorePilot dashboard, kids' requests go to a parent's approval queue, and unlocking, opening the garage and disarming are never available to an agent. Bundles the chorepilot:household skill. Disclosure — each tool call sends HTTP requests with the bearer token in CHOREPILOT_TOKEN to the user's own ChorePilot server at CHOREPILOT_URL, and the plugin also lists that server's tools once at every Hermes start (plain http only to loopback, private, Tailscale or .local/.lan/.ts.net addresses); chorepilot_call runs any device or chore tool the token's person may use (lights, climate, vacuum, locking and more) without a Hermes approval prompt, with ChorePilot's own policy deciding, so water/heat actions wait up to two minutes for that person's yes in Telegram or the ChorePilot dashboard, kids' requests go to a parent, and unlocking, opening the garage and disarming are never available; no other network calls, no files read outside the plugin, no background processes, no telemetry, stdlib only.

Your system prompt is message zero and the user's question is message N. On models that weight recency hard, that is not a fair fight, and the instruction you care about most quietly loses to whatever was just asked. This plugin restates it at the end of every user turn instead. Append-only, API cop

Zalo Bot Platform gateway adapter for Hermes Agent — relays messages between Zalo DMs/groups and the agent over the official Bot API (bot-api.zaloplatforms.com), long-polling or webhook mode. Adds slash commands and moderation. Zero extra dependencies (uses httpx, already a Hermes dependency). Production-tested on multiple Vietnamese deployments. Disclosure — connects to the third-party Zalo Bot API (bot-api.zaloplatforms.com) with your bot token; long-polling by default, or opt-in webhook mode with a listener on 127.0.0.1 by default that checks the X-Bot-Api-Secret-Token header; the setup wizard writes ZALO_* values to ~/.hermes/.env; group chat history is stored locally under <HERMES_HOME>/zalo-history.
ZeroSignal — private, pay-per-request inference through the local zs-proxy; no API key, your wallet is the credential.

`hermes import-agent`: import an OpenClaw (~/.openclaw, or legacy ~/.clawdbot / ~/.moltbot), Claude Code (~/.claude), Codex CLI (~/.codex) or Cursor (~/.cursor) setup into Hermes in one command; always previews first and asks before applying. Claude Code / Codex / Cursor: instructions, Cursor rules and memories become memory entries, Bash permission rules become command allow/deny lists, MCP servers land in config.yaml, skills are copied, and `--sync` re-imports sources that changed. OpenClaw (core's former `hermes claw migrate`; the plugin keeps that spelling, `hermes claw cleanup` and the openclaw-migration skill): persona, memories, skills, model and messaging settings, MCP servers and agent behaviour. Formerly built into Hermes core; `hermes setup` offers to install it when it finds one of these agents, and profiles with a registered sync source are migrated automatically. Disclosure — no Python dependencies, no network calls and no model calls. Claude Code / Codex / Cursor: reads those agents' local config trees (never their credential files; secret-looking MCP env vars and headers are stripped and listed) and writes only into the active profile (memories/MEMORY.md with a backup, config.yaml, skills/ and import-sync.json). OpenClaw: reads the OpenClaw dir (openclaw.json, its .env, workspace files such as SOUL.md / MEMORY.md / USER.md, skills); API keys and bot tokens come over only with --migrate-secrets (allowlisted names, shown in the preview). It writes into the active profile (config.yaml, .env, SOUL.md, memories/, skills/openclaw-imports/, a migration/openclaw/<time>/ report with item backups, and a backups/pre-migration-*.zip restore point), plus a workspace dir only when --workspace-target names one. It runs local pgrep / systemctl / tasklist checks to warn when OpenClaw or a Hermes gateway is still running, and `hermes claw cleanup` renames the OpenClaw dir to *.pre-migration after a confirmation.

brethof-brain long-term memory provider — the memory's briefing in the system prompt at session start, ambient recall on every turn, every turn archived; one memory shared with the user's other agents (Claude Code, Codex, OpenCode and more). Sends each turn to the user's own brethof-brain memory (on their machine at 127.0.0.1:8610, or hosted at memory.brethof.cloud). Needs a brethof-brain account. Disclosure — sends every user prompt and each turn's user and assistant text, with your API key, to the brethof-brain server you configure (default a local box at 127.0.0.1:8610; hosted at memory.brethof.cloud), and puts the server's returned briefing and recall text into the system prompt and each turn; reads BRETHOF_BRAIN_* from $HERMES_HOME/.env and ~/.brethof-brain/config.json.

fmsg platform adapter for Hermes Agent. Real-time inbound over the fmsg-webapi WebSocket (/fmsg/ws), outbound via its JSON REST routes. Authenticates with an fmsg API key (fmsgk_...) exchanged for a short-lived JWT — run the agent as a derived sub-account such as @alice_hermes@example.com. Only http

hermes inbox: one read-only view of everything in flight for the active profile: failed or paused cron jobs, stalled or dropped delegations, orphaned background processes, blocked kanban tasks, running work, undelivered delegation results, upcoming cron runs and open chat sessions, with --json for scripts. A Hermes Labs plugin: built by Nous Research, not supported. Disclosure — reads processes.json, cron/jobs.json, runtime/active_sessions.json and state.db (SQLite read-only) in the profile's home, plus the shared kanban board's kanban.db (read-only); it never writes, repairs or prunes them, adds no model tools or hooks, and sends nothing anywhere.

hermes record: demonstrate a browser workflow once (clicks, field values, navigations) and its bundled skill lets /learn turn the recording into a skill that replays it with the browser tools. A Hermes Labs plugin: built by Nous Research, not supported. Disclosure — attaches over CDP to a Chromium you point it at (--cdp, BROWSER_CDP_URL, browser.cdp_url or 127.0.0.1:9222) and records what you do in that tab until Ctrl-C; password, one-time-code and card fields are masked inside the page as {SECRET:name} and never written. Recordings stay local in <HERMES_HOME>/recordings; nothing is sent anywhere until you run /learn on one, which hands it to your active model.

looot gives Hermes one sign-in and one prepaid balance for 2,500+ data API endpoints from 90+ providers: work emails and phones, company and people search, Google results, web pages as markdown, news, local businesses. Portable Agent Plugins v1 package with the hosted MCP server (remote streamable-http, OAuth 2.1 with dynamic client registration) and 21 skills. Disclosure — the run tool spends your prepaid looot balance (Hermes asks before each paid call and refuses them in unattended runs); the names, domains and emails you look up are sent to looot.ai and its upstream data providers; a `looot` server you define in config.yaml replaces the package's and drops that prompt unless you add `trust: untrusted`.

lumberroom memory provider. One durable store shared with every agent you use, recalled on every turn and written through the engine's own memory_write. Self-hosted open-source engine or lumberroom.cloud; OAuth or a static token. Maintained by the lumberroom team. Disclosure — when active, every non-trivial user message (first 1,000 characters) and the absolute git-root path of the working directory are sent on each turn to the configured lumberroom engine, which defaults to https://mcp.lumberroom.cloud (operated by Cybersapien Technologies, India) unless base_url names a self-hosted engine; the model is instructed to store decisions, preferences and facts there through memory_write, the engine's live tool descriptions and server instructions are injected into the system prompt each session, and setup switches off Hermes' built-in MEMORY.md/USER.md store.

ntfy push-notification gateway adapter for Hermes Agent. Subscribes to a topic on ntfy.sh or any self-hosted ntfy server via HTTP streaming, and publishes replies via HTTP POST. Lightweight — no external SDK, only httpx (already a Hermes dependency).
ntfy has no native user-identity primitive; the adapter treats each topic as a single trusted channel and never derives user identity from publisher-controlled fields. Use a private topic + read token for any real trust boundary.

pass (password-store) secret source: resolves secrets from a local, GPG-encrypted, git-tracked password store into environment variables at startup, as a first-class SecretSource beside the built-in Bitwarden and 1Password sources. Stdlib-only (subprocess + pathlib), no Python deps, no network — ever. Config: secrets.pass.{enabled,store_path,subdirs,override_existing,timeout_seconds}. Disclosure — when enabled, shells out to the local pass binary (10 s per entry) for every .gpg entry under the configured store subdirs and injects each as an env var that by default overrides .env and shell values; when enabled, also adds a ~900-char system-prompt note about secret resolution; no network.

past.dev memory provider: recall before each turn from source-traced memory of past conversations, with sessions sent to past.dev when they end. Maintained by past.dev. Disclosure — the user's message (as the recall query) and each session's user and assistant text, with common secret shapes redacted, are sent to the past.dev API (api.past.dev by default, or the address you configure) under your past project key, with a past-hermes/<version> User-Agent; the key and identity are read from PAST_API_KEY or ~/.past/config.json, which past.dev's other connectors share; off by default on messaging-gateway sessions.

pixel art sprite sheet cutter. png to tileset splitter. cut pixel art into game tiles. sprite sheet from pixel png. 2d walk cycle sprite sheet. tileset cutter for pixel art. split png into sprite sheet. shore tiles tileset tool. pixel art walk cycle sheet. png sprite and shore tiles. Cuts a pixel-art png into frames. Tools: inspect_grid, slice_grid, place_kit for a 2D game. Disclosure — The png stays on this computer. Nothing is sent. No API key. No daily cap. A gateway room can call the tools. Stop them with hermes tools. One approval on one line via pre_tool_call. Choosing always covers only the same call. An oversized line writes one list file. A failed check writes nothing. Hermes yolo and approvals off skip that prompt. cron, -q, and unattended sessions default to deny. Empty, unknown, or a restrictive license is not written. Unknown text is copied and next warns. CC-BY-SA is copied and next names share-alike. No license chunk still writes and next says no rights are attached. Import once or play fails: godot --headless --editor --quit --path <project>. No solid-color box and no sound effect. Does not launch Godot or Unity. Play may write app-userdata. Uninstall leaves no cron job. Linux is untested. Unity editor 6000.6.6f1 on macOS kept the walk-sheet fileIDs after a reopen.

pre_llm_call hook plugin, enabled with `hermes plugins enable`: injects ambient context from a GBrain instance before each turn (volunteer_context, then a hybrid-query fallback). Not a `memory.provider`. Silent no-op when GBrain is unreachable or no token is set. Disclosure — before each non-trivial turn the last six user and assistant messages (truncated) and the current message are sent with a GBRAIN_TOKEN bearer token to GBRAIN_MCP_URL (default http://127.0.0.1:3131/mcp), and returned brain-page text is injected into the turn.

ree_validate_receipt, ree_verify_receipt, ree_infer. Validate does not re-execute and does not stand behind text_output, finish_reason, token_count, model.name, or ree_version. Verify re-executes on CPU. Infer runs one of three small models and writes one receipt. Disclosure — Starts containers from the local image gensynai/ree:v0.8.0 (pinned by digest) and never pulls it; running docker pull yourself is consent to the REE-Binary-License. ree_verify_receipt and ree_infer mount ~/.cache/gensyn and ~/.cache/huggingface read-write (a Hugging Face token file stored there is visible to the container; no token is passed in the environment), may download Hugging Face weights for any model a receipt names, and their container network is not limited to Hugging Face; they ask for Hermes approval on every call and refuse under cron, yolo, approvals off, single-query, unattended runs, host isolation, or when the approval API is missing. ree_validate_receipt runs with network none, does not ask, and returns no receipt text. Any person admitted to one of your gateways can call these tools and approve containers on your Docker daemon; disable per surface with hermes tools. Choosing "always" adds one config.yaml allowlist line per call and never covers the next call. New receipts and temporary work files are written under ~/.cache/hermes-ree; nothing is stored under HERMES_HOME. The container is not a hostile-code sandbox. No cron is created.

rply gateway platform: talk to Hermes from the rply inbox on your phone and laptop, with web push. Messages and files both ways, seen/working/done with a live activity note, clarify questions and command approvals as tappable questions, cron delivery, a pinned table of scheduled jobs, a dashboard app with run/pause/resume, and an rply_request_secret tool that saves API keys to the profile's .env without the value passing through the chat. Each profile joins the channel as its own agent. Disclosure — keeps a long-polling connection to the configured rply server only (RPLY_SERVER, default https://app.rply.sh; self-hostable, AGPL server); messages the channel's members send reach Hermes as user instructions and members answer its approval and clarify prompts; the dashboard sends the server Hermes' cron job list, the titles and previews of the 10 most recent sessions from every platform, token and cost totals and the default model, and runs, pauses or resumes jobs when its buttons are pressed; stores the agent token in the profile's .env, an X25519 keypair in <profile>/rply/secret-key.json (0600) and secrets the human provides in the profile's .env under a variable name the agent picks (core's env denylist applies; the .env path is sent to the server with the request); the secret tool waits up to 15 minutes for the human and refuses under cron; adds a `hermes rply` setup command; credentials read through Hermes' profile-scoped route; no shell commands, no telemetry, no self-update.
